clean_body: I know what it's like to live paycheck to paycheck | Peter, I never dreamed I would be in this position. Just over a month ago, I was just a mom, a grandmother, and a wife. I was not in the public eye. I was helping my youngest daughter get ready for her final year of high school. I’ve spent my life serving South Carolina from behind the scenes. I’ve run a state agency with 130 employees and a $90 million budget. We turned it from a struggling organization into a national model helping people find work and live independently. We made sure all spending was reasonable, allowable, and necessary. I fought against duplication of services, knowing it wasted taxpayers' dollars. I did not think I would become the first female United States Senator from South Carolina, but when President Trump asked me to serve, I knew I had to answer the call. Peter, we have just days left before the runoff on August 25th. I am up against a career politician - and I have only been running for weeks. Because after this Runoff Election, we have to look to November. My Democrat opponent has been raising millions since the passing of my brother, Lindsey. Welcome to the official _Team Kristi!_ newsletter. _Walk the Walk_ isn't just a slogan on this campaign, it's our daily drive! Let's dive into this past week and see what all happened with our movement to bring real representation for Tennessee's 1st District to Washington!
* * *
### Kristi and State Candidates Inspire the Crowd in Jonesborough
This past weekend, Kristi joined Tennessee State House candidates **Brad Batt** and **Sarah Jayne Della Vecchia** for a Democratic Town Hall in Tennessee's Oldest Town.
As the campaign shifts gears and heads into the general election race, it's important to **take stock of our values and remember why we got into this fight in the first place**.
Check out Kristi's opening statement from the event here:
[](https://substack.com/redirect/25d480da-bea0-4011-93b9-148beba14d9e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

body:
Essential Tuesday to choose the top contender who can win in November. That's Shelley Hughes!

| | | | |
---
| | **STRAIGHT TALK:**
**A Vote for Anyone but Hughes Tuesday **
**Risks Being a Vote for a **
**Democrat Governor and Taxes in November**
---
**Greetings, Alaskans: **
**We are hopeful and excited! We've worked hard, and you all have been fantastic in stepping up to support our ticket. The momentum has grown weekly, and now we're down to the wire! As I have always been transparent and forthright with you, I won't stop now. This primary election is unusually consequential. If a Democrat governor wins in November, our state will turn blue until 2042 due to redistricting. That's not a typo: 2042. There will be an income tax, a suppression of resource development, an exodus out of our state, increased wokeness in our schools. We CANNOT risk that happening. **
**Now here's the straight talk. Not all candidates who've been out campaigning can beat the Democrat in November. It is due to their baggage, skeletons, and/or high negatives. Of those Republicans in range of making the top four to win the primary, I am the Republican who** _**can**_**beat the Democrat. The Hughes/Gettys ticket does not have baggage, skeletons, or high negatives. **
**In a three-way senate race with a Democrat and a Libertarian, I won by 78%. That's not a typo either: 78%. That district included the blue pocket in Mat-Su, Palmer (its city council is controlled by Democrats) and yet I won by a very wide margin. The bottom line: I can beat the Democrat in November, and I need your vote in order to do it!**
**Before Tuesday, if you're not aware already, I'd like to make sure you realize the Hughes/Gettys ticket is more than just a clean one! So I've added a section (down among the photos and videos below) to overview my action plan to fix the decades old problems to address the affordability crises and stop the brawn and brain drain of our young people. I've also included my pragmatic vision for the coming decades.**
**In closing, many are asking as they make their final decision, "What is different about your candidacy?" Scroll down by the videos and photos to see my answer to that great question! **
**Now let's go do this: let's choose Hughes Tuesday!**** ****Ready to serve you,**
---
---
**Republican Candidate for Governor****of the Great State of Alaska**
---
**p.s. It's here; the Primary Election is tomorrow, Tuesday August 18, 7 AM to 8 PM, and every Alaskan for the Hughes/Gettys ticket needs to rally behind us at the ballot box! Can we count on your vote? **
**Sign waving opportunities today and Tuesday across the state! Stop by and join us! Reach out to us at **[**info@alaskansforhughes.com**](mailto:info@alaskansforhughes.com)** for more information. **

** "What is different about your ****Republican candidacy/ticket?" **
**What a great question! You may be wondering the same. Here goes. **

* **Only candidate who's lived in nearly every region of the state so I bring a statewide perspective like no other. **
* **Only candidate with the highest rate of Alaskan donors (97%); other candidates had rates as low as 33% Alaskan donors.**
* **Only candidate with a recent proven track record that verifies that what I say when I campaign is what I do when I get elected; I keep my word. **
* **Only candidate who's successfully navigated a tricky legislature from both a majority and minority standpoint, gotten major items across the finish line, and has already established good relationships with House and Senate members.**
* **Only candidate who stood strong and fought for the PFD year after year and was punished for it (lost chairmanships, committee assignments, staff, district resources, office space).**
* **Only candidate who hasn't just talked about protecting girls sports but also worked to make it happen.**
* **Only candidate who received an A+ for support of the Second Amendment and who has declared publicly on the record that Second Amendment rights are the most important, because without them, we could lose all our other rights.**
* **Only candidate who is conservative who has current knowledge on the wide spectrum of issues from twelve recent years of working in the House and Senate.**
* **Only candidate who has a highly competent retired General as a running mate who will be tasked to lead some of the crucial work. **
* **Only candidate who has laid out a detailed action plan with feasible steps to solve existing problems as well as a pragmatic vision to advance Alaska to her rightful destiny as a hub for the top of the world.**
* **Only candidate who is a top contender with a clean ticket (no baggage, no skeletons, no high negatives).**
* **Only candidate who's won a three-way state senate race with an extremely high margin (78% of the vote). The three candidates in the race: a Democrat, and a Libertarian, and me (the Republican). This occurred in a district where the local city council is controlled by Democrats. so the district is not bright red. I have never lost to a Democrat.**

We are fully focused on solving decades-old problems to address our present affordability crisis and brawn and brain drain of our young people. We will put accessible Alaska lands into Alaskans' hands through a state homestead act and work to restore some of the federal land grab that occurred at statehood. # **3 Ways A.I. 's Boom Could Bust Your Retirement**

---|---|---
Experts in the tech and finance sectors both agree, AI will change the world. But here's the rarely mentioned truth.
If you are in or near retirement, the unintended consequences of the AI boom could end up costing you dearly. **[There are three key factors that present major risks if your savings are tied to retirement funds such as a 401(k), IRA, or pension.](https://substack.com/redirect/b375ebea-2694-4baa-9db5-03ae1b74a112?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
It starts in your 401(k). AI-linked companies now carry an estimated 36% of holdings in major indexes, leaving many 401(k)s overcommitted to this one sector. If those companies fall short of earnings projections at any point, retirement balances could fall fast.
Then there's job risk. AI-driven layoffs accounted for over 54,000 job cuts in 2025 alone. Fewer high-paying jobs can mean weaker consumer spending, softer earnings, and more pressure on the stocks and dividends inside retirement accounts.
Third, may leave you paying higher utility costs as communities upgrade infrastructure to fuel the beast. It's estimated, data centers nationwide use 400 million gallons of water per day to cool down the massive machinery that powers AI.
AI may be the future, but your life's savings should not be forced to carry every risk it creates.

# **Trump confirms Iran backchannel talks as ceasefire deadline hits**
President Donald Trump **[told Fox News](https://substack.com/redirect/cc4d3e84-4f62-40f3-91e6-321bded6d3a1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** his 60-day ceasefire deadline with Iran expires Monday, but he's in "no hurry" and confirmed direct backchannel talks with the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, bypassing mediators and Iranian political officials, reiterating that Iran must not obtain a nuclear weapon in any form.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/cc4d3e84-4f62-40f3-91e6-321bded6d3a1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

* **He rejected suggestions that midterm politics are shaping his Iran strategy** and warned Oman against interfering in negotiations, while saying he'll likely stay out of Israel's upcoming elections but might endorse a candidate.
* **Trump also said Israel shouldn 't be striking Gaza as Hamas disarmament talks continue**, claimed the U.S. has its own relationship with Hamas, and downplayed strain on American weapons stockpiles from the conflict, calling usage so far "peanuts."

Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez said Saturday on Instagram she **[has no regrets](https://substack.com/redirect/daf0d632-28d3-4ea2-a9d1-0a26366948ec?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** about publicly documenting her egg-freezing journey, which she began sharing Aug. 8, framing the backlash she's faced as part of a broader sexist double standard she's experienced since entering politics.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/daf0d632-28d3-4ea2-a9d1-0a26366948ec?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

Critics have also pointed out complications and concerns associated with the egg freezing including low **[success rates.](https://substack.com/redirect/eedcdd3e-a851-445e-878f-14085b7e2a2b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
* **The disclosures also fueled speculation that she split from fianc e Riley Roberts,** whom she got engaged to in 2022 but hasn't been seen wearing a ring from in months; she has not publicly confirmed a breakup, though sources have told The NY Post it occurred some time ago.
* **The timing of the egg freezing disclosure also fuels rumors of a 2028 presidential run** for the socialist congresswoman, though she has not announced intentions to run at this time.

# Wes Moore Won't Debate - Yet. Help Us Demand He Debate Me. _We Have 48 Hours to Post A Strong, First Financial Report Total_.
Friend, Wes Moore and I appeared at the Maryland Association of Counties Gubernatorial Candidate Forum this past weekend, but he refused to debate me face to face.

Instead, he read from his pre-written pad-folio to every question. That's not a debate, and I called him out to both debate me and to expose his scandalous leadership in Maryland. Maryland Matters reported on the event [here](https://us.list-manage.com/fNBjXqLE_Sx?e=5bb5efcda7&c2id=56a77d5a7be3731f6f21d9e4cc6a323b). You may also [watch it here](https://us.list-manage.com/19mVEVgIwZr?e=5bb5efcda7&c2id=56a77d5a7be3731f6f21d9e4cc6a323b).

A great article by mdbaynews.com analyzing the entire presentation is available [here](https://us.list-manage.com/mOLMwwRE9FV?e=5bb5efcda7&c2id=56a77d5a7be3731f6f21d9e4cc6a323b).

We have only 48 hours to post our first financial report. Please join and [support us now with any amount](https://us.list-manage.com/HtV5iqxDXTG?e=5bb5efcda7&c2id=56a77d5a7be3731f6f21d9e4cc6a323b) \- show your support and help us show the strength we have to win against Wes Moore's outrageous, conflicted policies this Nov. 3.

Thank you!

For Maryland,

Dan Cox
Republican Nominee for Governor

# Iran
* **Sixty-day negotiating period for U.S.-Iran Islamabad agreement ends without final deal:** The 60-day period set out for negotiations following the U.S.-Iran Islamabad memorandum of understanding ended Monday without a final agreement or a joint announcement of an extension.
* Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei [said](https://substack.com/redirect/e620250e-e45d-4b13-abbc-a1ae1933bc54?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Monday there was no 60-day deadline in the Islamabad memorandum, adding that Tehran does not formulate its policies under pressure or ultimatums, the Islamic Republic's News Agency reported.
* He said the memorandum provided for 60 days of talks on sanctions relief and the nuclear issue, with the possibility of an extension if no agreement was reached.
* However, according to Baghaei, those talks never began because the U.S. breached the memorandum weeks after it was signed. "We did not start any negotiations at all, and the U.S. violated the understanding from the very beginning; as a result, the issue of a 60-day deadline became entirely moot," Baghaei said.
* A senior Iranian official [told](https://substack.com/redirect/951fdfdf-b008-4cb9-8a04-8e5ccdd4f4db?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Reuters that Tehran has reportedly given Washington "a few weeks" to fully implement the memorandum and "will not wait indefinitely" for the U.S. naval blockade to end, warning that Iran would be prepared to escalate tensions in the Strait of Hormuz and the wider region if diplomacy fails.
* **Trump tells Iran to "put up the white flag of surrender," threatens to bomb Oman:** U.S. President Donald Trump called on Iran to "put up the white flag of surrender" and threatened to bomb Oman, which is currently in talks with Tehran regarding the administration of the Strait, if it obstructs U.S. efforts to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. "If Oman gets in the way, we'll bomb the shit out of them," Trump told Fox News Monday.
* Asked about U.S. weapons stockpiles in the Middle East, he claimed, "What we have used so far is peanuts."
* Trump said he was under no pressure to end the conflict. "I have no time schedule...I'm not in a hurry," adding, "The midterms have nothing to do with my thinking."
* **Iran reaffirms that Oman deal is separate from full Hormuz reopening:** Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on Monday that an "understanding" has been reached in negotiations with Oman on a transit route through the Strait of Hormuz.
* Baghaei said the talks have proceeded slowly, "but we had planned, and still plan, to finalize the understanding in the form of a package: the map plus a joint statement."
* The talks with Oman, Araghchi said, focus narrowly on mapping new navigation lanes for ships, since the previous routes are no longer operational. Whether the Strait actually reopens, he said, "will depend on the fulfillment of other conditions to which the United States must adhere."
* **Iran says Qatar holding Iranian pilots as POWs:** Iran formally [accused](https://substack.com/redirect/4e8b4cd6-6470-49fe-b95c-f5e7c51e99bd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Qatar of holding three Iranian military pilots as prisoners of war for about six months and asked the Red Cross to intervene on Saturday.
* In a letter to ICRC President Mirjana Spoljaric Egger, Brig. Gen. Mohammad Bagherzadeh, who heads Iran's committee for missing personnel, said the pilots were shot down over Qatar during a March 2 mission against an "enemy military base."
* Bagherzadeh said Qatar has denied the prisoners contact with their families and urged the ICRC to visit them and help secure their release.

* A White House official said the incident "had nothing to do with the Chief of Staff's devices being hacked," though officials within the UK government feared Wiles' phone had been compromised again following a similar hacking investigation last year, in which someone claiming to be Wiles contacted senators, governors and business executives.

Photo by Houssam Shbaro/Anadolu via Getty Images. Monday, August 17, 2026 - Sixty-day negotiating period for U.S.-Iran Islamabad agreement ends without final deal. U.S. President Donald Trump tells Iran to "put up the white flag of surrender," threatens to bomb Oman. Iran reaffirms that Oman deal is separate from full Hormuz reopening. Iran says Qatar is holding Iranian pilots as POWs. Drones target Kurdistan Prime Minister's office, Intelligence Chief's residence. Ansarallah says it struck Mokha and Marib. Yemen's Saudi-backed government says it carried out 181 military operations in 24 hours. Israel continues its assault on Gaza. Israeli attacks in the occupied West Bank. Jared Kushner meets with Hamas leadership in Cairo. Regional powers condemn Israel for rejecting the Gaza roadmap. Over 70 Palestinian families face eviction in Lydd. Palestinian Red Crescent evacuates 74 people from Gaza. Palestinian paramedic released by Israel after more than two months. At least 10 Palestinian women prisoners contract scabies in Israel's Damon Prison. Israeli Supreme Court considers case of detained Palestinian journalist. Israeli strikes on Lebanon kill 11 amid supposed ceasefire. Lebanese leaders condemn Saturday attacks; Hezbollah vows response. Lebanese President Joseph Aoun says Israel is pushing to end UNIFIL presence as Israeli military activity surges in southern Lebanon. Democratic National Committee votes to back abolishing ICE. Trump orders reduction of joint military exercises with South Korea. Attorney General Todd Blanche declines to pledge Department of Justice independence from Trump on prosecutions. Supreme Court again rejects Trump's bid to overturn E. Jean Carroll verdict. UAE trained mercenaries in Sudan. Fighting in Sudan's Blue Nile State displaces thousands as RSF advances. Russia jails opposition party chairman for 11 years over anti-war comments. Taiwan plans record defense spending amid growing Chinese pressure. Somali troops claim to retake Baidoa from opposition forces. India claims to foil Pakistan-backed militant plot. Syrian detainee dies in government custody amid torture allegations. British prime minister exchanged messages with an impersonator posing as Trump aide. This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday - Friday Iran Sixty-day negotiating period for U.S.-Iran Islamabad agreement ends without final deal: The 60-day period set out for negotiations following the U.S.-Iran Islamabad memorandum of understanding ended Monday without a final agreement or a joint announcement of an extension. Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei Monday there was no 60-day deadline in the Islamabad memorandum, adding that Tehran does not formulate its policies under pressure or ultimatums, the Islamic Republic's News Agency reported. He said the memorandum provided for 60 days of talks on sanctions relief and the nuclear issue, with the possibility of an extension if no agreement was reached. However, according to Baghaei, those talks never began because the U.S. breached the memorandum weeks after it was signed. "We did not start any negotiations at all, and the U.S. violated the understanding from the very beginning; as a result, the issue of a 60-day deadline became entirely moot," Baghaei said. A senior Iranian official Reuters that Tehran has reportedly given Washington "a few weeks" to fully implement the memorandum and "will not wait indefinitely" for the U.S. naval blockade to end, warning that Iran would be prepared to escalate tensions in the Strait of Hormuz and the wider region if diplomacy fails. Trump tells Iran to "put up the white flag of surrender," threatens to bomb Oman: U.S. President Donald Trump called on Iran to "put up the white flag of surrender" and threatened to bomb Oman, which is currently in talks with Tehran regarding the administration of the Strait, if it obstructs U.S. efforts to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. "If Oman gets in the way, we'll bomb the shit out of them," Trump told Fox News Monday. Asked about U.S. weapons stockpiles in the Middle East, he claimed, "What we have used so far is peanuts." Trump said he was under no pressure to end the conflict. "I have no time schedule...I'm not in a hurry," adding, "The midterms have nothing to do with my thinking." Iran reaffirms that Oman deal is separate from full Hormuz reopening: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on Monday that an "understanding" has been reached in negotiations with Oman on a transit route through the Strait of Hormuz. Baghaei said the talks have proceeded slowly, "but we had planned, and still plan, to finalize the understanding in the form of a package: the map plus a joint statement." The talks with Oman, Araghchi said, focus narrowly on mapping new navigation lanes for ships, since the previous routes are no longer operational. Whether the Strait actually reopens, he said, "will depend on the fulfillment of other conditions to which the United States must adhere." Iran says Qatar holding Iranian pilots as POWs: Iran formally Qatar of holding three Iranian military pilots as prisoners of war for about six months and asked the Red Cross to intervene on Saturday. In a letter to ICRC President Mirjana Spoljaric Egger, Brig. Gen. Mohammad Bagherzadeh, who heads Iran's committee for missing personnel, said the pilots were shot down over Qatar during a March 2 mission against an "enemy military base." Bagherzadeh said Qatar has denied the prisoners contact with their families and urged the ICRC to visit them and help secure their release. Qatar these accusations, with a Foreign Ministry spokesperson saying that the pilots entered Qatari airspace and ignored radio warnings before being shot down. Qatar claims rescue teams recovered the remains of one pilot, repatriated in July, and Tehran never answered an April invitation to review the Qatari search operation for the other two. Drones target Kurdistan Prime Minister 's office, Intelligence Chief's residence: Two explosive-laden drones the office of Kurdistan Region Prime Minister Masrour Barzani and the residence of the head of the region's intelligence agency on Monday, Asharq Al-Awsat reported. Barzani said the Kurdistan Region's Counter-Terrorism Directorate determined that the attacks were carried out using "Iranian drones," calling them "a dangerous escalation and a direct threat to the security and stability of the region." Yemen Ansarallah says it struck Mokha and Marib: Yemen's Ansarallah on Sunday that it had struck Saudi-backed military forces in the Red Sea port of Mokha and in Marib, the country's oil-rich province, with ballistic missiles and drones, according to the Ansarallah-affiliated Saba news agency. Operations at Mokha were suspended on Sunday, with the port's director saying that strikes had killed seven people and caused an estimated $16 million in damage. Ansarallah's spokesperson also claimed a missile attack on a "Saudi military vessel and four escort ships" off Mokha in the Red Sea on Monday. Yemen 's Saudi-backed government says it carried out 181 military operations in 24 hours: The armed forces of Yemen's Saudi-backed government they used drones, artillery, and rocket launchers in 181 operations against Ansarallah from Saturday to Sunday, according to military spokesman Col. Majed al-Nuzaili. Al-Nuzaili claimed the strikes killed and wounded dozens of Ansarallah fighters and destroyed equipment and weapons depots along front lines stretching from the Red Sea coast to the Saada and Marib areas. Palestine Killed and wounded in Gaza: Over the past 48 hours, two Palestinians were killed and 18 were injured in Israeli attacks across Gaza, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health. Three bodies were also recovered from beneath the rubble. The total recorded death toll since October 7, 2023 has risen to 73,399 killed, with 174,310 injured. Since October 11, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,265 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 4,198, while 813 bodies have been recovered from under the rubble. Israel continues its assault on Gaza: Israeli forces a Palestinian man in Deir Al-Balah, striking him as he walked through Nuseirat refugee camp on Saturday evening, and wounded four others in strikes that day. Israeli artillery also densely populated areas of Khan Younis on Saturday, causing additional injuries and displacement. Forces opened fire toward Bureij and Jabalia refugee camps, bombarded Gaza City's Al-Zaytoun neighborhood, and demolished homes and residential buildings in Al-Tuffah neighborhood and Rafah. An Israeli airstrike on a Khan Younis tent encampment wounded at least 5 Palestinians on Sunday, while a separate strike on an apartment in Nuseirat wounded several others. Israeli attacks in the occupied West Bank: Hebron: Mohammed Al-Mutawwar, 27, an intensive care nurse at Dura Governmental Hospital, was in the back during a Friday evening attack on the town of Sa'ir by Israeli settlers, according to the Palestinian Nursing and Midwifery Association. The bullet severed his spinal cord, causing permanent paralysis, the association said. A young woman was also shot in the back and head during the attack, the Palestinian Red Crescent said. Israeli settlers under military protection attacked the Al-Ras area of Hebron city early Sunday, shooting two Palestinians and beating eight others, the Palestinian Red Crescent said. A 60-year-old man was shot in the back and hand; a 46-year-old man was shot and then detained by Israeli forces. A 66-year-old woman was among those beaten. In the village of Massafer Yatta, Israeli settlers into a Palestinian home, besieged the family, vandalized the yard, and then held a celebration on the family's balcony, Israeli lawmaker Ofer Casif said on Sunday. Jenin: Israeli forces on Monday two Palestinian farmers in Faqqu'a after armed settlers detained them while they were picking prickly pears on their land near a newly established outpost. Qalqilya: Residents of Azzun the continued closure of the town's main northern entrance, sealed by Israeli forces since October 7, 2023, restricting movement and hurting local businesses. Nablus: Israeli settlers, backed by the army, on Monday for a ninth consecutive day to besiege three families' homes in Qusra amid attempts to seize them. Israeli forces have also blocked access roads, forced residents from two homes and turned 16 others into military posts. In Beit Dajan, Israeli forces on Monday demolished a residential structure and two agricultural structures and filled in a water well. Bethlehem: About 10 Israeli settlers Palestinian doctor Majed Dwayat with stones and sticks in Jannatah, east of Bethlehem, breaking his hand and smashing his car's windows, WAFA reported on Sunday. Kushner meets with Hamas leadership in Cairo: President Donald Trump's son-in-law and "Board of Peace" member Jared Kushner Hamas leaders in Egypt on Sunday to press the group to disarm and relinquish authority in Gaza, Axios reported. The Hamas delegation, led by political leader and chief negotiator Khalil Al-Hayya and including several senior leaders, attended talks with Kushner, Trump's board envoy Nickolay Mladenov, and Egyptian, Qatari, and Turkish mediators, according to Reuters. Tony Blair was also at the talks, according to Axios. A source familiar with the meeting told Axios that the talks sought "concrete, verifiable steps" toward Hamas decommissioning its weapons and military infrastructure, transferring governing authority to a Palestinian technocratic administration, and permitting an international force to deploy--commitments the group has already agreed to and repeatedly reaffirmed. At an earlier meeting with Egyptian intelligence chief Hassan Rashad, Al-Hayya stressed Hamas is ready to implement the agreement "as soon as Israel announces its commitment to it." Kushner and Mladenov met Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Monday. Regional powers condemn Israel for rejecting Gaza roadmap: Eight Muslim-majority countries issued a joint statement on Sunday condemning Israel for rejecting the roadmap saying, "Israel now bears responsibility for obstructing the efforts to bring peace in Gaza." The statement signed by Saudi Arabia, Turkey, the United Arab Emirates, Egypt, Jordan, Qatar, Indonesia, and Pakistan, called on the Board of Peace and the U.S. to take "immediate and concrete measures" to keep any party from obstructing the plan's implementation. Over 70 Palestinian families face eviction in Lydd: Israel has ordered the eviction of more than 70 Palestinian families in the city of Lydd in Israel, to Wafa. Israeli authorities issued the orders under the pretext of "seizing state lands." Palestinian Red Crescent evacuates 74 people from Gaza: The Palestine Red Crescent Society, with the help of the World Health Organization, 74 people from Gaza through the Rafah crossing on Sunday, including 38 patients and 36 companions, WAFA reported. When it first reopened Rafah earlier this year, Israel promised it would allow 50 Palestinian patients, with up to two companions each, to leave Gaza daily. Since the ceasefire began, 11,186 people, out of 28,600 scheduled, have passed through the crossing, a compliance rate of 39.1%. Nearly 20,000 patients, including thousands of children and cancer patients, require treatment that is unavailable in Gaza. Palestinian paramedic released by Israel after more than two months : Palestinian Red Crescent Society paramedic Waseem Al-Mughari, 33, was Sunday after 68 days of enforced disappearance, Healthcare Workers Watch (HWW) reported. HWW said an Israeli-backed armed militia intercepted his marked ambulance on Salah al-Din Road on June 9 while he was on duty. The militia subjected him and six PRCS colleagues to field interrogation before handing Al-Mughari over to Israeli forces. At least 10 Palestinian women prisoners contract scabies in Israel 's Damon Prison: These cases come amid severe overcrowding, poor ventilation, and shortages of cleaning supplies and clothing, the Palestinian Prisoners' Society Monday. More than 90 Palestinian women are currently held at the prison, including pregnant women, minors and prisoners with chronic health conditions. The group said scabies has continued to spread through Israeli prisons since May 2024, while Israeli prison authorities have failed to adequately address the conditions driving the outbreak or provide effective treatment. The group described the continuing outbreak and denial of medical care as part of a broader system of "torture and systematic medical neglect." Israeli Supreme Court considers case of detained Palestinian journalist: The Israeli Supreme Court a session Sunday to review the case of Palestinian journalist Mohammad Arab, Haaretz reported. Israeli forces detained Arab on March 14, 2024, while he was working as a correspondent for Al-Araby TV inside the Al-Shifa Hospital complex in Gaza City. Since March 2024, he has been held under Israel's "Unlawful Combatants Law," which permits the state to hold individuals indefinitely without formal charge or trial, and his detention has repeatedly been extended at six-month intervals. Reports from his lawyers indicate that Arab's health has deteriorated drastically over the course of his 29 months in custody, and he previously engaged in a hunger strike to protest the prison's conditions. The court considered an appeal by his lawyers to halt the repeated six-month extensions of his detention. The hearing concluded without a ruling, and Arab remains detained at the Ketziot prison in the Negev desert. Lebanon Israeli strikes on Lebanon kill 11 amid supposed ceasefire: Israeli on Ansar and Deir Al-Zahrani in southern Lebanon on Saturday killed 11 people and wounded 19, the highest single-day toll since the June ceasefire, according to Lebanon's Health Ministry. Israeli strikes on Ansar killed seven, including a mother and four children, and killed four in Deir Al-Zahrani, where 17 others were wounded. Israel claimed its attacks targeted "Hezbollah infrastructure" in response to activity against Israeli troops in the Ali Al-Taher Heights, which Israel claimed is inside what it calls its "security zone." A Hezbollah drone struck a combat engineering unit near the Ali Al-Taher Saturday, three Israeli soldiers, the Israeli military later claimed on Sunday. Separately on Saturday, Israeli forces the last remaining houses in the town of Mais Al-Jabal, began constructing an earthen barrier near Khallet Haris-Haddatha, deployed troops along the road between Mais Al-Jabal and Wadi Slouki, and fired artillery at Taybeh, Kfar Tibnit, Zawtar Al-Sharqiya and Mansouri. On Monday, Israeli forces targeted Aitaroun in Bint Jbeil district with artillery and machine-gun fire, according to Lebanon's National News Agency. Israeli warplanes also two rounds of strikes on Mansouri in Tyre (Sour) district. Lebanese leaders condemn Saturday attacks; Hezbollah vows response: Leaders from Lebanon's government Israel's escalation in the country's south on Saturday, while Hezbollah promised an "appropriate" response to the strikes. President Joseph Aoun called the attacks "a clear message against the negotiation process and U.S. efforts to implement the agreement." Prime Minister Nawaf Salam condemned Israel's killing of civilians, noting that the women and children killed in Ansar were "not 'military infrastructure.'" In a Saturday, Hezbollah warned that Israel's continuing violations and "attempts to impose a fait accompli" would draw an "appropriate response." The group demanded that Lebanese authorities abandon what it called "humiliating direct negotiations" under U.S. sponsorship, arguing that these negotiations made the government "complicit" in Israeli attacks on the country. Hezbollah has refused to engage in direct talks with Israel and was not a party to the deal. Aoun says Israel pushing to end UNIFIL presence as Israeli military activity surges in southern Lebanon: The United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon (UNIFIL), the UN peacekeeping mission deployed in southern Lebanon, Monday that Israeli military activity in the area had increased significantly over the past two weeks, recording an average of 137 Israeli projectiles per day between August 5 and 16, including 208 on Saturday and 185 on Sunday. The figures came as Lebanese President Joseph Aoun calls to extend UNIFIL's mandate. "Israel rejects UNIFIL's presence and has been pushing in this direction for nearly a year, while we are demanding that it remain," Aoun said, adding that Lebanon's first choice is to extend the force's mandate, with an alternative international force alongside the Lebanese army as a second option. U.S. News DNC votes to back abolishing ICE: The Democratic National Committee a non-binding resolution Saturday during its summer meeting in Austin urging Congress to abolish ICE and wind down the immigration detention system, alongside a more strongly backed separate proposal calling for reforms to the agency. The resolution passed in Austin calls for federal legislation to abolish ICE, for the agency's operations and its detention infrastructure to conclude and close down, to condition DHS appropriations on reducing ICE's operations, to terminate private prison contracts and to release immigration detainees except under limited circumstances. It also calls for expanded civil rights oversight in the U.S. immigration system. In response to Saturday's vote, DNC Chair Ken Martin said official party positions are set every four years at the national convention but that Democrats remain united in opposing current enforcement tactics. Trump orders reduction of joint military exercises with South Korea: President Donald Trump Sunday he instructed War Secretary Pete Hegseth to "substantially reduce" U.S. participation in joint military exercises with South Korea, complaining in a social media post that Seoul had not joined U.S. efforts on Iran's "denuclearization" while praising his "very good relationship" with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un. The announcement, which caught the Pentagon off guard according to a senior U.S. military official, comes as the U.S.'s 11-day Ulchi Freedom Shield exercises with South Korea began on Monday. Blanche declines to pledge DOJ independence from Trump on prosecutions : Attorney General Todd Blanche Sunday to pledge that the Justice Department would "always act independently" of the White House, telling NBC's Meet the Press that "no attorney general should ever pledge that" and that President Donald Trump should "of course" have a voice in individual prosecution decisions, according to Axios. Blanche called it an "extraordinarily false narrative" that Trump directs him to prosecute specific people, even as Trump has repeatedly named individuals he wants charged, including former FBI Director James Comey and New York Attorney General Letitia James , both of whom the DOJ has prosecuted. During a separate interview with Fox News, Blanche said that Trump "would expect me to tell him no" in cases of legal disagreement, saying "the president loves disagreement." Supreme Court again rejects Trump 's bid to overturn E. Jean Carroll verdict: The Supreme Court a second request from President Donald Trump's lawyers to reconsider throwing out a jury's $5 million finding that he sexually abused writer E. Jean Carrol l in the 1990s and later defamed her, according to the Associated Press. Trump paid the $5 million judgment shortly after the Court refused to take up his appeal in June. Trump and the Justice Department are separately asking the high court to toss out a second Carroll verdict totaling $83 million, arguing presidential immunity shields him from being sued over 2019 comments he made about her while in office, a case the court has not yet acted on. 📥 Have a tip on Capitol Hill? Email DC Correspondent Julian Andreone at Julian@dropsitenews.com Other International News UAE trained mercenaries in Sudan: Seven Colombian mercenaries the Financial Times that UAE-based GSSG recruited, trained and deployed about 2,000 fighters to support Sudan's Rapid Support Forces, according to an investigation from the outlet published on Saturday. "It's the Emirates that put in the most money and resources," one former commander explained. Around 300 specialists trained in drones and anti-aircraft weapons at Emirati bases, including in Abu Dhabi, and traveled through UAE-backed hubs in Somalia and Libya. One battalion fought beside the RSF in the siege and capture of El Fasher, where Yale estimates 60,000 civilians were killed in the weeks after its fall. Fighters said GSSG paid bonuses when the city fell. Fighting in Sudan 's Blue Nile State displaces thousands as RSF advances: Clashes between the Sudanese army and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces have thousands of residents to flee parts of southeastern Blue Nile State, with civil society monitors reporting civilians crossing the river by small boat after the RSF-aligned Tasis Coalition seized the strategic town of Geissan near the Ethiopian border on Tuesday. The Blue Nile Civil Society Initiative warned that military operations during a period of extreme weather in the region pose a direct threat to civilians and called for an immediate ceasefire and safe humanitarian corridors to reach stranded populations. The RSF and its ally, the Sudan People's Liberation Movement-North, have advanced in both Geissan and the border town of Kurmuk in August. Russia jails opposition party chairman for 11 years over anti-war comments: A Russian court Lev Shlosberg, deputy chairman of the liberal Yabloko party, to 11 years in a penal colony after convicting him of "discrediting" the armed forces and spreading false information about the war in Ukraine following comments criticizing the invasion. Shlosberg used his closing statement to demand an immediate ceasefire and denounce the war as a catastrophe for Russia, stating "one day the entire nation will shudder at this list of martyrs," from the conflict. The sentence comes a week after Russia's Supreme Court barred Yabloko--the only registered party calling for an end to the war--from participating in next month's parliamentary election. Taiwan plans record defense spending amid growing Chinese pressure: Taiwanese President Lai Ching-te said Taiwan's 2027 defense budget will to the equivalent of $31.4 billion USD, exceeding 3% of GDP for the first time, as Taipei accelerates military modernization in response to mounting Chinese pressure. Lai called the spending "an investment in peace," while Taiwan continues developing submarines and expanding preparations for scenarios including a Chinese maritime blockade. The increase also reflects sustained U.S. pressure on Taipei to shoulder more of its own defense costs. Somali troops claim to retake Baidoa from opposition forces: Somali federal forces that they had driven opposition fighters out of the city of Baidoa after heavy clashes. Federal authorities said that they had repelled an attack by Laftagareen's forces using vehicle-borne explosives and that around 30 assailants were killed, while statements on social media by Laftagareen's office claimed that the city center was still held by his movement. Baidoa has been a flashpoint since federal troops seized the city in March after forces loyal to former South West state president Abdiaziz Hassan Mohamed Laftagareen broke with Mogadishu over constitutional disputes. India claims to foil Pakistan-backed militant plot: Indian security agencies more than 200 alleged members of what Home Minister Amit Shah claimed was a militant network backed by Pakistani intelligence in a coordinated operation across 14 states. Shah said the crackdown targeted what he called the "Shahzad Bhatti Network" and prevented planned "subversive attacks," with authorities claiming to recover pistols, ammunition, and grenades bearing Pakistan Ordnance Factory markings. Syrian detainee dies in government custody amid torture allegations: Mohammad Ghamira, a resident of rural Latakia and former member of the Syrian Civil Defense, in government custody while he was being held over a financial complaint, according to the Syrian Observatory for Human Rights, which said that accusations of torture had emerged in connection with his death. Ghamira developed severe bleeding in detention over several days, and after release was found to have suffered a brain hemorrhage, falling into a coma and dying in intensive care at a nearby hospital. Syria's Interior Ministry said that it had initiated an investigation into the circumstances of Ghamira's death. British prime minister exchanged messages with an impersonator posing as Trump aide: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham with messages from someone impersonating White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles before growing suspicious the contact was illegitimate, four officials told Politico, prompting the British embassy in Washington to raise concerns with the White House. One person briefed on the exchange said a "few messages" were sent after Burnham entered No. 10 but described them as "of no significance." A White House official said the incident "had nothing to do with the Chief of Staff's devices being hacked," though officials within the UK government feared Wiles' phone had been compromised again following a similar hacking investigation last year, in which someone claiming to be Wiles contacted senators, governors and business executives. | | ---|---|--- 🛒 for your Drop News/Not Bombs Hoodie 💬 our Whatsapp Broadcast Channel for the latest reporting, podcasts, and breaking news, delivered directly ⚠️ You can go to your to unsubscribe from the Drop Site Daily newsletter--while still getting the rest of our reporting Become a Drop Site News Paid Subscriber Drop Site News is reader-supported. I want to use this space this morning to talk about Laura Loomer -- who I've come to believe is one of the most tragic people holding onto power anywhere inside Donald Trump's MAGA movement.
For the better part of the last several years, she has tried to destroy my life. She's gone after my staff. She's gone after my company. She's gone after my family. She is, by any honest measure, a miserable person, and it would be the easiest thing in the world for me to sit here and tell you that I hate her. Frankly, I have every reason to.
But I don't. This weekend -- after _The New York Times_ published a story about Donald Trump's Department of Justice targeting my consulting business -- I sat with all of it. And what I landed on isn't hate. It isn't even anger anymore. It's something closer to pity. I actually just feel bad for her.
Let me tell you how Laura spent her weekend. She spent it yelling into the void about conspiracy theories she invented. She attacked me for my weight. She attacked me for my history with my own mental health. She attacked me for being empathetic -- for being willing, during the darkest stretch of the COVID pandemic, to talk openly about a period when I seriously considered harming myself. That's what she did with her Saturday and her Sunday. Think about that. Two days of your one precious life, spent obsessing over somebody you hate.
And I'm telling you: what a sad and lonely way to live. It's the behavior of someone with no real human connection -- no community holding her up outside of a handful of dead-enders on X. She has traded intimacy for engagement. She has substituted clickbait for love. And I say all of this as a content creator myself, somebody who understands the pull of the feed better than most. I know how easy it is to start confusing people paying attention to you with people actually caring about you. They aren't the same thing. Not even close.
Because here's the contrast. I worked this weekend too -- I sure didn't plan to spend my Saturday morning reacting to a DOJ story, and I wasn't happy about it. But I also built Legos with my son. I watched the Cubs. I took my wife downtown for a date to see _The Notebook_ and a great dinner. I grilled out back and made a hell of a pork roast. I did all of that because I have a full, vibrant life -- one filled with meaning and connection and love. And somewhere in the middle of all of that, it hit me: Laura Loomer can't take any of it away from me. Donald Trump can't either. And that's _real_ power.
Laura Loomer doesn't have that. She thinks she does. She thinks the false admiration she gets from Donald Trump every time she manufactures a conspiracy against one of his enemies is the same thing as being loved. She thinks the hearts and the shares on X and Rumble -- the only two platforms that will still have her, because they're built for exactly this -- are the same thing as community. They aren't. Her own father has publicly said that his daughter has serious mental health issues and probably needs to be institutionalized. Think about what that does to a person who has no family and no friends to catch them.

Each one makes this movement harder to kill.](https://substack.com/redirect/1353e624-0d9e-4605-bbf0-a395fb66bcae?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**_

* * *
And it points to something sick in our culture right now. In any other era, Laura Loomer would be a crackpot on a street corner in a tinfoil hat, and the world would simply walk past her. Instead, the worst version of social media handed her a rocket. Then MAGA handed her power. And Donald Trump handed people like her access to the machinery of the federal government. That's where this stops being pathetic and starts becoming dangerous. She got the entire MAGA movement to come after me, my business partner, and my staff -- with no credible evidence of anything. She got the House Judiciary Committee to open an investigation based on her so-called "reporting," which amounts to posting FEC screenshots of which congressional candidates have paid my firm to run digital ads. That's the whole case.
And because Donald Trump is the most corrupt man on the planet -- so committed to punishing his opponents, so desperate to build a culture of fear that lets him get away with his own corruption and incompetence -- his DOJ has picked it up too. Except there's no there there. They can't even name the law I'm supposed to have broken. And that's the point. They don't necessarily need a crime. They need an investigation. They need the headline. They need you hiring lawyers and wondering what's coming next. They need your employees scared, your clients nervous, your family worried.
Jim Jordan didn't have the balls to hold me in contempt when he investigated me after Laura Loomer harassed him. He didn't have the guts to invite me to testify in front of his committee -- which I would have done gleefully, and which would not have gone well for them. I'd have walked in there like Pam Bondi with a burn book and roasted every one of them. The difference is mine would've been justified. I wouldn't have been there to cover up the abuse of kids.
And here's the truth of it: the day Donald Trump leaves office or leaves this earth, Laura Loomer becomes instantly irrelevant. Her only value is her usefulness to him. Nobody else is particularly interested. Because the power Laura Loomer has isn't actually hers. It's borrowed. It belongs to Donald Trump. And eventually, the bill comes due on borrowed power.
A lot of you have reached out to ask what you can do. Here it is: keep supporting us as independent content creators, so we can build something fully sustainable and impossible to intimidate. Because that's how you beat this shit. You build things they can't scare into submission. You build communities they don't control. You build a life whose meaning doesn't rise and fall with the attention of powerful people. Don't start a GoFundMe. Don't worry about us. We are going to be okay -- financially and legally.
I'm a practicing Catholic. I try to lead with redemption and empathy and love, and I'll be honest with you, that is hard to do when the person coming for the people you love is as miserable as Laura Loomer. But I want to extend her some grace anyway. Not because she deserves a pass for what she's done. She doesn't. And not because I'm pretending I'm above being angry. I'm not. But because I refuse to let people like Laura Loomer decide what kind of person I become. I don't want to spend my one life consumed by people I hate. I don't want cruelty to become my personality. She is hurting. And hurt people hurt people.
So, Laura -- if you're reading this, and I suspect you will be because you're obsessed with me: I hope you get the help you need. I hope that one day you find real community, real connection, something you don't have to manufacture from a screen. It's a sad way to exist.
As for me, I'm going to keep doing what actually matters. Focus on the people you love. Work on being better. Be of service to your community. Do some good. Build some Legos. Grill a pork roast. Touch grass. Build a life so full of meaning that people like Laura Loomer can't possibly take it from you. And whatever you do -- don't let the bastards grind you down.
With Urgency,
--Mike

What did the American public get in return? Steep, high-elevation, inaccessible peaks. Unless you brought the climbing gear required to scale a vertical wall of shale rock, **you are now locked out of your own public land.** They are effectively building a ring of private wealth around our shared natural heritage, cutting off regular hunters, hikers, and anglers from the places they've enjoyed for generations. And they are doing it right out in the open because they are betting that you won't fight back. They are testing the waters. If Doug Burgum and his billionaire buddies can get away with privatizing the Crazy Mountains piece by piece, they will use this exact blueprint to lock up every piece of prime public land in the West. But they severely miscalculated. At Public Land Warriors, we won't let them turn our national heritage into a private playground for the 0.1%. My job is to make sure every voter in this district gets the full truth.

## **ICYMI: Union Leader: Patrick Hynes: Pappas takes Granite Staters for a ride, Washington style**
---
| | | | | |

**Patrick Hynes: Pappas takes Granite Staters for a ride, Washington style
** Patrick Hynes
[Union Leader](https://us.list-manage.com/UFItCJheA3W?e=f3aa6419cd&c2id=cbe815d8d4829b0196839495b093775b&m=8rxpnKOmWj6Sv8ngZ1DtP83CwV08pe-yqBnIk7NBL3XbKFaA71nLHXIwtQ==)[
](https://us.list-manage.com/ZYujr4g280p?e=f3aa6419cd&c2id=cbe815d8d4829b0196839495b093775b&m=RYuNDpcpaw8E0kf0TV_DqHWBj-5JWflEUEYhuIxg5rmAdLmgNh03xNBAXg==)August 15, 2026
Congressman Chris Pappas, the Granite State Democrat running for Senate on a solemn vow to fight “corporate special interests,” sits on the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee. His husband, Vann Bentley, works for Uber. Pappas and his husband own up to $350,000 worth of Uber stock, according to the congressman’s own financial disclosure filings.**On May 22, Pappas sat in a committee room in Washington and voted to advance a $580 billion federal transportation bill. Tucked inside that bill is a provision that would functionally immunize Uber the next time one of its drivers assaults a passenger. Under the language Pappas voted to advance, victims of everything from kidnapping to rape could not hold Uber itself accountable in court unless they could prove the corporation was guilty of “gross negligence” or “criminal wrongdoing.” Trial lawyers say clearing that bar is nearly impossible and Uber’s lawyers agree.** ...Now, consider the number of daughters, sisters and mothers who climb into Ubers every weekend from Portsmouth to Manchester to Hanover to Concord. Who is looking out for them?Three weeks after voting the Uber liability shield out of committee, [Pappas signed a letter](https://us.list-manage.com/DFeRgUL92Zp?e=f3aa6419cd&c2id=cbe815d8d4829b0196839495b093775b&m=l5oY6kcpirYj8xxpfmwurMsg7WYW9G5ODeQCYirng-jbHMWlV6vWwJtKFw==) along with 127 other Democrats politely asking Speaker Mike Johnson to strip out the provision Pappas had just voted to advance. The letter warns the language could be read to preempt state liability laws and shield rideshare companies when their drivers harm passengers. No kidding. A group of California Democrats sent a sharper letter the same week.In other words, Pappas voted with the corporation and then, when it became politically untenable, papered it over.This isn’t the first time Pappas has voted on legislation that directly impacts his family’s bottom line.In an October 2020 debate on WMUR, Republican challenger Matt Mowers asked Pappas whether he was dating an Amazon lobbyist while voting on legislation Amazon lobbied on. “How dare you?” Pappas snapped. “That is not true, Matt. This is an outrageous charge.”It was true. Pappas was dating Amazon lobbyist Vann Bentley. He would go on to marry him in 2023. That same year, Bentley took his current job with Uber.Pappas’ campaign website, meanwhile, informs prospective donors he “won’t take a dime of corporate PAC money.” And yet, [NH Journal reported](https://us.list-manage.com/DgIGQfgPobs?e=f3aa6419cd&c2id=cbe815d8d4829b0196839495b093775b&m=ql8vRzUD29B12O8_es7YIPpf5on74AGaa9N66Nj6WGW7jVax-sb6ldNNMw==) last month that his **Senate campaign had already cashed a $5,000 check from an energy industry corporate PAC, quietly refunded only after reporters started asking questions. The campaign called this a “clerical error.” Individual Uber lobbyists have been permitted to give the Pappas campaign $5,250, because personal checks from corporate lobbyists apparently don’t count against a pledge about corporate lobbyist money.** The transportation bill now moves to the House Rules Committee, and from there to the House floor. Chris Pappas will be asked to vote on it a second time. He has a choice: He can vote to protect the Granite State women who ride in Ubers on Friday nights. Or he can vote to protect the balance sheet of the company writing his husband’s paychecks....Read more [here](https://us.list-manage.com/4suia7itOmW?e=f3aa6419cd&c2id=cbe815d8d4829b0196839495b093775b&m=K5dafqhrE3NTHOh31Ie9ar_ady4h7f2nFlUliyUUHe-GmU6owE2InwW_XQ==).

name: Gina Hinojosa
subject: I never planned for this.
body:
I didn’t plan to run for governor. But Greg Abbott left me no choice.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
For so many families across Texas, the past few weeks have revolved around one thing: back to school.
My boys are both starting school again. As hectic as it’s been on the campaign trail, I’m never too busy to not be in “mom mode,” especially during back-to-school season.
You see, Peter, the fight to save my son’s school is why I first chose to run for office at all.
**I never planned on running for Governor. I never even planned on being in politics. But sometimes life puts a decision in front of you that you can’t ignore.**
For me, that moment came the day I learned my son’s elementary school was being closed because of budget cuts. It wasn’t failing or unsafe — just “in the way” of a plan to hand schools over to private interests looking to profit off our kids' futures. Families and teachers were shaken and uncertain of what would come next, and I realized something terrifying:_No one was coming to save us._
So I stepped up. I ran for the Austin ISD’s Board of Trustees, won, and helped block a corporate takeover of our public schools.
It taught me something powerful: **When Texans stand up, we win big battles.**
But the fight was just starting. Neighborhood schools kept closing across Texas because Republican leaders kept diverting money away from classrooms. So I made another decision I never expected to make: I ran for the Texas House.
As a state representative, I secured billions in school funding. I passed a first-of-its-kind law so Texas businesses could do well financially _and_ do good in our communities. I delivered nearly a billion dollars in healthcare funding to Travis County. I helped organize walkouts that blocked Abbott’s voter suppression bill and fought back against his school voucher scheme.
**The same determination I’ve had my entire career is why I’m running for Governor of Texas today — to defend the Texas I grew up with and fight for every student and family who calls this state home.[If you’re able to chip in $5 or more today to power our fight, I’d be so grateful.](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260817_1_politics.nW2jOG&refcode=em20260817-1853&amount=5&t=1&akid=1853%2E299639%2EGRi1UD)**
Texas simply can’t afford another four years of Greg Abbott.
For a decade, Abbot has sold out working families to enrich the wealthy and powerful at every step. He kicks children off Medicaid to save a few extra bucks for Big Pharma. He shuts down public schools so private interests can get rich on vouchers. He ignores families crushed by rising prices while he funnels nearly a billion of our taxpayer dollars into no-bid contracts for his donors.
With your help, I can become the next Governor of Texas. I’ve beaten Abbott before, and I’m ready to do it again. **Right now, he’s the least popular he’s ever been, and multiple polls are showing that we’re within the margin of error — so this is our chance.**
I’m asking you directly, Peter: **[Can I count on you to pitch in $5 today and power the movement to take Texas back?](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260817_1_politics.nW2jOG&refcode=em20260817-1853&amount=5&t=2&akid=1853%2E299639%2EGRi1UD)**
[Donate $5 »](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260817_1_politics.nW2jOG&amount=5&refcode=em20260817-1853&t=21&akid=1853%2E299639%2EGRi1UD)
I’ve said it before, and I’ll say it again: Never mess with Texas teachers, and never mess with Texas moms.
Gratefully yours,
Gina Hinojosa

[ Donate » ](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_gh_footer?refcode=em20260817-1&t=22&refcode2=1853_299639_GRi1UD&akid=1853%2E299639%2EGRi1UD)

Cami Clark, the secretive wife and key adviser to Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, sought[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/bff7fbd6-cd74-4921-b9a4-03afc20e01d3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[investment from Jeffrey Epstein for her revolutionary porn company years after](https://substack.com/redirect/bff7fbd6-cd74-4921-b9a4-03afc20e01d3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** his prison sentence for sex crimes.

---|---|---
* **Key adviser presence** : Clark maintains a minimal public profile while acting as a sounding board and strategic adviser, often seen at Davos and talking with investors at Sun Valley.
* **Brought early investor** : She brought Democrat megadonor Eric Schmidt, whom she had dated, as a key early investor to Anthropic in early 2021 as the company got off the ground.
* **Porn company pursuit** : Scrutiny revealed she started a revolutionary porn company and courted convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein for investment years after he served a jail sentence.
* **Information scrubbed online** : Efforts have been made to remove references to her from the internet, and Anthropic's Claude AI appears to have little information about her.

# [Wall Street fear gauge hits 2026 low amid complacency](https://substack.com/redirect/2567095e-5aa2-4800-94f7-3bb49562031c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The VIX dipped to 14.2 on Friday, its lowest level of 2026, as the S&P rose some 16% year-to-date toward record highs, **[but strategists warn the calm is unlikely to last.](https://substack.com/redirect/1799345a-f847-45a7-925c-b6ff308a1ec4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

A personalized model of Ferrari's first fully electric vehicle, the Luce, **[sold for $40 million in a Sotheby's charity auction at Monterey Car Week,](https://substack.com/redirect/dba2a467-6b8b-4400-96c7-64b4de768a2c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** setting a record for a new car.

---|---|---
* **Record auction result** : The Sotheby's sale of the Luce tailor-made first production chassis featured a unique semi-gloss finish and bespoke parts, with proceeds going to Ferrari's educational foundation.
* **Base model pricing** : The Luce was unveiled nearly three months ago and priced at 550,000 euros or roughly $640,000, marking Ferrari's first fully electric car amid design criticism.

Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw
Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

_**by Ellie Leonard, Blue Amp Media Contributing Editor**_
With the help of a great crowdsourcing community on Substack, we were able to find multiple documents in the Epstein Files that showed Epstein likely visited Trump Tower on November 13th, 2016, 5 days after Donald Trump won the presidency.
According to media outlets, including the [Sun Sentinel](https://substack.com/redirect/ae277eab-1d03-40ae-9eb8-1485767efe2f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [Roll Call](https://substack.com/redirect/3391bc94-bbf3-4876-942c-23724f160807?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and [CNN](https://substack.com/redirect/d7737018-66e0-4009-a95f-7e8ff02da6f9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), Trump spent the day holed up on the 5th floor making decisions about high-level cabinet positions. Downstairs in the lobby, important characters came and went, documented throughout the week by a bank of photographers that seemingly never slept.
But how do we know Epstein, who was never photographed, was in the room as these important decisions were made? Well, that's where the power of crowdsourcing and "two heads are better than one" comes in.
In this case, it took four simple documents--all that mattered individually, but combined provided proof of Epstein's whereabouts.
#### 1\. EFTA01620474
On November 10th, 2016, Ken Mapp, then Governor of the U.S. Virgin Islands, received a text (SMS) message from an unknown sender, saying, _" Trump means many opportunities. I'll be back next week."_
Three days later, the unknown sender reaches out again.
"Seeing Trump people today, can we speak? I know it's Sunday :)"
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b6c0b09e-439c-4df6-8ccb-ac7b8181daea?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Ken Mapp changes the subject and begins discussing permitting on Great St. James, the big island between Little St. James and the mainland. He's disappointed that "unknown" has not followed the protocols. And although we know Epstein purchased the big island in 2016, we still can't verify for sure who is speaking.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b6c0b09e-439c-4df6-8ccb-ac7b8181daea?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
But on November 15th, 2016, the unknown sender says something unique.
"as you might guess , If i feel a sneeze coming on , I ask for legal advice. What john woods ericka, and amy say, contradict some of the contentions. I have no relevant view. ( not my expertise )"
When I saw this, I thought we might be able to figure out who was speaking to Mapp. Unique phrases are often the key to finding unredacted documents in the DOJ files. Sure enough, with a little digging, something else popped up,
* * *
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b6c0b09e-439c-4df6-8ccb-ac7b8181daea?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* * *
#### 2\. EFTA02669184
On the same day that the "unknown" sender told Mapp "If i feel a sneeze coming on," Epstein sent an email to himself saying the exact same phrase. This is something he often did, to either give himself a virtual high-five to refer to later, or to document things he'd said to important people.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b6c0b09e-439c-4df6-8ccb-ac7b8181daea?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
This verified that Jeffrey Epstein was the "unknown" sender in the SMS text thread on November 13th, 2016 who claimed to be _" seeing Trump people,"_ the same day Donald Trump met with high-level officials at Trump Tower.
_But we 'd need more proof._
[Ellie's Coffee Fund](https://substack.com/redirect/49f8da84-82ef-49d3-8b72-8f8818360c72?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
_**We got it**_ --and it's two words Epstein typed himself.

| | | Friend, you deserve to know why Alaska’s primary election is so important. We’re just one day out from Primary Day, so in a moment, I’m going to ask you to make a contribution to help get out the vote in this final window before voters cast their ballots. But first, let me explain why Alaska’s primary is special – and why your support will make a big difference to my campaign. Tomorrow is Primary Day in Alaska. Alaska has an open primary, which means I’ll be on the ballot with every other candidate running for U.S. Senate – including incumbent Senator Dan Sullivan. This is our first chance to flex our grassroots power directly against the DC establishment at the ballot box, and you can bet that everyone will be watching to see where we fall. And the truth is, Friend – the moment Primary Day passes, the general election will start in full swing. That means we need to be ready. We have to get out the vote to win big tomorrow, and then we have to hit the ground running in what will be the most competitive and consequential Senate race this year. I’m going up against an opponent backed by billionaire donors who want to keep the rigged DC system that’s benefiting them in place, so I need a huge grassroots team to come together to show them we can do this. If everyone reading this chipped in $5, $10, or $50, we’d be well on our way to raising what we need to win. But unfortunately, not everyone is in a place to give. We’re just one day out from Primary Day, so in a moment, I’m going to ask you to make a contribution to help get out the vote in this final window before voters cast their ballots. But first, let me explain why Alaska’s primary is special – and why your support will make a big difference to my campaign. Tomorrow is Primary Day in Alaska. Alaska has an open primary, which means I’ll be on the ballot with every other candidate running for U.S. Senate – including incumbent Senator Dan Sullivan. This is our first chance to flex our grassroots power directly against the DC establishment at the ballot box, and you can bet that everyone will be watching to see where we fall. And the truth is, Friend – the moment Primary Day passes, the general election will start in full swing. That means we need to be ready. We have to get out the vote to win big tomorrow, and then we have to hit the ground running in what will be the most competitive and consequential Senate race this year. I’m going up against an opponent backed by billionaire donors who want to keep the rigged DC system that’s benefiting them in place, so I need a huge grassroots team to come together to show them we can do this. If everyone reading this chipped in $5, $10, or $50, we’d be well on our way to raising what we need to win. But unfortunately, not everyone is in a place to give. subject: We passed it. Now let’s build it.

body:
Insulin at $35. Medicare negotiating drug prices. The biggest climate investment in history.
---
| | Peter,

Four years ago, the Inflation Reduction Act was signed into law. I want to be direct with you about what it did, and about what is happening to it right now.

**My proposal to allow Medicare to negotiate drug prices was included in this legislation, giving it the power to negotiate drug prices. This was a huge win.** For decades the largest purchaser of prescription drugs in the country was forbidden by law from asking for a better deal. That is over. We capped insulin at $35 a month and capped out-of-pocket drug costs for seniors at $2,000 a year.

**We made the largest climate investment in American history.** Not a pledge - money, on the ground, for clean energy, resilience, and manufacturing. In a county that just spent five days under an extreme heat warning, that is not abstract.

**And I keep pushing on the piece nobody puts on a bumper sticker: permitting reform.** Clean energy does not cut a single ton of emissions sitting in a warehouse or waiting a decade for a grid connection. We passed the investment. Now we have to be able to build - the transmission lines, the housing, the projects. _That is the work I have spent years on, and it is not finished._

Here is why I am writing today instead of just celebrating...

This administration is already moving to end subsidies for Medicare drug premiums. The climate money is being clawed at. Every one of these wins is a law, and laws can be repealed by a Congress that wants to repeal them.

We are less than 90 days from the election. My Republican opponent finished too close for comfort in the primary, in a year national Republicans have decided they are keeping control of Congress.

clean_body: Insulin at $35. Medicare negotiating drug prices. The biggest climate investment in history. | | Peter, Four years ago, the Inflation Reduction Act was signed into law. I want to be direct with you about what it did, and about what is happening to it right now. My proposal to allow Medicare to negotiate drug prices was included in this legislation, giving it the power to negotiate drug prices. This was a huge win. For decades the largest purchaser of prescription drugs in the country was forbidden by law from asking for a better deal. That is over. We capped insulin at $35 a month and capped out-of-pocket drug costs for seniors at $2,000 a year. We made the largest climate investment in American history. Not a pledge - money, on the ground, for clean energy, resilience, and manufacturing. In a county that just spent five days under an extreme heat warning, that is not abstract. And I keep pushing on the piece nobody puts on a bumper sticker: permitting reform. Clean energy does not cut a single ton of emissions sitting in a warehouse or waiting a decade for a grid connection. We passed the investment. Now we have to be able to build - the transmission lines, the housing, the projects. That is the work I have spent years on, and it is not finished. Here is why I am writing today instead of just celebrating... This administration is already moving to end subsidies for Medicare drug premiums. The climate money is being clawed at. Every one of these wins is a law, and laws can be repealed by a Congress that wants to repeal them. We are less than 90 days from the election.
