name: Aaron Ford
subject: This made me furious
disclaimer_text: Paid for by the Committee to Elect Aaron Ford
body:
I know how exciting it is for kids to get back in the classroom and learn new things, but I also know that this time of year can put an extra financial strain on working families.
# [](https://act.fordfornevada.com/go/12?t=1&akid=702%2E127862%2E2ZRelF)
Folks, it’s back-to-school season, and this time of year is extra special to me.
I used to be a public school math teacher. I know how exciting it is for kids to get back in the classroom and learn new things, but I also know that this time of year can put an extra financial strain on working families.
I’ve been there, personally — food stamps and WIC kept my family afloat when I was a single dad putting myself through school.
That’s why when I saw MAGA Gov. Lombardo veto a bill that would’ve guaranteed free meals for public school kids, I was _furious._
**When I’m governor, I'll make sure that bill becomes law.**
And I won’t stop there. Nevada's classrooms are already among the most crowded and worst-funded in the nation. Our teachers are stretched thin.
**As governor, I'll invest in and protect our public schools, because I know firsthand what it means when our government shows up for kids. It changed my life. It can change theirs.**
As students and teachers return to the classroom, they deserve someone in the governor’s office who has their backs. **[Will you chip in $5 today to help us get there?](https://act.fordfornevada.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_af_20260817_1_ak.v3j5bz&amount=5&refcode=em20260817-702&t=3&akid=702%2E127862%2E2ZRelF)**

Thanks so much,
Aaron

👆 A pic from earlier this month, where we gave out free backpacks and back-to-school haircuts for our kids.

name: Brandon Gill
subject: I crashed my first tractor the summer after 3rd grade.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Brandon Gill for Texas
body:
It’s Congressman Brandon Gill. You could say I first learned what It meant to be a conservative while I was out on the ranch.

| |
---
| | [](https://email.editor.goppresidential.com/c/eJyckLGO3SAQRb8GdzwZzAKvcBHpyak22S6lNQtjexQMFox38_4-sqL8wJYjje655_56nV-BEuX1B-w4ruU45tpmChXahnF_LlQbc4XApfKGs-61lb2Xys0QmD5wNtDF0YA11toOR-W8vXtrle62UTnU2gX7Yv2Cxt2NUREcKOU8Ll75jsYrsPfKKad61d-i98tdoXkBHXrrB2F6jMSl3q5uFRtFzEyQbqHsXRo35qOJ4ZvQk9BTw3BWvH1SrhivD6Gn9wo5lixXSkkupUrGP9CEnnJBaE-G9lu-n5Qi5TVsZw0btnrmfJ3AnFDiLg-4AMNUL0ClvIrhwfVEoe3J-8xBDI_vP9_e5H8doS3sfJRGTCWL4aG6Osbjk1KiZp0w_boD_bPgr-7-Meq_AQAA__-w7JVb)
---
Patriot, — I crashed my first tractor the summer after 3rd grade. I spent my summers building churches and running cattle. My high school class had 24 kids in it – We didn't even have enough people to field a football team. It’s Congressman Brandon Gill. You could say I first learned what It meant to be a conservative while I was out on the ranch. When you're building fence out on the ranch you need something to keep your mind going - that's when I started listening to the radio. Rush Limbaugh, Mark Levin, Sean Hannity were on full blast as I drove my tractor, operated the backhoe and built fences. Rush Limbaugh’s voice always seemed to have a way of settling the nervous cattle down. **That's when I first started to think that I wanted to be in politics. I didn't quite know how, but _God had his plan for me._** Those early mornings, those long days, that crackly AM radio — it shaped who I am today. It taught me that America is the greatest place on earth. a land of intrinsic beauty and wonder. It taught me that freedom is worth fighting for as something real and precious that you protect with every fiber of your being. It taught me that God and family are the foundation of everything. So at 29 years old, I decided to run for Congress where I became the youngest House Republican. **[I never imagined that just a few years later, I’d be facing a deadline as massive as this one and sending a final message like this one pleading for your help.](https://email.editor.goppresidential.com/c/eJyckLGO3SAQRb8GdzwZzAKvcBHpyak22S6lNQtjexQMFox38_4-sqL8wJYjje655_56nV-BEuX1B-w4ruU45tpmChXahnF_LlQbc4XApfKGs-61lb2Xys0QmD5wNtDF0YA11toOR-W8vXtrle62UTnU2gX7Yv2Cxt2NUREcKOU8Ll75jsYrsPfKKad61d-i98tdoXkBHXrrB2F6jMSl3q5uFRtFzEyQbqHsXRo35qOJ4ZvQk9BTw3BWvH1SrhivD6Gn9wo5lixXSkkupUrGP9CEnnJBaE-G9lu-n5Qi5TVsZw0btnrmfJ3AnFDiLg-4AMNUL0ClvIrhwfVEoe3J-8xBDI_vP9_e5H8doS3sfJRGTCWL4aG6Osbjk1KiZp0w_boD_bPgr-7-Meq_AQAA__-w7JVb)** Look, when I first made my decision to go to Washington, I made a promise to myself, to my wife, and to my children. I told them that as long as I live, I will FIGHT to preserve the soul of America. I promised my kids I would fight for their future. Now, more than ever before, the radical left has infected the minds of our next generation with a poisonous hatred for our country. subject: Give me a break…
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY VOTEVETS, VOTEVETS
body:
Now he says the ballroom is inseparable from the military complex that’s going underneath it.
#
Peter, give us a break. Take a look at this:
[](https://act.votevets.org/go/2927?c0=vv-pac-em-aug26.uvTq9l&refcode=em260817-1-360&t=1&akid=35472%2E3013755%2E7xFaRJ)
But let’s run this back a bit, because it’s important to remember what’s happened up until now. First, Trump demolished an entire wing of the White House so he could build himself a ballroom.
Originally, he said it would be funded by private donors. Then he said it would mostly be funded by private donors. Then... some. And now, as the price tag approaches $900,000,000, the bill is going to be footed almost entirely by taxpayers.
Originally he said the ballroom was so he could wine and dine VIPs, no doubt to shake all the change out of their pockets on the way out. But federal courts ordered construction of the ballroom to be stopped, because that’s just literally not how any of this works.
But now, to get it moving again, Trump changed his tune. Now he says the ballroom is inseparable from the military complex that’s going underneath it. That the ballroom is absolutely essential to “National Security” and “Military Readiness” because that’s how he thinks he can forge ahead and build it without following the rules.
Unfortunately, you can’t just slap “National Security” and “Military Readiness” on a vanity project to dodge a court order and the Constitution. Particularly while you wage an illegal war, while stocks of defensive and offensive munitions are exhausted, and sailors are literally trying to end their own lives because their deployments have gone on so long. This is an insult to our Troops.
Look, we know how this is going to go. Republicans won’t lift a finger to stop it, right?
Wrong. If we do what needs to be done between now and Election Day, a Democratic Congress is going to take power in January. They are going to stop Trump’s ballroom, the Arc de Trump, and force Trump into ending his illegal war with Iran.
But none of that happens if we don’t raise the resources we’ll need to elect our candidates. It’s going to take a lot of work. It’s going to take a lot of time. It’s going to take a ton of money. But if we commit now, we can do it.
[**So, Peter, we’re humbly asking you: Will you please make a donation to VoteVets so we can elect Democrats to the House and Senate, end this chaos, and hold Trump accountable? We wouldn’t ask if this wasn’t important.**](https://act.votevets.org/go/2927?c0=vv-pac-em-aug26.uvTq9l&refcode=em260817-1-360&t=2&akid=35472%2E3013755%2E7xFaRJ)

This is an insult to our Troops. Look, we know how this is going to go. Republicans won’t lift a finger to stop it, right? Wrong. If we do what needs to be done between now and Election Day, a Democratic Congress is going to take power in January. They are going to stop Trump’s ballroom, the Arc de Trump, and force Trump into ending his illegal war with Iran. But none of that happens if we don’t raise the resources we’ll need to elect our candidates. It’s going to take a lot of work. It’s going to take a lot of time. It’s going to take a ton of money. But if we commit now, we can do it. subject: Meet the farmer who's going to fight for South Dakota

Meet Steve McCleerey, a farmer, rancher, man of faith, and your next Lt. Governor

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/6ebf2b48833c/health-care-you-deserve-10597766?e=cee7b49c04)

| | | | | | Friend,
Wednesday, I introduced South Dakota to my running mate: Steve McCleerey, a rancher and farmer from Sisseton who’s spent his life doing the work instead of just talking about it.
Steve’s not a career politician. Instead, he’s:
* **Spent 20 years working South Dakota’s family farms:** A cow/calf operation and row crops after years as a dairy farmer. Steve knows what it costs to make a living off the land and he knows what Pierre owes the people who feed this nation.
* **Served six years in the State House:** Rising to Assistant Minority Leader, where he made a name for himself bringing Republicans to the table because he knows state government should work for everybody.
* **Spent two decades on his local hospital board:** Plus service on a nursing home board, because rural health care and long-term care shouldn’t just be abstractions.
* **Been a property rights advocate:** Steve understands that when government overreaches on the land South Dakotans work for, someone has to stand up.

At our press conference, Steve made a simple statement, “We’re here to help solve problems, not cause problems.” That’s Steve’s word. And that’s our ticket.
The GOP represents 50 years of one-party rule in Pierre that’s left our state struggling and working South Dakotans without a seat at the table. Steve and I represent something different; a promise to work for all South Dakotans, not just the connected few in Pierre.
We don't have the same donor network the other side does. What we have is a true message, and a team that's earned it. _**That’s why we need you.**_
Could you chip in _**$25, $50, or whatever you can right now**_ to help take this ticket across the finish line in November?
Forever fighting for you,Dan Ahlers _Your Candidate for Governor_

[ ](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137401588/640661009/693975070?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzAvMS85MTExMyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJlNjNlZTZkZi01ZjlhLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=w5Uyt2N4DbgGhOPrZYBxBRvUaX2IEgObXvLwJNeYg3A=&emci=6819b3ed-de98-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&emdi=e63ee6df-5f9a-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&ceid=15820338)

Peter,

As summer comes to a close and kids across Washington start getting ready to head back to school, I've been thinking about just how much we ask of our public schools—and how much they give us in return.

But before I go any further, **[will you sign my petition if you agree Congress needs to be doing more to protect our kids' futures and defend our public schools from Trump's politically motivated attacks?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137401589/640661010/1546051260?ms=em26_260815_schl_adv_gq_act___ks_ettx&refcode=em26_260815_schl_adv_gq_act___ks_ettx&source=em26_260815_schl_adv_gq_act___ks_ettx&utm_campaign=em26_260815_schl_adv_gq_act___ks_ettx&utm_medium=email&contactdata=O+K5Hqy1DwJBwdMGcdsC18vweI4A1C/NEeBQ8uzBHtefef9/H7bjwClzSR9xieydkaw3cGsEIj+uTkHPEIJ+H8Yd360WovLWJ0n+cC8dSukMGqe5tRs5lfwdeLFFH0A8JJfBqPhEhbOD4+laOMkcEDdDmGjVfYyIxnMf9QGhMZA=&refcode2=e63ee6df-5f9a-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzAvMS85MTExMyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJlNjNlZTZkZi01ZjlhLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=w5Uyt2N4DbgGhOPrZYBxBRvUaX2IEgObXvLwJNeYg3A=&emci=6819b3ed-de98-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&emdi=e63ee6df-5f9a-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&ceid=15820338)**

**For me, helping our public schools thrive is personal.** My mother was a public elementary school teacher, my son attends our local public school, and my entire education—from kindergarten through college and medical school—was public. We have been so fortunate.

To put it very plainly: _I would not be where I am today without the teachers who believed in me and the public schools that gave me the opportunity to succeed._ I want every child to have that same chance, no matter their zip code or how much money their family makes.

That means investing in our schools. It means paying our teachers what they deserve. And it means making sure students have the resources and support they need to learn, grow, and build the futures they dream of. But unfortunately, Donald Trump and his Republican allies are determined to take us in the opposite direction.

Almost immediately after taking office, Trump moved to dismantle the Department of Education, cutting roughly 1,200 workers and putting critical services for students at risk. Experts have warned these cuts could delay FAFSA processing and financial aid for students across the country, but that hasn't stopped this administration from taking an axe to our children's futures. And that's just the tip of the iceberg.

Trump has shamelessly used funding cuts, lawsuits, visa actions, and threats to accreditation to pressure schools and universities. Our kids' education should never be a political bargaining chip. We should be opening doors for the next generation—not making it harder for students to get an education or taking resources away from the teachers and schools they depend on.

**[If you agree, add your name to my petition today and demand that Congress protect public education from the Trump administration's attacks and stand up for our students, teachers, and schools.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137401590/640661011/1546051260?ms=em26_260815_schl_adv_gq_act___ks_ettx&refcode=em26_260815_schl_adv_gq_act___ks_ettx&source=em26_260815_schl_adv_gq_act___ks_ettx&utm_campaign=em26_260815_schl_adv_gq_act___ks_ettx&utm_medium=email&contactdata=O+K5Hqy1DwJBwdMGcdsC18vweI4A1C/NEeBQ8uzBHtefef9/H7bjwClzSR9xieydkaw3cGsEIj+uTkHPEIJ+H8Yd360WovLWJ0n+cC8dSukMGqe5tRs5lfwdeLFFH0A8JJfBqPhEhbOD4+laOMkcEDdDmGjVfYyIxnMf9QGhMZA=&refcode2=e63ee6df-5f9a-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzAvMS85MTExMyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJlNjNlZTZkZi01ZjlhLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=w5Uyt2N4DbgGhOPrZYBxBRvUaX2IEgObXvLwJNeYg3A=&emci=6819b3ed-de98-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&emdi=e63ee6df-5f9a-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&ceid=15820338)**

Every child deserves the opportunity to succeed. I'll keep fighting to make sure they have it.

Thank you,

Most of the political world had counted us out when we were trailing by double digits in the polls. But just like working people across our state, we didn’t give up. Well, the votes have been counted. And Wisconsin Democrats came together and won by working hard and building a real coalition. So let's be honest about what happens now. The general election started last week, and Tom Tiffany started it loaded. Here's the gap we're facing: 💰MAGA Tom Tiffany already raised more than $15 million, including a $10 million transfer straight from the state Republican Party. 📺 He's basically been running unopposed and has been able to run ads against Democrats for months. 📉 We just spent everything we had to win this last election. That's why the next few days are so important. What we raise right now gets read by every politician and pundit in this state as a measure of whether Democrats can come together after a hard primary. | | I'm no stranger to coalition building. I got my start in the Legislature finding common ground to pass legislation that helped people. As Milwaukee County Executive, the youngest person and the first Black person to hold that office, I brought together labor, business, and community organizations to get real results. That's the job now: bringing together every part of this state to beat MAGA Tom Tiffany. Early polls already show us with a lead against him, but if we learned anything from this primary, it's that we can't always trust the polling in Wisconsin. If you know Sherrod Brown, you know the guy loves baseball. Especially the Guardians. So today, we're breaking this race down in terms our fellow baseball fans will understand.

**Top of the first: National Republicans think Jon Husted is an all-star.** They handed him a Senate seat – no election, just called him up and put him in the lineup.

Turns out he has no idea how to hit for Ohio. He's been striking out ever since.

He struck out on health care, voting to strip coverage from millions to pay for a tax break for the wealthy. He struck out on tariffs that raised prices for Ohio families. And on data centers, he didn't just strike out – he recruited the pitcher, cut him a deal, and then told the fans it was their fault the game was going badly.

name: Autism Health
subject: Help Shape the Future of Autism: Your Voice Matters
body:
We have an incredible opportunity to help shape the future of autism research, medical care, services, and supports in the United States... but we need your voice.

The Interagency Autism Coordinating Committee (IACC) has released its 2026–2028 Working Draft Strategic Plan for public comment. This document represents a significant step toward creating a more comprehensive federal framework for autism that addresses the needs of individuals and families across the lifespan. The working draft is still subject to revision and public feedback will play an important role in determining the final version.

** Why Your Positive Feedback Matters
------------------------------------------------------------

If you believe this Strategic Plan moves our community in the right direction, please take a few minutes to submit a positive public comment.

Constructive, supportive feedback helps demonstrate that families want to see this work move forward. The more positive comments received, the stronger the message to federal leadership that these priorities matter and deserve to be implemented.

This plan has the potential to improve the lives of countless individuals and families by expanding the federal focus beyond diagnosis alone and addressing many of the real-world challenges our community faces every day.

** Highlights of the Working Draft
------------------------------------------------------------

The proposed Strategic Plan includes a broad range of priorities, including:
* A stronger focus on co-occurring medical conditions and whole-person health.
* Increased attention to gastrointestinal health, immune function, metabolism, mitochondrial function, sleep, epilepsy, and other medical conditions that frequently impact individuals with autism.
* Recognition of neurodevelopmental regression as a national research priority.
* Greater investment in precision medicine and personalized approaches to autism care.
* Improved access to diagnosis, treatment, and clinical care across the lifespan.
* Expanded support for nonspeaking and minimally speaking individuals through improved communication access.
* Better resources for caregivers, including respite services, family support, and navigation.
* Increased focus on housing, employment, transportation, aging, and adult services so individuals with autism receive support throughout every stage of life.
* Greater federal coordination, transparency, and accountability for implementing measurable outcomes.

** How You Can Help
------------------------------------------------------------

Please submit a brief, respectful comment expressing your support for this working draft and why these priorities are important to you and your family.

Email your comments to: iaccpublicinquiries@mail.nih.gov (mailto:iaccpublicinquiries@mail.nih.gov)

Deadline: Thursday, August 20

For more information on the IACC meeting, the Strategic Plan, and the public comment process, go to www.iacc.hhs.gov (https://track.pstmrk.it/3s/links.givebutter.com%2Fengage%2FVa6wL%2FgVQqGbn/b43o/YXHHAQ/AQ/1cdf835c-19f5-49a4-92da-ba2d83599484/2/82CSsj5eAK?mc_cid=7864c36eaf&mc_eid=UNIQID) or click HERE (https://track.pstmrk.it/3s/links.givebutter.com%2Fengage%2FaeK5e%2FgVQqGbn/b43o/YXHHAQ/AQ/1cdf835c-19f5-49a4-92da-ba2d83599484/3/t9NI4NQGSf?mc_cid=7864c36eaf&mc_eid=UNIQID) .

Every voice matters.

Together, we can help ensure that this Strategic Plan reflects the real needs of autism families and moves us closer to better research, better healthcare, better services, and a better future for everyone impacted by autism.

Thank you for standing with us and making your voice heard.

With Sincere Gratitude,
Steve & Tracy Slepcevic
Founders of Autism Health Inc.

It can be easy to feel overwhelmed by the headlines.

The work ahead is enormous. The right is carrying out a coordinated attack on our basic civil liberties. Too many families are struggling to afford housing, healthcare, and the basics. And there is no shortage of people who would rather divide us than solve problems.

But here’s something I don’t want us to lose sight of: **Progressives are showing up. Our ideas are resonating. And we’re winning.**

name: Dan Osborn
subject: Why I was fired:
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY RESIST RECLAIM REBUILD PAC (WWW
body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-osborn [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-osborn]
In October 2021, I had been an employee of Kellogg’s for almost 18 years.
I had dropped out of college and started working for the company after my wife got pregnant. Life’s easy when all you gotta do is take care of yourself – but we needed diapers and health insurance for our growing family.
Working at Kellogg’s used to be a lifelong career. A good-paying job that lets you become a homeowner, live decently, and hopefully retire someday.
But over the years, that changed. Workers were paid less. Cost-of-living adjustments weren’t keeping up anywhere near inflation. Retirement and health insurance plans were gutted. It just wasn’t right. They were making record profits – and doing it off the backs of workers.
So in October 2021, we walked out. And as president of our local union, I led the strike. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-osborn]
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP62/1/120031/images/Screen%20Shot%202026-04-24%20at%2011.20.44%20AM.png]
Most of us had never walked a picket line. It was cold, but we were determined to hold our lines through the dead of winter if we had to. We were a part of something bigger than ourselves. We were in a fight for the future of the American middle class.
After 11 weeks in the cold, we reached an agreement. More importantly, we saved 500 good-paying union jobs.
It was one of the proudest moments of my life.
Following the strike, I was fired. Someone had to pay – and as union president, my head was on the chopping block.
It’s easy to let yourself get beaten down by life. To let big corporations and the politicians they own in Washington make all the decisions – and just accept that that’s how things will always be. But that’s not me.
Instead, I decided last year to run against one of the most corporate politicians – U.S. Senator Republican Deb Fischer – and we nearly won. I got 47% of the vote in one of the closest Senate races in the country.
Now, I’m running again for the U.S. Senate – this time against billionaire Republican Pete Ricketts – and the first poll shows us virtually TIED: 46% to 45%.
I am taking on a literal billionaire senator. We can finish what we started last year and flip Nebraska’s Senate seat for working-class people, but I need grassroots donors like you to give now if we’re going to win.
Please, will you contribute to my campaign for U.S. Senate to help me defeat billionaire Republican Pete Ricketts here and flip Nebraska’s Senate seat? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-osborn]
DONATE TODAY TO DEFEAT THE MAGA BILLIONAIRES! [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-osborn]
I believe we can win this race and keep up the fight for the American middle class. But I’m counting on your support now to win.
Thank you,
Dan Osborn

We are officially less than two months out from the start of voting in North Carolina!
I am so grateful for everyone who has supported me in whatever ways they could. Some folks knock doors on the weekends, some make calls after a long day, some show up to an event or make a donation to help fuel this campaign. It all matters!
We're building something special here in North Carolina, and we're doing it with the grassroots support of people like you. So I wanted to give you an update on our folks on the ground, and all of their great work.
[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/7c1e522c-4f45-40aa-beb3-e97041aa9a35?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Volunteers canvassing all across the state
Our team has knocked over 215,000 doors, called more than 440,000 voters and signed up over 16,000 volunteers. To all the people who have invested in this campaign and joined this fight: **Thank You.**
This work is far from over and I am so fortunate to have you all by my side. Over the next 59 days, we're going to continue traveling across the state making sure folks are ready for the start of voting: talking with more voters, knocking on more doors, hosting more Make Stuff Cost Less events and more.
Volunteers canvassing all across the state
I know that this will be the toughest race I've faced. And I'm grateful to have you with me in this fight to fix what's broken in Washington DC and return power to the hands of the people.
Our leaders should be focusing on strengthening our communities by investing in public schools, making health care more affordable and prioritizing hardworking families. That work starts with talking with voters all across the state, and I'm grateful for all of our volunteers helping us do just that.
If you're able to help us [knock doors](https://substack.com/redirect/44eea1f3-d68f-4ecb-bf57-6fa877995ff6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [call voters](https://substack.com/redirect/44eea1f3-d68f-4ecb-bf57-6fa877995ff6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) or [chip in](https://substack.com/redirect/7c1e522c-4f45-40aa-beb3-e97041aa9a35?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) what you can, thank you for your help. Every effort counts and I couldn't do this without you.
P.S. Make sure you register to vote or check your voting status [here](https://substack.com/redirect/65fb4e09-425e-4e89-bd11-285a26d1ab9b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)!

**Hey folks - it's Roy Cooper.**
I've spent my life serving the people of North Carolina. As Governor, I expanded Medicaid to hundreds of thousands of hardworking people and fought for better health care. As Attorney General, I protected working families from fraud and abuse. As a State Legislator, I pushed for policies that made everyday people's lives easier.
But before all of this, I was just a boy from Nash County - the son of a public school teacher who tried to do right by his family, friends and neighbors.
Now, I'm running for the U.S. Senate because I've seen what's possible when government actually puts people first. When those in power lead with a sense of duty, purpose and moral clarity. That's not happening in Washington DC right now. **[Will you chip in today to help me change that?](https://substack.com/redirect/7c1e522c-4f45-40aa-beb3-e97041aa9a35?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

body:
The DLCC believes it can flip this LD2 State Senate seat.

| | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/24LtBAMN3BG?e=a7ab36849c&c2id=b6e4918ecaa4a9e494d38fc9e6fde211)
| | | | | | 📣 **August 17****th****Campaign Update**
ICYMI, last week the Democratic Legislative Campaign Committee (DLCC) added LD2 to its 2026 target list. This State Senate seat is being targeted once again as part of a coordinated national effort by the democrats to flip one or both chambers of the Arizona Legislature. LD2 is now a nationally targeted race — and I am one of only a handful of GOP incumbents the DLCC believes it can flip. **This means LD2 is now considered one of the most competitive legislative seats in the country.**
🧭**DLCC Targeting Context** Arizona is one of the DLCC’s top national priorities. Their strategy includes:• targeting 7 legislative districts for potential flips• heavy investment in suburban districts with narrow margins• messaging focused on national issues rather than local governance
🗳 **What This Means for Our Community and State** Democrats see LD2 as one of their best pickup opportunities. DLCC leadership publicly framed Arizona as “within striking distance” of flipping for the first time since the 1960s, and LD2 is one of their Senate level targets. My democrat general election opponent has already received more than 40% of her campaign funding from out-of-state leftwing donors who want her to implement policies that will hurt Arizona. She is also endorsed by a group that wants to defund the police, making our communities less safe. As you know, I have made safe communities a very high priority of mine.Now that my opponent has received the DLCC designation, her campaign will have access to • national data and analytics• a robust voter contact infrastructure from out of state organizations• national messaging support that may not reflect LD2’s local priorities• outside spending and independent expenditures from coordinated leftwing groups• and a surge in national moneyWe expected our opponent to receive a significant influx of national dollars. However, LD2 remains a district where local issues matter more than national narratives. This district supports pragmatic governance, and affordability issues resonate strongly.In November 2024, I won this R+1 district State Senate seat by 3.6% (~3,700 votes). Historically, LD2 runs close margins, but LD2 remains competitive, but not hostile territory. I have remained steadfast and focused on addressing cost of living and affordability issues to counter inflation, including reducing the red tape on housing, eliminating the municipal food tax, and bringing in competition for additional fuels to Arizona to open up the market. Democrats view LD2 as essential to breaking up our slight Republican majority in the Arizona State Senate, but they don’t have the winning message when it comes to affordability and pragmatic governance. I have been a voice for both these past two years.
🧭 **District Character** LD2 is a north Phoenix suburban district defined by rapid growth, family centered communities, and strong civic engagement. It’s one of Arizona’s most competitive legislative areas—balanced between long time homeowners and new arrivals drawn by the 303 corridor’s development near TSMC.
📊 **LD2 Data Snapshot** LD2 is one of the few Republican held Senate seats on their list. Our district’s voter registration (as of August 2026)• Republican: ~34%• Democratic: ~33%• Independent / Other: ~33%• Net Advantage: R+1
📰 **Call to Action** LD2 is now in the national spotlight—but our campaign remains focused exactly where it should be on the families, neighborhoods, and small businesses that make our district strong. While national leftwing groups pour money into Arizona, we will continue doing what we’ve always done—listening, engaging, and delivering results that matter.**I can’t do it alone. I need your support.** If you live in District 2 and would like to request a yard sign, we would be happy to deliver one to you. Please [email me](https://us.list-manage.com/R5kxHkLOkd8?e=a7ab36849c&c2id=b6e4918ecaa4a9e494d38fc9e6fde211) and we will make it happen!If you’re interested in hosting a meet‐and‐greet or volunteering, please reach out—these gatherings are a great way to connect with neighbors and discuss the issues that matter most to our community. Please [email me](https://us.list-manage.com/9s3_UaCya2v?e=a7ab36849c&c2id=b6e4918ecaa4a9e494d38fc9e6fde211) so we can get it scheduled!If you can’t make a donation, you can make one [online](https://us.list-manage.com/pdjXKIw7zrV?e=a7ab36849c&c2id=b6e4918ecaa4a9e494d38fc9e6fde211) today. I appreciate your continued support and for staying informed as we move into the heart of the 2026 election cycle. LD 2 is a competitive, but balanced legislative district.
📆 **Upcoming Events** In order to make the right investments to hold this highly competitive State Senate seat, we are continuing to hold fundraisers to raise the necessary resources to keep the GOP majority. You can help by making a [donation](https://us.list-manage.com/_65iTNoloj7?e=a7ab36849c&c2id=b6e4918ecaa4a9e494d38fc9e6fde211), or inviting other potential donors to donate as well.📍 August 19, 2026Fundraiser – Downtown Phoenix🕓 4:00 PM to 6:00 PM📩 [RSVP for the address.](mailto:info@bolickforarizona.com?subject=I%20want%20to%20support%20Shawnna%20on%208%2F19&body=)
📍 September 16, 2026Fundraiser – North Scottsdale🕠 4:30 PM to 6:30 PM📩 [RSVP for the address](mailto:info@bolickforarizona.com?subject=I%20want%20to%20help%20Shawnna%20on%209%2F16&body=).See you on Wednesday. Thank you for your continued support!Best,ShawnnaP.S. Do you have an hour or two between now and the November election? I represent the most highly competitive State Senate district in Arizona, and your support can make a meaningful difference. Whether it’s canvassing, phone banking, or helping at events, we would love to have you on our volunteer team. Please [email me](mailto:info@bolickforarizona.com?subject=I'd%20like%20to%20volunteer%20to%20help%20hold%20the%20State%20Senate&body=) so we can pull together to protect this seat.

* * *
April 9, 2026 started like any other Thursday for Maryam Tahmasebi. She was teaching a statistics class at Los Angeles Pierce College when her son texted her: his father hadn't picked him up from school, and wasn't answering his phone. That was strange. Eissa Hashemi is not a man who forgets his son. Maryam picked the boy up herself, drove home, and called the police, terrified something had happened to her husband.
Something had. It just wasn't the kind of thing the police could fix. Eissa -- a business psychology professor with a decade of mentoring PhD students, including U.S. military veterans, behind him -- had been picked up by ICE agents, with no warning to his family and no explanation given.
The next morning, Maryam drove her son to school. Department of Homeland Security vehicles surrounded her car. She watched her sixteen-year-old -- a kid who has lived in California, and only California, since before kindergarten, who speaks only English -- get handcuffed in front of his school. Mother and son were detained on the spot, then flown overnight to Texas, separately from Eissa.
That was more than four months ago. Eissa has been held at the South Texas Detention Center in Pearsall ever since. Maryam and their son have been held ninety miles away, at the Dilley "family detention center." When Maryam asked whether her husband could at least be transferred to Dilley so the family could be together, she says she was told, plainly, that keeping them apart is "the policy and the rule" in their specific case. Mother, father, and son now get ten minutes on the phone together, supervised, once every two weeks. That is the entire contact this family is permitted.
Here is what **none** of that was in response to: **a crime**. Eissa and Maryam do not have so much as a traffic ticket between them. They are lawful permanent residents -- green card holders -- who have lived in the United States for more than a decade, built careers as professors, mentored students, paid taxes, put down roots. If you wanted a checklist for what people are told to do to build a life here the right way, this family did **everything right.** That's not a rhetorical flourish. It's the undisputed record, and the government has never claimed otherwise.
None of it mattered. And the deeper you go into **why** , the stranger -- and more disturbing -- the answer gets.
Because in the middle of the four months this family has spent torn apart, in inhumane facilities they were shipped to overnight with no warning, something happened that should have ended this. An immigration judge looked at Eissa Hashemi's case and granted him permission to leave the United States voluntarily. His own court docket confirms it -- an exhibit filed in federal court is labeled, plainly, "Voluntary Departure Order."
**The United States government 's response was to appeal that order and keep him locked up anyway.**
Not deported. Not released. **Held** in detention -- while the government fights his own permission to leave a country that has already spent four months tearing his family apart trying to prove he shouldn't be here.
According to the family's attorneys, they've gone further than simply accepting an order -- they've offered to pay their own way out, to resettle in Turkiye, immediately, on their own money. **The government has fought that too.**
If you're having trouble understanding why a government would spend four months and counting keeping a law-abiding family separated in detention that it could simply put on a plane, you're reacting correctly. That confusion is the whole story. Getting this family out of America was never really the point. What the government actually wants is stranger, and more dangerous, than that.

## A law almost nobody has heard of
Most people assume deportation requires some concrete act -- a crime, immigration fraud, unlawful presence. There is another category, tucked into 8 U.S.C. § 1227(a)(4)(C)(i), that most Americans have never had reason to learn: a green card holder can be deported if the Secretary of State simply says that the person's presence "would have potentially serious adverse foreign policy consequences."
Note what that provision does not require. It is not the espionage statute. It sits nowhere near an accusation of spying, sabotage, or clandestine activity -- those live elsewhere in the same section of law. This is a different, much softer threshold: not what you did, but what your presence is said to mean.
The government's own public explanation for detaining this family makes the distinction explicit. Eissa's mother, Masoumeh Ebtekar, was a 19-year-old university student who served as the English-language spokeswoman for the group that seized the U.S. embassy in Tehran in 1979 -- before Eissa was even born. She went on to hold senior positions in the Iranian government.
When asked to justify detaining her son, daughter-in-law, and grandson, a State Department spokesman said only that people with close ties to senior Iranian officials **could** be exploited by Tehran for propaganda -- offering no example, no allegation, and no evidence specific to this actual family. Reporters who asked what Eissa, Maryam, or their son had individually done have not been given an answer, because there isn't one on the record.
The Secretary of State announced the move personally, on social media, in his own name: he had "terminated" the family's lawful permanent residence, and they were now in ICE custody "pending their removal."
## This didn't start in 2026
It would be easy to write this as if one administration simply invented a weapon. That's not quite right, and the more accurate version is more disturbing. In 1999, the Board of Immigration Appeals decided _Matter of Ruiz-Massieu_ , holding that a "facially reasonable" Secretary of State determination could itself serve as sufficient evidence of foreign-policy deportability -- the government **didn 't have to independently prove** the underlying harm.
The same decision held something else worth sitting with: the government is not required to let someone found deportable on foreign-policy grounds simply leave voluntarily before being run through full removal proceedings.
The tool has existed in the drawer for a quarter century. What's new is the willingness to use it, and what it's now being used for.

## The decision that changed the stakes: Matter of M-K-
On April 9, 2026, the Board of Immigration Appeals issued a decision in the case of Mahmoud Khalil -- the Columbia University graduate and Palestinian activist arrested in March 2025 over a Secretary of State letter asserting that his presence created foreign-policy consequences. On April 16, that decision was published as binding precedent: _Matter of M-K-_ , 29 I&N Dec. 556. **Binding** , meaning every immigration court in the country now has to follow it.
The holding is remarkable in plain English. The Board said Secretary Rubio's letter was itself "presumptive and sufficient evidence" of removability -- **DHS did not need to produce additional evidence proving the foreign-policy harm actually existed**.
The Board went further, comparing the Secretary's determination, without any proof, to a certified criminal conviction for evidentiary purposes, and instructed immigration judges generally not to "look behind" a facially valid foreign-policy letter, on the theory that doing so would intrude on the executive's foreign affairs power.
Read that again. One official writes a letter asserting a consequence. The letter itself then becomes the proof that the consequence is real. Khalil's case did still involve his own conduct -- his organizing activity, twisted into a "national security" threat.
Whatever you think of that case, it was still, nominally, about something **Khalil himself** did.

## From what you did to who you're related to
That is exactly the distinction the Hashemi/Tahmasebi case erases.
**There is no public allegation that Eissa Hashemi, Maryam Tahmasebi, or their son did anything at all.** Not a statement, not a donation, not a meeting, not an online post. The government's stated theory rests **entirely** on the fact of Eissa's mother's actions -- decades before he was born, in a country he left over a decade ago to build an academic career in the United States.
**And this is not an isolated case:** reporting has documented a broader effort by this administration against relatives of other Iranian officials, including relatives of Qassem Soleimani, and an immigration lawyer who has campaigned for years for such deportations has said he was contacted by DHS in January **seeking names.**
I want to be careful about what that proves and what it doesn't. It proves the administration is willing to apply this provision to people based on family relationship alone, and that this family is not the only one. It does not prove that officials deliberately selected this case to manufacture a favorable precedent -- I have no internal memo saying that, and I'm not going to pretend I do, although you're welcome to infer.
But intent isn't actually the load-bearing question here. However this case was chosen, if the government wins it on a theory where the only "foreign policy consequence" is a family tree, the precedent doesn't stay contained to one family.
_Matter of M-K-_ shows this Board is willing to publish decisions like this as binding law. A published win here would mean any immigration court in the country could treat kinship to a disfavored foreign official as sufficient grounds to strip a green card holder of their status -- no actual action, mistake, or conduct required.

## The trap built into the detention itself
Here's a question worth asking before we go further: **how can someone be detained at all before a final order of removal exists?** The answer, unfortunately, is that the law allows it. Under 8 U.S.C. § 1226(a), immigration authorities may arrest and detain someone "**pending** a decision on whether the alien is to be removed." Astonishingly, detention doesn't wait for a verdict. It's part of how the case is litigated.
But there's a second, even uglier layer specific to this provision. Under 8 C.F.R. § 1003.19, immigration judges are barred from redetermining custody conditions -- the ordinary bond hearing -- for anyone classified under section 237(a)(4), the national security (NS) provision.
A detainee can still argue they don't belong in that category, and DHS itself retains the power to release someone, but the normal path to a bond hearing before a judge is **closed** the moment this label attaches. The accusation doesn't just provide a theory for removal based on a single official's accusation. It helps build the cage the family has to argue their way out of, and makes sure they can't just be let go while their case is pending.
That's why this family's lawyers are in federal court on a habeas petition rather than simply asking an immigration judge for bond -- the ordinary door was locked by the same charge they're contesting. And which they had no notice of, and no opportunity to contest prior to their abduction. Filings in the consolidated case have continued through this month, with a bond motion and responses from the government still being litigated as of mid-August, last week.

## The voluntary departure order is the hinge of the whole story
Now return to where we started, because this is where the legal architecture gets genuinely strange.
Current regulation -- 8 C.F.R. § 1240.26 -- says an **immigration judge cannot grant voluntary departure to someone who is deportable under section 237(a)(4).** Not "shouldn't." Cannot. It's a categorical bar.
And yet an immigration judge apparently granted Eissa Hashemi voluntary departure.
Those two facts should not be able to coexist -- _**unless**_ something happened to the government's foreign-policy charge in front of that judge, that made it irrelevant -- that made the national security charge fail to stick.
To be eligible for the pre-case-completion form of voluntary departure, a person still has to concede removability on _some_ ground and give up their own right to appeal. So the most legally coherent reading of what we can see from the outside is this: **the government 's underlying theory that Eissa is deportable **_**for being his mother 's son**_**did not survive in front of the immigration judge,** even if the person was willing to give up the fight and leave the country.
I want to be precise about what this is: an inference, drawn from the fact that the regulation makes the two outcomes incompatible on their face. This is not a confirmed reading of an order none of us have seen.
But if it's right, the picture snaps into focus. Eissa is willing to leave. A judge has said he may. And the government is spending its resources not on removing him from the country, but on **overturning the judge 's refusal to brand him deportable on the ground that ties this to his mother.**

## Departure and removal are not the same thing, and that's the point
It would be easy to hear "he can leave voluntarily" and assume it settles the matter. It doesn't, legally. Voluntary departure and a formal removal order carry different consequences on a person's immigration history -- the regulations themselves require an alternate order of removal to sit behind every voluntary departure grant precisely because the two are treated as legally distinct outcomes.
**So ask again: what does the government actually want?**
If the goal were simply "this family should not be in the United States," an order letting Eissa leave accomplishes that, today, on his own dime. Fighting it doesn't advance that goal -- it actively delays it. The government's behavior only makes sense if there's a **second objective** : **not just his departure, but a formal legal finding that he is deportable** _**because of who his mother is**._ Voluntary departure denies the government that finding. A sustained removal order provides it.
I can't hand you a memo that says this in so many words. What I can hand you is a government that had the option to simply let a willing, green-card-holding professor leave the country months ago, and chose litigation and keeping him behind bars, instead.
## This is happening while the US is waging war on Iran
Wartime governments have always tried to blur the line between an enemy state, supporters of that state, nationals of that state, and -- the newest and most dangerous slide -- the family members of people connected to that state's government.
**The Constitution** -- **and the law** -- **exists to hold that line.** A family relationship is not a choice, an act, or an allegiance. The most basic principle we have -- older than the Republic -- is that **people answer for what they do, not for their blood.** One of this family's own attorneys put it plainly to a Texas reporter: it is **shameful** for the government to hold children accountable for the acts of their parents and grandparents.
Their son is sixteen. He has lived in California, and only in California, since before kindergarten. He speaks only English. He has been detained, apart from his father, for months, for something that happened forty-seven years before he was born.

## What comes next?
If this precedent holds, where else does the logic land?
Should the children of war criminals be imprisoned for their parents' crimes? Should the relatives of foreign officials in regimes currently committing genocide, be abducted from their homes and imprisoned without charge in terrible conditions indefinitely?
Who defines _**which**_ acts committed by parents, grandparents, or distant relatives, should suddenly be visited upon normal people living normal, peaceful, constructive lives today?
Where does it end?
## The feedback loop, laid out plainly
It's worth seeing the whole machine at once:
> **The Secretary of State determines, based on opaque and arbitrary reasoning, that a peaceful, law-abiding family 's presence in the US creates a "foreign-policy consequence."**
> -> DHS charges them as deportable under section 237(a)(4).
> -> ICE arrests them with no warning before any final order of removal exists.
> -> Their classification blocks the normal path to a bond hearing and release while their case is pending.
> -> Binding BIA precedent says the Secretary's letter alone can be sufficient proof, with no further evidence required.
> -> The family must fight the charge from inside detention.
> -> An immigration judge grants one of them permission to leave anyway.
> -> The government appeals that grant, preventing their departure.
> -> The appeal keeps the order from taking effect.
> -> He stays detained. So does his family.
No single link in that chain has to say **" indefinite political detention"** out loud for the chain, taken together, to produce something that looks exactly like it.
## A second, quieter due-process problem
One more thread worth pulling. The State Department has publicly described this as "terminating" the family's green cards, as though that were something the Secretary could simply announce.
But the federal regulation defining lawful permanent residence says status terminates upon entry of a _final administrative order_ of removal -- not upon a press release, and not upon a determination letter.
Until we see whatever instrument the government claims actually accomplished that termination, the administration's public language is running well ahead of what the regulation on its face appears to allow. That's a separate, quieter due-process question sitting underneath the louder one, and it deserves its own scrutiny.

## What the government's strongest defense looks like -- and why it still doesn't answer the question
It's worth taking the other side seriously, because this argument is harder to dismiss than it looks.
Congress did deliberately give the Secretary of State unusual latitude in this specific area, on the theory that foreign-policy judgments sometimes turn on relationships and networks that don't fit neatly into a criminal charge. Masoumeh Ebtekar was not an anonymous grandmother -- she was a public figure in a hostage crisis, and later a senior official in a government the United States has now decided to treat as hostile.
Grant all of it. It still leaves the load-bearing questions unanswered: **What, specifically, did Eissa Hashemi do? What did Maryam Tahmasebi do? What did their son do?**
If the danger is what their continued presence might mean to a foreign government, why does an order letting one of them leave immediately fail to eliminate that danger? Why is detention -- rather than, say, passport surrender and reporting requirements -- necessary while the government litigates a theory it hasn't yet proven?
And if family relationship alone is enough here, what is the limiting principle? How far does the bloodline have to run before it stops counting as evidence? Spouses. Children. Grandchildren, apparently. Where, exactly, does it end?
The government's strongest case still can't answer that last question. That's the tell.
## What should be demanded, publicly, right now
A few documents and a few answers would resolve most of what's still inference here:
1. **Release Eissa Hashemi 's voluntary departure order.** What, specifically, happened to the foreign-policy charge in front of that judge?
2. **Release DHS 's appeal of that order.** What is the government actually asking the Board to reverse?
3. **Release the Secretary 's foreign-policy determination for each family member.** Is there any individualized basis at all, or is it the same letter with three names attached?
4. **Identify the instrument that supposedly terminated their green cards** , and reconcile it with the regulation's final-order requirement.
5. **Explain, specifically, why detention is necessary** when the family has offered to leave, funded, immediately.
6. **Explain the sixteen-year-old 's detention separately**, in terms that don't reduce to his grandmother. The standard regulations for detention of children impose a _**maximum of 20 days**_. It's been over four months.
7. **State the limiting principle.** How distant can the relationship be and still count? Let's get that answer in writing.
8. **Disclose how many people have been investigated or detained under this provision since January 2025** , and on what stated basis in each case.

These aren't rhetorical questions. They're the specific things that would decisively answer what the legal end-game is here. We can't properly fight a problem we've only partially identified.
## What the government actually wants
Return to where this started. A man offered to leave. A judge said he could. The government that arrested him in the first place is now the party fighting to keep that from happening.
There may be a narrower explanation sitting inside a document none of us have seen yet. If so, it should be made public, because the family, the public, and frankly the government's own credibility would all benefit from it.
But on everything visible right now, the government's own behavior is doing the talking, and what it's saying is uncomfortable: physical departure was never going to be enough. Something more was being sought. And the only "something more" available on this record is a formal legal finding that a green card holder's presence in America can be treated as dangerous -- not because of anything he did, but because of who he was born to.
The US is functionally at war with Iran right now. Laws written for extraordinary, individualized foreign-policy cases do not stay abstract once they start being applied to professors and their sixteen-year-old sons because of their relatives' politics.
The question in front of us is no longer only whether this one family gets to go home, or to Turkiye, or anywhere else they choose.
It's whether the United States is building a legal pathway where ancestry itself can be entered into evidence against you.

This is the case -- not "Tahmasebi v. Mullin."

### The statutes and regulations
**8 U.S.C. § 1227(a)(4)(C) -- the foreign-policy deportability ground.** [https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/8/1227](https://substack.com/redirect/c09e0153-043d-4ecf-bdff-2c61f5438fb9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) The provision itself: a green card holder is deportable if the Secretary of State determines their presence would have "potentially serious adverse foreign policy consequences."
**8 U.S.C. § 1226(a) -- pre-removal-order detention authority.** [https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/8/1226](https://substack.com/redirect/0f459599-e290-4e60-8913-e4496c41fff4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Confirms ICE can detain someone "pending a decision on whether the alien is to be removed" -- detention doesn't wait for a final order.
**8 C.F.R. § 1240.26 -- voluntary departure eligibility.** [https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-8/chapter-V/subchapter-B/part-1240/subpart-C/section-1240.26](https://substack.com/redirect/bd0c9cea-9c83-4304-a69c-db1916a66c05?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) The regulation that makes Eissa's voluntary departure order legally strange: someone deportable under § 237(a)(4) is categorically barred from receiving it.
**8 C.F.R. § 1003.19 -- the bond-hearing bar.** [https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-8/chapter-V/subchapter-A/part-1003/subpart-C/section-1003.19](https://substack.com/redirect/c5c4b519-9217-4c8a-8019-39332c606a82?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Blocks immigration judges from redetermining custody conditions for anyone classified under § 237(a)(4) -- the provision that forced the family into federal habeas court instead of an ordinary bond hearing.

### The case law
**Matter of Ruiz-Massieu, 22 I &N Dec. 833 (BIA 1999).** [https://myattorneyusa.com/immigration-blog/deportation-and-removal/removal-deportation-defense/section-237-deportability-statutes-security-and-related-grounds/](https://substack.com/redirect/e350cfa7-53b0-4814-977b-48448fb207d8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) The 1999 precedent holding that a facially reasonable Secretary of State letter is itself sufficient evidence of foreign-policy deportability, and that the government isn't required to let someone leave voluntarily before deportation proceedings begin.
**Matter of M-K-, 29 I &N Dec. 556 (BIA 2026) -- official decision text.** [https://www.justice.gov/eoir/media/1436196/dl?inline=](https://substack.com/redirect/1d8f002c-6dbd-455e-9f13-a9ca5e68921a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) The Mahmoud Khalil decision itself. Decided April 9, 2026.
**ARLnow, "Board of Immigration Appeals swats away Mahmoud Khalil's appeal," Apr. 16, 2026.** [https://www.arlnow.com/2026/04/16/board-of-immigration-appeals-swats-away-mahmoud-khalils-appeal-mon1/](https://substack.com/redirect/1b3e5407-65e8-4f7e-9511-988c26d2d11d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Explains the gap between the two M-K- dates: decided April 9, publicly released and designated binding BIA precedent April 16 -- the distinction the essay draws on directly.
