Two law-abiding professors and their teenage son have become this regime's test case for indefinite political detention based solely on "family guilt." No civilized country is supposed to do this. | | | Aug 17 | | | | | | | | | | | | They followed every rule the American immigration system laid out and built a life here. ICE tore them apart anyway -- the father seized one day, the mother and son the next -- and has refused, for four months and counting, to let this family so much as sit in the same room. Then a judge gave one of them permission to leave the country voluntarily. The government is fighting that too. | | ---|---|--- April 9, 2026 started like any other Thursday for Maryam Tahmasebi. She was teaching a statistics class at Los Angeles Pierce College when her son texted her: his father hadn't picked him up from school, and wasn't answering his phone. That was strange. Eissa Hashemi is not a man who forgets his son. Maryam picked the boy up herself, drove home, and called the police, terrified something had happened to her husband. Something had. It just wasn't the kind of thing the police could fix. Eissa -- a business psychology professor with a decade of mentoring PhD students, including U.S. military veterans, behind him -- had been picked up by ICE agents, with no warning to his family and no explanation given. The next morning, Maryam drove her son to school. Department of Homeland Security vehicles surrounded her car. She watched her sixteen-year-old -- a kid who has lived in California, and only California, since before kindergarten, who speaks only English -- get handcuffed in front of his school. Mother and son were detained on the spot, then flown overnight to Texas, separately from Eissa. That was more than four months ago. Eissa has been held at the South Texas Detention Center in Pearsall ever since. Maryam and their son have been held ninety miles away, at the Dilley "family detention center." When Maryam asked whether her husband could at least be transferred to Dilley so the family could be together, she says she was told, plainly, that keeping them apart is "the policy and the rule" in their specific case. Mother, father, and son now get ten minutes on the phone together, supervised, once every two weeks. That is the entire contact this family is permitted. Here is what none of that was in response to: a crime. Eissa and Maryam do not have so much as a traffic ticket between them. They are lawful permanent residents -- green card holders -- who have lived in the United States for more than a decade, built careers as professors, mentored students, paid taxes, put down roots. If you wanted a checklist for what people are told to do to build a life here the right way, this family did everything right. That's not a rhetorical flourish. It's the undisputed record, and the government has never claimed otherwise. None of it mattered. And the deeper you go into why , the stranger -- and more disturbing -- the answer gets. Because in the middle of the four months this family has spent torn apart, in inhumane facilities they were shipped to overnight with no warning, something happened that should have ended this. An immigration judge looked at Eissa Hashemi's case and granted him permission to leave the United States voluntarily. His own court docket confirms it -- an exhibit filed in federal court is labeled, plainly, "Voluntary Departure Order." The United States government 's response was to appeal that order and keep him locked up anyway. Not deported. Not released. Held in detention -- while the government fights his own permission to leave a country that has already spent four months tearing his family apart trying to prove he shouldn't be here. According to the family's attorneys, they've gone further than simply accepting an order -- they've offered to pay their own way out, to resettle in Turkiye, immediately, on their own money. The government has fought that too. If you're having trouble understanding why a government would spend four months and counting keeping a law-abiding family separated in detention that it could simply put on a plane, you're reacting correctly. That confusion is the whole story. Getting this family out of America was never really the point. What the government actually wants is stranger, and more dangerous, than that. A law almost nobody has heard of Most people assume deportation requires some concrete act -- a crime, immigration fraud, unlawful presence. There is another category, tucked into 8 U.S.C. § 1227(a)(4)(C)(i), that most Americans have never had reason to learn: a green card holder can be deported if the Secretary of State simply says that the person's presence "would have potentially serious adverse foreign policy consequences." Note what that provision does not require. It is not the espionage statute. It sits nowhere near an accusation of spying, sabotage, or clandestine activity -- those live elsewhere in the same section of law. This is a different, much softer threshold: not what you did, but what your presence is said to mean. The government's own public explanation for detaining this family makes the distinction explicit. Eissa's mother, Masoumeh Ebtekar, was a 19-year-old university student who served as the English-language spokeswoman for the group that seized the U.S. embassy in Tehran in 1979 -- before Eissa was even born. She went on to hold senior positions in the Iranian government. When asked to justify detaining her son, daughter-in-law, and grandson, a State Department spokesman said only that people with close ties to senior Iranian officials could be exploited by Tehran for propaganda -- offering no example, no allegation, and no evidence specific to this actual family. Reporters who asked what Eissa, Maryam, or their son had individually done have not been given an answer, because there isn't one on the record. The Secretary of State announced the move personally, on social media, in his own name: he had "terminated" the family's lawful permanent residence, and they were now in ICE custody "pending their removal." This didn't start in 2026 It would be easy to write this as if one administration simply invented a weapon. That's not quite right, and the more accurate version is more disturbing. In 1999, the Board of Immigration Appeals decided Matter of Ruiz-Massieu , holding that a "facially reasonable" Secretary of State determination could itself serve as sufficient evidence of foreign-policy deportability -- the government didn 't have to independently prove the underlying harm. The same decision held something else worth sitting with: the government is not required to let someone found deportable on foreign-policy grounds simply leave voluntarily before being run through full removal proceedings. The tool has existed in the drawer for a quarter century. What's new is the willingness to use it, and what it's now being used for. The decision that changed the stakes: Matter of M-K- On April 9, 2026, the Board of Immigration Appeals issued a decision in the case of Mahmoud Khalil -- the Columbia University graduate and Palestinian activist arrested in March 2025 over a Secretary of State letter asserting that his presence created foreign-policy consequences. On April 16, that decision was published as binding precedent: Matter of M-K- , 29 I&N Dec. 556. Binding , meaning every immigration court in the country now has to follow it. The holding is remarkable in plain English. The Board said Secretary Rubio's letter was itself "presumptive and sufficient evidence" of removability -- DHS did not need to produce additional evidence proving the foreign-policy harm actually existed. The Board went further, comparing the Secretary's determination, without any proof, to a certified criminal conviction for evidentiary purposes, and instructed immigration judges generally not to "look behind" a facially valid foreign-policy letter, on the theory that doing so would intrude on the executive's foreign affairs power. Read that again. One official writes a letter asserting a consequence. The letter itself then becomes the proof that the consequence is real. Khalil's case did still involve his own conduct -- his organizing activity, twisted into a "national security" threat. Whatever you think of that case, it was still, nominally, about something Khalil himself did. From what you did to who you're related to That is exactly the distinction the Hashemi/Tahmasebi case erases. There is no public allegation that Eissa Hashemi, Maryam Tahmasebi, or their son did anything at all. Not a statement, not a donation, not a meeting, not an online post. The government's stated theory rests entirely on the fact of Eissa's mother's actions -- decades before he was born, in a country he left over a decade ago to build an academic career in the United States. And this is not an isolated case: reporting has documented a broader effort by this administration against relatives of other Iranian officials, including relatives of Qassem Soleimani, and an immigration lawyer who has campaigned for years for such deportations has said he was contacted by DHS in January seeking names. I want to be careful about what that proves and what it doesn't. It proves the administration is willing to apply this provision to people based on family relationship alone, and that this family is not the only one. It does not prove that officials deliberately selected this case to manufacture a favorable precedent -- I have no internal memo saying that, and I'm not going to pretend I do, although you're welcome to infer. But intent isn't actually the load-bearing question here. However this case was chosen, if the government wins it on a theory where the only "foreign policy consequence" is a family tree, the precedent doesn't stay contained to one family. Matter of M-K- shows this Board is willing to publish decisions like this as binding law. A published win here would mean any immigration court in the country could treat kinship to a disfavored foreign official as sufficient grounds to strip a green card holder of their status -- no actual action, mistake, or conduct required. The trap built into the detention itself Here's a question worth asking before we go further: how can someone be detained at all before a final order of removal exists? The answer, unfortunately, is that the law allows it. Under 8 U.S.C. § 1226(a), immigration authorities may arrest and detain someone "pending a decision on whether the alien is to be removed." Astonishingly, detention doesn't wait for a verdict. It's part of how the case is litigated. But there's a second, even uglier layer specific to this provision. Under 8 C.F.R. § 1003.19, immigration judges are barred from redetermining custody conditions -- the ordinary bond hearing -- for anyone classified under section 237(a)(4), the national security (NS) provision. A detainee can still argue they don't belong in that category, and DHS itself retains the power to release someone, but the normal path to a bond hearing before a judge is closed the moment this label attaches. The accusation doesn't just provide a theory for removal based on a single official's accusation. It helps build the cage the family has to argue their way out of, and makes sure they can't just be let go while their case is pending. That's why this family's lawyers are in federal court on a habeas petition rather than simply asking an immigration judge for bond -- the ordinary door was locked by the same charge they're contesting. And which they had no notice of, and no opportunity to contest prior to their abduction. Filings in the consolidated case have continued through this month, with a bond motion and responses from the government still being litigated as of mid-August, last week. The voluntary departure order is the hinge of the whole story Now return to where we started, because this is where the legal architecture gets genuinely strange. Current regulation -- 8 C.F.R. § 1240.26 -- says an immigration judge cannot grant voluntary departure to someone who is deportable under section 237(a)(4). Not "shouldn't." Cannot. It's a categorical bar. And yet an immigration judge apparently granted Eissa Hashemi voluntary departure. Those two facts should not be able to coexist -- unless something happened to the government's foreign-policy charge in front of that judge, that made it irrelevant -- that made the national security charge fail to stick. To be eligible for the pre-case-completion form of voluntary departure, a person still has to concede removability on some ground and give up their own right to appeal. So the most legally coherent reading of what we can see from the outside is this: the government 's underlying theory that Eissa is deportable for being his mother 's sondid not survive in front of the immigration judge, even if the person was willing to give up the fight and leave the country. I want to be precise about what this is: an inference, drawn from the fact that the regulation makes the two outcomes incompatible on their face. This is not a confirmed reading of an order none of us have seen. But if it's right, the picture snaps into focus. Eissa is willing to leave. A judge has said he may. And the government is spending its resources not on removing him from the country, but on overturning the judge 's refusal to brand him deportable on the ground that ties this to his mother. Departure and removal are not the same thing, and that's the point It would be easy to hear "he can leave voluntarily" and assume it settles the matter. It doesn't, legally. Voluntary departure and a formal removal order carry different consequences on a person's immigration history -- the regulations themselves require an alternate order of removal to sit behind every voluntary departure grant precisely because the two are treated as legally distinct outcomes. So ask again: what does the government actually want? If the goal were simply "this family should not be in the United States," an order letting Eissa leave accomplishes that, today, on his own dime. Fighting it doesn't advance that goal -- it actively delays it. The government's behavior only makes sense if there's a second objective : not just his departure, but a formal legal finding that he is deportable because of who his mother is. Voluntary departure denies the government that finding. A sustained removal order provides it. I can't hand you a memo that says this in so many words. What I can hand you is a government that had the option to simply let a willing, green-card-holding professor leave the country months ago, and chose litigation and keeping him behind bars, instead. This is happening while the US is waging war on Iran Wartime governments have always tried to blur the line between an enemy state, supporters of that state, nationals of that state, and -- the newest and most dangerous slide -- the family members of people connected to that state's government. The Constitution -- and the law -- exists to hold that line. A family relationship is not a choice, an act, or an allegiance. The most basic principle we have -- older than the Republic -- is that people answer for what they do, not for their blood. One of this family's own attorneys put it plainly to a Texas reporter: it is shameful for the government to hold children accountable for the acts of their parents and grandparents. Their son is sixteen. He has lived in California, and only in California, since before kindergarten. He speaks only English. He has been detained, apart from his father, for months, for something that happened forty-seven years before he was born. What comes next? If this precedent holds, where else does the logic land? Should the children of war criminals be imprisoned for their parents' crimes? Should the relatives of foreign officials in regimes currently committing genocide, be abducted from their homes and imprisoned without charge in terrible conditions indefinitely? Who defines which acts committed by parents, grandparents, or distant relatives, should suddenly be visited upon normal people living normal, peaceful, constructive lives today? Where does it end? The feedback loop, laid out plainly It's worth seeing the whole machine at once: The Secretary of State determines, based on opaque and arbitrary reasoning, that a peaceful, law-abiding family 's presence in the US creates a "foreign-policy consequence." -> DHS charges them as deportable under section 237(a)(4). -> ICE arrests them with no warning before any final order of removal exists. -> Their classification blocks the normal path to a bond hearing and release while their case is pending. -> Binding BIA precedent says the Secretary's letter alone can be sufficient proof, with no further evidence required. -> The family must fight the charge from inside detention. -> An immigration judge grants one of them permission to leave anyway. -> The government appeals that grant, preventing their departure. -> The appeal keeps the order from taking effect. -> He stays detained. So does his family. No single link in that chain has to say " indefinite political detention" out loud for the chain, taken together, to produce something that looks exactly like it. A second, quieter due-process problem One more thread worth pulling. The State Department has publicly described this as "terminating" the family's green cards, as though that were something the Secretary could simply announce. But the federal regulation defining lawful permanent residence says status terminates upon entry of a final administrative order of removal -- not upon a press release, and not upon a determination letter. Until we see whatever instrument the government claims actually accomplished that termination, the administration's public language is running well ahead of what the regulation on its face appears to allow. That's a separate, quieter due-process question sitting underneath the louder one, and it deserves its own scrutiny. What the government's strongest defense looks like -- and why it still doesn't answer the question It's worth taking the other side seriously, because this argument is harder to dismiss than it looks. Congress did deliberately give the Secretary of State unusual latitude in this specific area, on the theory that foreign-policy judgments sometimes turn on relationships and networks that don't fit neatly into a criminal charge. Masoumeh Ebtekar was not an anonymous grandmother -- she was a public figure in a hostage crisis, and later a senior official in a government the United States has now decided to treat as hostile. Grant all of it. It still leaves the load-bearing questions unanswered: What, specifically, did Eissa Hashemi do? What did Maryam Tahmasebi do? What did their son do? If the danger is what their continued presence might mean to a foreign government, why does an order letting one of them leave immediately fail to eliminate that danger? Why is detention -- rather than, say, passport surrender and reporting requirements -- necessary while the government litigates a theory it hasn't yet proven? And if family relationship alone is enough here, what is the limiting principle? How far does the bloodline have to run before it stops counting as evidence? Spouses. Children. Grandchildren, apparently. Where, exactly, does it end? The government's strongest case still can't answer that last question. That's the tell. What should be demanded, publicly, right now A few documents and a few answers would resolve most of what's still inference here: 1. Release Eissa Hashemi 's voluntary departure order. What, specifically, happened to the foreign-policy charge in front of that judge? 2. Release DHS 's appeal of that order. What is the government actually asking the Board to reverse? 3. Release the Secretary 's foreign-policy determination for each family member. Is there any individualized basis at all, or is it the same letter with three names attached? 4. Identify the instrument that supposedly terminated their green cards , and reconcile it with the regulation's final-order requirement. 5. Explain, specifically, why detention is necessary when the family has offered to leave, funded, immediately. 6. Explain the sixteen-year-old 's detention separately, in terms that don't reduce to his grandmother. The standard regulations for detention of children impose a maximum of 20 days. It's been over four months. 7. State the limiting principle. How distant can the relationship be and still count? Let's get that answer in writing. 8. Disclose how many people have been investigated or detained under this provision since January 2025 , and on what stated basis in each case. These aren't rhetorical questions. They're the specific things that would decisively answer what the legal end-game is here. We can't properly fight a problem we've only partially identified. What the government actually wants Return to where this started. A man offered to leave. A judge said he could. The government that arrested him in the first place is now the party fighting to keep that from happening. There may be a narrower explanation sitting inside a document none of us have seen yet. If so, it should be made public, because the family, the public, and frankly the government's own credibility would all benefit from it. But on everything visible right now, the government's own behavior is doing the talking, and what it's saying is uncomfortable: physical departure was never going to be enough. Something more was being sought. And the only "something more" available on this record is a formal legal finding that a green card holder's presence in America can be treated as dangerous -- not because of anything he did, but because of who he was born to. The US is functionally at war with Iran right now. Laws written for extraordinary, individualized foreign-policy cases do not stay abstract once they start being applied to professors and their sixteen-year-old sons because of their relatives' politics. The question in front of us is no longer only whether this one family gets to go home, or to Turkiye, or anywhere else they choose. It's whether the United States is building a legal pathway where ancestry itself can be entered into evidence against you. Confirms ICE can detain someone "pending a decision on whether the alien is to be removed" -- detention doesn't wait for a final order. 8 C.F.R. § 1240.26 -- voluntary departure eligibility. The regulation that makes Eissa's voluntary departure order legally strange: someone deportable under § 237(a)(4) is categorically barred from receiving it. 8 C.F.R. § 1003.19 -- the bond-hearing bar. Blocks immigration judges from redetermining custody conditions for anyone classified under § 237(a)(4) -- the provision that forced the family into federal habeas court instead of an ordinary bond hearing. The case law Matter of Ruiz-Massieu, 22 I &N Dec. 833 (BIA 1999). The 1999 precedent holding that a facially reasonable Secretary of State letter is itself sufficient evidence of foreign-policy deportability, and that the government isn't required to let someone leave voluntarily before deportation proceedings begin. Matter of M-K-, 29 I &N Dec. 556 (BIA 2026) -- official decision text. The Mahmoud Khalil decision itself. Decided April 9, 2026. ARLnow, "Board of Immigration Appeals swats away Mahmoud Khalil's appeal," Apr. 16, 2026.** Explains the gap between the two M-K- dates: decided April 9, publicly released and designated binding BIA precedent April 16 -- the distinction the essay draws on directly. Build community power with us on August 19 | | | Peter, Gerson Turcios was mowing lawns in his hometown of Rhinebeck, New York, when immigration officers took him off the street. But his neighbors didn't wait for someone else to act. Friends, classmates, and people across Rhinebeck came together almost immediately, raising funds, packing courtrooms, and refusing to let Gerson be forgotten. Gerson had fled violence in Honduras at 17 to build a new life in the US. clean_body: Build community power with us on August 19 | | | Peter, Gerson Turcios was mowing lawns in his hometown of Rhinebeck, New York, when immigration officers took him off the street. But his neighbors didn't wait for someone else to act. Friends, classmates, and people across Rhinebeck came together almost immediately, raising funds, packing courtrooms, and refusing to let Gerson be forgotten. Gerson had fled violence in Honduras at 17 to build a new life in the US. Six years later, that life, the one he built mowing lawns and becoming part of his town, was the same life his neighbors fought to protect. He's still fighting for his freedom today. This is what it looks like to build power with your community.** is a virtual block party where we'll introduce UWD's new membership model, walk through the teams you can join, and hear directly from organizers building community in their own towns, just like Rhinebeck did for Gerson. When Rhineback showed up for Gerson, people found their own way in – packing courtooms, raising funds, spreading the word. Our membership model works the same. You can choose the team that feels most like home: 💬 Text Team: Send the messages that turn petitions and cals into action 🪧 Event Leads: Run the rallies and actions 🗣️Outreach Team: Grow our base, person by person 🏫 School/Community Chapter Team: (Northeast, Midwest, Southwest): Build Power Locally 📱 Storytelling Team: Make sure stories like Gerson’s get told Take the call from your favorite outdoor spot, or use one of our fun summer backgrounds if you're staying inside. 💻 ✨ —Nico and the UWD team | Follow us on: | | | | |

body:
This is the final push. We need you! | | | | [ ](https://us.list-manage.com/iXK7t2UOLJk?e=6679001ba0&c2id=4b8979688b40abb82eda840804c92b8e)

| | | Fellow Alaskans,

**Tomorrow is Primary Election Day, and I'm asking for your vote.**

When you sent me to Washington, I made a promise: Alaska First. Together, we've delivered. In my first term, we passed more bills into law than any freshman member of Congress in recorded history.
* **No tax on tips** — letting workers keep every dollar they earn
* **No tax on overtime** — rewarding hard work, not punishing it
* **The largest tax cut for seniors in history**
* **Tax relief for hardworking Alaska families**
* **Permanent small business tax relief** — certainty for the businesses that power our economy
* **More acres opened for resource development in Alaska than at any time in history**
* **A historic share of new energy lease royalties for Alaskans**
* **Returning federal lands to Alaskan control**
* **Resources for roads, ports, and rail**
* Largest **Coast Guard investment** in history
* Protecting our **Second Amendment** Rights
* And much, much more...

**But make no mistake: all of it is on the ballot tomorrow.** We must continue the fight to ensure Alaska remains unlocked and socialism never wins.

And here's the truth about our primary system: every single vote tomorrow shapes the outcome in November. A strong showing sends a message. **It tells the country that Alaska is open and will stay that way. **

So if you haven't voted yet, vote early today or head to the polls tomorrow. Bring your family. Bring your neighbors. Every ballot cast helps keep our Alaska First agenda moving forward, and sends the socialist candidates and their dark money packing back to the Lower 48.

**I'm honored to fight for you. **

For Alaska,

Nick Begich

_P.S. Polls are open tomorrow, Tuesday, August 18th, from 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. Find your polling place and make a plan to vote — Alaska is counting on you._

The ink was barely dry on last night's primary results when the attacks started.

Cook Political Report downgraded our Senate race from "Likely Republican" to "Lean Republican." That is not a clerical change. **[That is the left wing media signaling to every left-wing donor in America that they believe that Texas is in play.](https://links.iterable.com/s/c/_4IvFCAvJVHmOR8i2wWC4KE9IPhMN4Z39NHo2FXUq1FTTQrfwL4AVcMKIt4OfgGRK5NOK2an2mD_Jl4deb01iVwonmRqKpLZtNJzLNKdp7KbvNWV-jmSTrEn_ZhgyNYxBTaqYxDqYVPIuRVidntMyljCP2RfHz3O0Kr0c26yE7jnDZMIaVVdD-RrncwOhOtfSDhZnAGqwKGxnUQETldEpyUXBXKL2T2nSQgWeqyRuARjZX1zdKhQ0ErBaNFyKima1onIvTpFubm2mEbX85tPqrL3HwmnBrFtH8zhUpn5im2UP0BvMKU8EeF95kGhMK05ou291wvFLPPm2vJG90QygdVSEnglKdQR6fy2WS4d5BPUjUJ2HZR54DEulKrUlSUEXeZqyHq-GhhLYqCg1V5q2mDfkxaoR4r1c_huyOUPHS1ObWFYInCrjjJ_h7TodgqYnlMNQ_pqtEDy_bpYIAoOu2Z1rSNjNVdIbqwBtUEoJCLKlhs0h1AFsq4_KbbSoIr380wcwzewaryyyE6Fm2hgh_eF0WGxUcNGvL-eAQFiOTiCEkH5W576wiEF3dgjWsV2QFjBuQBCZaf8GI_fFAn4TQq8qCNs3ZZlkgruYMvsYV8Tbraw1uoBywwaoH5oIkjyCYMSzJSAmSzt6cM20bsmlxN0wcwEwV0DwSJlD-m6qUX1t901a8fhoSYWzFN7EOv4SAZ8sNyGcfkpVgWtyrI0ykV-q3t7wDlfnYpXWth02DusBB3S_a9zxjGUJbT89qKm5TbkSOet2eLzqe1HXTAwP-SWj8LJOpu-6iL51Ln1jGaNgNvldGxyTOKsee89rfDSOAy2Yi9LRz0c-uH7AY7blS2XviCrArWb28-BuSPBznTciSKWxF794uXeUBazfGxCqvaaZGc36nstwyFcTW9dM0MVqQOpK81-zeDpRpwNB6vUaaPhc8KfV-DAP7KVhaRerb3CAQ0guJxoy4-I7unq8554qCse-3EdyQMIFWIQlFOu5fCg7vt6e6DPFl-nbcOKsmcHJfS4HnxBQRxAZNOvvayAMhU4ucR2CASE-8JFejF81S0X01I8Tyu8fpkVzoA/PYNp0tml6X4EAYG4VBmKJ13RRd0nGxYk/23)**

body:
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

AUGUST 17, 2026

MONDAY NEWS DIGEST

Dear Rocky Mountain Voice family,

If there was a common thread running through the stories Coloradans
responded to most this week, it was ACCOUNTABILITY.

Accountability for public safety. Accountability from elected
officials. And accountability when government places new barriers
between citizens and their constitutional rights.

Three stories in particular took off across Rocky Mountain Voice this
week—and together, they paint a concerning picture of where Colorado
stands today.

DENVER BUCKS THE NATIONAL TREND ON HOMICIDE
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

Across much of the country, violent crime is falling.

Denver is moving in the opposite direction.

New data from the Major Cities Chiefs Association found homicides
across 66 major law enforcement jurisdictions fell 17.2% during the
first half of 2026 compared with the same period last year. In Denver,
however, homicides rose roughly 30%—one of the largest increases
among major cities nationwide.

That's a statistic that should stop every Coloradan in their tracks.
While Denver did see declines in reported rape, robbery and aggravated
assault, the increase in killings comes as cities across the country
are experiencing the opposite trend. Denver police are now
implementing a new strategy aimed at reducing homicides.

For years, Coloradans have been told not to believe their lying eyes
when it comes to crime and public safety. But when Denver is bucking a
nationwide decline in homicide, the question isn't whether there's a
problem. It's what our leaders are going to do about it.

A JUDGE ORDERS GRISWOLD TO TURN OVER TAXPAYER-FUNDED RECORDS
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

Transparency was also front and center this week after a Denver
District Court judge ordered Secretary of State Jena Griswold's office
to comply with an open-records request involving taxpayer-funded
consulting work—or potentially face contempt.

The state paid Sage River Consulting nearly $25,000 for "leadership
development" and "findings, conclusions, and recommendations." But
when former Deputy Secretary of State Suzanne Taheri requested the
resulting report, Griswold's office maintained it didn't possess the
documents and refused to ask the consultant for them.

The judge called the suggestion that records might not exist
"implausible" and ordered the office to request them from the
consultant. Former employees also told CBS Colorado that documents do
exist, alleging Griswold declined to take custody of them because they
were highly critical of her—an allegation from those former
employees, not a finding by the court.

And this isn't happening in a political vacuum: Griswold is now the
Democratic nominee for Colorado attorney general this November. When
taxpayers pay for government work, they deserve to know what they paid
for. It shouldn't require a lawsuit and a court order to get answers.

COLORADO'S NEWEST GUN LAW IS ALREADY BACK IN COURT
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

Finally, one of Colorado's newest gun laws took effect August 1—and
it's already facing another major legal challenge.

The Colorado State Shooting Association, the state's NRA affiliate, is
seeking a preliminary injunction against SB25-003, which requires
Coloradans purchasing certain semiautomatic firearms with detachable
magazines to complete a state-approved safety training course.

The group argues the law creates a maze of requirements—including
sheriff approval, in-person training, a written test requiring a 90%
score, fees, background checks and Colorado's existing three-day
waiting period—and amounts to an unconstitutional burden on the
Second Amendment. Perhaps most striking: according to the motion, at
least 21 of Colorado's 64 counties lacked an approved trainer when the
law took effect.

Supporters argue the requirements are reasonable safety regulations,
and courts elsewhere have reached differing conclusions on similar
laws. Now Colorado's courts will have their say.

Three very different stories. But the questions underneath them are
remarkably similar: _Is government delivering on its most basic
responsibilities? Is it being transparent with the people it serves?
And when it restricts a constitutional right, who is holding it
accountable?_

Those are the questions Rocky Mountain Voice will continue
asking—even when they're uncomfortable. Because Coloradans deserve
more than talking points. They deserve the truth.
__

In truth & liberty,
Team RMV

TOP STORIES OF THE WEEK

DENVER BALLOT MEASURE WOULD DROP CITIZENSHIP RULE FOR POLICE-FIRE
OVERSIGHT BOARD
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

BY SHAINA COLE, ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

This November, Denver voters will decide whether to change the city
charter with a ballot question that never mentions the word
“citizenship.” The question they’ll see asks whether the charter
should be “amended to modernize the Civil Service Commission and
Department of Safety by removing outdated language, giving City
Council the ability to add duties via code, and providing for an
extension of probation when required for medical, military, or other
approved leave.”

WEISER’S BLUEPRINT: MORE OFFICES, IN THE NAME OF STREAMLINING
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

BY SHAINA COLE, ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

Phil Weiser’s plan for Colorado runs 109 pages. It promises,
throughout the document, to make state government simpler, faster, and
less tangled in its own rules. It also proposes a new set of offices,
officers, and coordinating teams to carry it out.

__

FEDERAL VACCINE RULES JUST CHANGED. COLORADO’S SCHOOL REQUIREMENTS
DIDN’T.
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

BY RMV STAFF, ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE

When President Donald Trump signed an executive order establishing a
new federal “Gold Standard” childhood vaccine schedule this week,
it marked a major shift in federal vaccine recommendations.

CONSULTING
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

CBS COLORADO

A Denver District Court judge has given Secretary of State Jena
Griswold until Thursday to comply with an open records request, or she
could be held in contempt. The records involve consulting work, paid
for with public funds. Griswold’s office says it doesn’t have the
documents and it refuses to ask the consultant for them, claiming that
would impose an undue “burden.”

COLORADO UTILITIES SAID A REGIONAL GRID WOULD STRENGTHEN RELIABILITY.
JULY 20 TESTED IT.
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

BY SHAINA COLE, ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE

On April 1, Colorado Springs Utilities and Platte River Power
Authority, two of the utilities that initiated SPP’s western
expansion effort, joined other Colorado utilities in the Southwest
Power Pool, a regional grid operator headquartered in Little Rock,
Arkansas. Neither utility was legally required to join. Both chose to.

REQUIREMENTS
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

COLORADO POLITICS
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

The Colorado chapter of the National Rifle Association is seeking an
injunction to stop the state from enforcing a new law that took effect
earlier this month. The new law requires anyone buying or selling
certain firearms to first complete a safety training course offered
through Colorado Parks and Wildlife.

in place and require clear support from a majority of teachers._

plenty of adults, and this month Colorado kids will line up to do it
on purpose.

clean_body: [ AUGUST 17, 2026 MONDAY NEWS DIGEST Dear Rocky Mountain Voice family, If there was a common thread running through the stories Coloradans responded to most this week, it was ACCOUNTABILITY. Accountability for public safety. Accountability from elected officials. And accountability when government places new barriers between citizens and their constitutional rights. Three stories in particular took off across Rocky Mountain Voice this week—and together, they paint a concerning picture of where Colorado stands today. DENVER BUCKS THE NATIONAL TREND ON HOMICIDE [ Across much of the country, violent crime is falling. Denver is moving in the opposite direction. New data from the Major Cities Chiefs Association found homicides across 66 major law enforcement jurisdictions fell 17.2% during the first half of 2026 compared with the same period last year. In Denver, however, homicides rose roughly 30%—one of the largest increases among major cities nationwide. That's a statistic that should stop every Coloradan in their tracks. While Denver did see declines in reported rape, robbery and aggravated assault, the increase in killings comes as cities across the country are experiencing the opposite trend. Denver police are now implementing a new strategy aimed at reducing homicides. For years, Coloradans have been told not to believe their lying eyes when it comes to crime and public safety. But when Denver is bucking a nationwide decline in homicide, the question isn't whether there's a problem. It's what our leaders are going to do about it. A JUDGE ORDERS GRISWOLD TO TURN OVER TAXPAYER-FUNDED RECORDS [ Transparency was also front and center this week after a Denver District Court judge ordered Secretary of State Jena Griswold's office to comply with an open-records request involving taxpayer-funded consulting work—or potentially face contempt. The state paid Sage River Consulting nearly $25,000 for "leadership development" and "findings, conclusions, and recommendations." But when former Deputy Secretary of State Suzanne Taheri requested the resulting report, Griswold's office maintained it didn't possess the documents and refused to ask the consultant for them. The judge called the suggestion that records might not exist "implausible" and ordered the office to request them from the consultant. Former employees also told CBS Colorado that documents do exist, alleging Griswold declined to take custody of them because they were highly critical of her—an allegation from those former employees, not a finding by the court. And this isn't happening in a political vacuum: Griswold is now the Democratic nominee for Colorado attorney general this November. When taxpayers pay for government work, they deserve to know what they paid for. It shouldn't require a lawsuit and a court order to get answers. COLORADO'S NEWEST GUN LAW IS ALREADY BACK IN COURT [ Finally, one of Colorado's newest gun laws took effect August 1—and it's already facing another major legal challenge. The Colorado State Shooting Association, the state's NRA affiliate, is seeking a preliminary injunction against SB25-003, which requires Coloradans purchasing certain semiautomatic firearms with detachable magazines to complete a state-approved safety training course. The group argues the law creates a maze of requirements—including sheriff approval, in-person training, a written test requiring a 90% score, fees, background checks and Colorado's existing three-day waiting period—and amounts to an unconstitutional burden on the Second Amendment. Perhaps most striking: according to the motion, at least 21 of Colorado's 64 counties lacked an approved trainer when the law took effect. Supporters argue the requirements are reasonable safety regulations, and courts elsewhere have reached differing conclusions on similar laws. Now Colorado's courts will have their say. Three very different stories. But the questions underneath them are remarkably similar: Is government delivering on its most basic responsibilities? Is it being transparent with the people it serves? And when it restricts a constitutional right, who is holding it accountable? Those are the questions Rocky Mountain Voice will continue asking—even when they're uncomfortable. Because Coloradans deserve more than talking points. They deserve the truth. In truth & liberty, Team RMV TOP STORIES OF THE WEEK DENVER BALLOT MEASURE WOULD DROP CITIZENSHIP RULE FOR POLICE-FIRE OVERSIGHT BOARD [ [ BY SHAINA COLE, ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE [ This November, Denver voters will decide whether to change the city charter with a ballot question that never mentions the word “citizenship.” The question they’ll see asks whether the charter should be “amended to modernize the Civil Service Commission and Department of Safety by removing outdated language, giving City Council the ability to add duties via code, and providing for an extension of probation when required for medical, military, or other approved leave.” WEISER’S BLUEPRINT: MORE OFFICES, IN THE NAME OF STREAMLINING [ [ BY SHAINA COLE, ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE [ Phil Weiser’s plan for Colorado runs 109 pages. It promises, throughout the document, to make state government simpler, faster, and less tangled in its own rules. It also proposes a new set of offices, officers, and coordinating teams to carry it out. FEDERAL VACCINE RULES JUST CHANGED. COLORADO’S SCHOOL REQUIREMENTS DIDN’T. [ [ BY RMV STAFF, ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE [ When President Donald Trump signed an executive order establishing a new federal “Gold Standard” childhood vaccine schedule this week, it marked a major shift in federal vaccine recommendations. STATE JUDGE ORDERS GRISWOLD TO TURN OVER RECORDS TIED TO TAXPAYER-FUNDED CONSULTING [ [ CBS COLORADO [ A Denver District Court judge has given Secretary of State Jena Griswold until Thursday to comply with an open records request, or she could be held in contempt. The records involve consulting work, paid for with public funds. Griswold’s office says it doesn’t have the documents and it refuses to ask the consultant for them, claiming that would impose an undue “burden.” COLORADO UTILITIES SAID A REGIONAL GRID WOULD STRENGTHEN RELIABILITY. JULY 20 TESTED IT. [ [ BY SHAINA COLE, ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE [ On April 1, Colorado Springs Utilities and Platte River Power Authority, two of the utilities that initiated SPP’s western expansion effort, joined other Colorado utilities in the Southwest Power Pool, a regional grid operator headquartered in Little Rock, Arkansas. Neither utility was legally required to join. Both chose to. FEDERAL COURT ASKED TO BLOCK COLORADO’S NEW SEMIAUTOMATIC FIREARM REQUIREMENTS [ [ COLORADO POLITICS [ The Colorado chapter of the National Rifle Association is seeking an injunction to stop the state from enforcing a new law that took effect earlier this month. The new law requires anyone buying or selling certain firearms to first complete a safety training course offered through Colorado Parks and Wildlife. READ MORE STATE NEWS [ LOCAL DENVER HOMICIDES SPIKE, RANKING AMONG THE HIGHEST IN MAJOR U.S. CITIES [ [ AXIOS DENVER [ Denver’s homicide spike during the first half of the year is among the highest in the country for major cities, according to preliminary data reviewed by Axios. COLORADO LAW ALREADY PROTECTS DOUGLAS COUNTY TEACHERS. WHY A UNION CONTRACT? [ [ BY MARTHA CARVER, ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE [ You may be aware that the Douglas County Federation (DCF), the teachers’ union, is asking the Douglas County School District to engage in Collective Bargaining. Before making a major shift in school governance, district leaders should recognize the protections already in place and require clear support from a majority of teachers. DEAR FRIENDS,

What a night we had on Saturday.

The 2nd Rhode Island First Rally at the Cranston Park Theater was packed with energy, patriotism, and real Rhode Island spirit.
Standing on that stage with Rudy Giuliani — America's Mayor — was an honor. Rudy has officially endorsed our campaign, and that
means a lot. He knows what strong leadership looks like, and he's putting his support behind putting Rhode Island first.

We also received a powerful endorsement from Cranston Mayor Ken Hopkins. Having the support of a mayor who actually delivers for
his city strengthens the message that this campaign is about results, not empty talk.

The energy in that room was electric. Rhode Islanders showed up ready to fight for jobs, safer communities, lower costs, and a
future where our young people don't have to leave the state to find opportunity. This is what the Rhode Island First movement
looks like in action.

Now the real work begins. The Republican Primary is on September 9, and this is crunch time.

If you or someone you know needs a ride to the polls, we are ready to help. Visit the website at vicmellor.com

clean_body: [] [] DEAR FRIENDS, What a night we had on Saturday. The 2nd Rhode Island First Rally at the Cranston Park Theater was packed with energy, patriotism, and real Rhode Island spirit. Standing on that stage with Rudy Giuliani — America's Mayor — was an honor. Rudy has officially endorsed our campaign, and that means a lot. He knows what strong leadership looks like, and he's putting his support behind putting Rhode Island first. We also received a powerful endorsement from Cranston Mayor Ken Hopkins. Having the support of a mayor who actually delivers for his city strengthens the message that this campaign is about results, not empty talk. The energy in that room was electric. Rhode Islanders showed up ready to fight for jobs, safer communities, lower costs, and a future where our young people don't have to leave the state to find opportunity. This is what the Rhode Island First movement looks like in action. Now the real work begins. The Republican Primary is on September 9, and this is crunch time. If you or someone you know needs a ride to the polls, we are ready to help. Visit the website at vicmellor.com [] or call 401-545-0127. We also need volunteers. Sign up for volunteer training on the website today. Every door knocked, every call made, and every ride given makes a difference. This race will be won by the people who show up and do the work. I am all in. I need you with me. Thank you for standing with me. Sincerely, Vic Mellor Candidate for Congress, Rhode Island's 2nd District [] [] [] [] [] [] [] Want to change how you receive these emails?

Help us reelect Katie Hobbs as Governor of Arizona.
#
Peter,

name: Courier Newsroom
subject: 25 must-follow people in pro-democracy media
body:
[ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/398?t=1064&refcode=20260817_Mark_Jacob&akid=204%2E344797%2EPpHCE8 ]COURIER Newsroom

Hey Peter, Mark Jacob here, contributor at COURIER.

It’s easy to feel overwhelmed by the state of our politics right now. But
there are still plenty of reasons to stay hopeful — especially when you
look at the journalists and commentators doing the hard work of defending
democracy and holding those in power accountable.

In this piece, I highlight 25 bright stars of pro-democracy media who are
informing, challenging, and motivating people through this moment. They’re
voices worth following, and reminders that good journalism is still making
a difference.

[ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/11000?t=1003&refcode=20260817_Mark_Jacob&akid=204%2E344797%2EPpHCE8 ]Before you read on, I hope you’ll consider supporting COURIER.
Independent journalism matters most when the stakes are this high — and
when we need people willing to keep telling the truth.

[ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/398?t=1066&refcode=20260817_Mark_Jacob&akid=204%2E344797%2EPpHCE8 ]→ Donate

--------------------------------------------------------------------------

[ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/11000?t=1004&refcode=20260817_Mark_Jacob&akid=204%2E344797%2EPpHCE8 ][IMG]

Negativity is a trap we can fall into during times like these. But we need
to stay optimistic and motivated if we’re going to defeat the criminals
who are trying to steal our country.Here’s my subjective list of 25 bright
stars of pro-democracy media, in no particular order, plus honorable
mentions at the end.

* Greg Sargent
No political commentator finds sharper news angles than Sargent, who
[ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/11001?t=1005&refcode=20260817_Mark_Jacob&akid=204%2E344797%2EPpHCE8 ]writes for The New Republic and hosts its Daily Blast podcast.
* Heather Cox Richardson
The Boston College history professor has nearly 3 million subscribers
to her [ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/11002?t=1006&refcode=20260817_Mark_Jacob&akid=204%2E344797%2EPpHCE8 ]Letters from an American newsletter. She’s earned that
attention with incisive analysis of today’s politics, often with a
historical perspective.
* Jamelle Bouie
The best political columnist, bar none, at [ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/11003?t=1007&refcode=20260817_Mark_Jacob&akid=204%2E344797%2EPpHCE8 ]the New York Times. He’s
also [ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/11004?t=1008&refcode=20260817_Mark_Jacob&akid=204%2E344797%2EPpHCE8 ]excellent on Bluesky.
* Margaret Sullivan
The former Buffalo News editor, New York Times public editor, and
Washington Post media columnist is one of the most sensible people
doing journalism criticism today. She writes the [ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/11005?t=1009&refcode=20260817_Mark_Jacob&akid=204%2E344797%2EPpHCE8 ]American Crisis
newsletter and also is [ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/11006?t=1010&refcode=20260817_Mark_Jacob&akid=204%2E344797%2EPpHCE8 ]a columnist for The Guardian. Check out
[ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/11007?t=1011&refcode=20260817_Mark_Jacob&akid=204%2E344797%2EPpHCE8 ]her most recent piece. It’s excellent.
* Allison Gill
A savvy commenter on Donald Trump’s governmental scams who gained
social media fame as [ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/11008?t=1012&refcode=20260817_Mark_Jacob&akid=204%2E344797%2EPpHCE8 ]“Mueller, She Wrote” but now goes by her
name, Gill founded the [ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/11009?t=1013&refcode=20260817_Mark_Jacob&akid=204%2E344797%2EPpHCE8 ]MSW Media podcasting network.
* Aaron Rupar
I don’t know how Rupar monitors so much video and posts it so quickly.
It’s amazing he hasn’t burned out from listening to wall-to-wall
right-wing disinformation. He and his team also write terrific essays
for his [ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/11010?t=1014&refcode=20260817_Mark_Jacob&akid=204%2E344797%2EPpHCE8 ]Public Notice newsletter.
* Judd Legum
His well-researched [ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/11011?t=1015&refcode=20260817_Mark_Jacob&akid=204%2E344797%2EPpHCE8 ]Popular Information newsletter is billed as
“news for people who give a damn.”
* Nicolle Wallace
No MS NOW host is better focused on [ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/11012?t=1016&refcode=20260817_Mark_Jacob&akid=204%2E344797%2EPpHCE8 ]the authoritarian threat to
our country.
* Jim Acosta
CNN tried to shove him into an overnight shift. He left instead. Now
he’s [ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/11013?t=1017&refcode=20260817_Mark_Jacob&akid=204%2E344797%2EPpHCE8 ]doing a podcast with straight talk about Trump’s abuses of
power.
* Marc Elias
Elias is the nation’s No. 1 fighter in court against the Republicans
assaulting our elections. His [ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/11014?t=1018&refcode=20260817_Mark_Jacob&akid=204%2E344797%2EPpHCE8 ]Democracy Docket keeps the public
focused on the battlegrounds.
* Katie Phang
The former MSNBC host is an activist journalist. [ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/11015?t=1019&refcode=20260817_Mark_Jacob&akid=204%2E344797%2EPpHCE8 ]She does videos
with the Meidas Touch Network and [ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/11016?t=1020&refcode=20260817_Mark_Jacob&akid=204%2E344797%2EPpHCE8 ]she has sued the Justice
Department over its mishandling of the Epstein files.
* Parker Molloy
I hate that Molloy is so good at her job because she often writes
about the same subject as me – journalists’ failure to confront
bigotry and fascism. Her [ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/11017?t=1021&refcode=20260817_Mark_Jacob&akid=204%2E344797%2EPpHCE8 ]Present Age newsletter is a must read.
* Marcy Wheeler
Known as “Empty Wheel” on [ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/11018?t=1022&refcode=20260817_Mark_Jacob&akid=204%2E344797%2EPpHCE8 ]social media and [ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/11019?t=1023&refcode=20260817_Mark_Jacob&akid=204%2E344797%2EPpHCE8 ]her blog, Wheeler
smartly explains developments in national security and civil
liberties.
* Angelo Carusone
He’s the president and chief executive officer of [ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/11020?t=1024&refcode=20260817_Mark_Jacob&akid=204%2E344797%2EPpHCE8 ]Media Matters
for America, which monitors extremism in right-wing media despite
[ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/11021?t=1025&refcode=20260817_Mark_Jacob&akid=204%2E344797%2EPpHCE8 ]harassment from Elon Musk and Trump’s Federal Trade Commission.
* Amy Goodman & Juan González
The hosts of the daily news hour [ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/11022?t=1026&refcode=20260817_Mark_Jacob&akid=204%2E344797%2EPpHCE8 ]“Democracy Now!” will make you
smarter. I guarantee it.
* Karen Attiah
She edited the work of Jamal Khashoggi at the Washington Post before
the Saudis murdered him. WaPo later fired her “for talking about
race,” as she put it. [ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/11023?t=1027&refcode=20260817_Mark_Jacob&akid=204%2E344797%2EPpHCE8 ]She’s not shutting up.
* Steven Beschloss
I’ve done video segments with Beschloss in the past, and I know he’s a
passionate fighter against MAGA fascism. He writes the [ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/11024?t=1028&refcode=20260817_Mark_Jacob&akid=204%2E344797%2EPpHCE8 ]America,
America newsletter and does [ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/11025?t=1029&refcode=20260817_Mark_Jacob&akid=204%2E344797%2EPpHCE8 ]“Six Questions With Steven Beschloss”
videos with Lincoln Square.
* Oliver Darcy
The former CNN reporter now runs [ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/11026?t=1030&refcode=20260817_Mark_Jacob&akid=204%2E344797%2EPpHCE8 ]the Status newsletter, which
regularly breaks news about the news industry. It’s subscription-only,
but worth it.
* Nina Burleigh
If you like a side dish of snark with your political commentary,
Burleigh’s [ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/11027?t=1031&refcode=20260817_Mark_Jacob&akid=204%2E344797%2EPpHCE8 ]American Freakshow newsletter is right for you. She has
one of the deepest and most sophisticated understandings of the
Epstein scandal.
* Radley Balko
A leading voice exposing abuses in law enforcement, Balko writes
[ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/11028?t=1032&refcode=20260817_Mark_Jacob&akid=204%2E344797%2EPpHCE8 ]The Watch newsletter and recently penned a New York Times op-ed
headlined [ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/11029?t=1033&refcode=20260817_Mark_Jacob&akid=204%2E344797%2EPpHCE8 ]“ICE Is Out of Control. Here’s What to Do About It”
(gift link).
* Catherine Rampell
MS NOW is on an upward track because of the addition of journalists
like Rampell, who [ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/11030?t=1034&refcode=20260817_Mark_Jacob&akid=204%2E344797%2EPpHCE8 ]cuts through spin and delivers facts, however
painful they may be. She’s also [ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/11031?t=1035&refcode=20260817_Mark_Jacob&akid=204%2E344797%2EPpHCE8 ]economics editor for The Bulwark.
* Stephanie Miller
Talk radio is dominated by the right, and progressive voices can
sometimes seem sincere but sleepy. [ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/11032?t=1036&refcode=20260817_Mark_Jacob&akid=204%2E344797%2EPpHCE8 ]“The Stephanie Miller Show” is
an exception. It’s freewheeling, funny, and aggressively anti-MAGA.
* Rex Huppke
Like Miller, Huppke uses humor to get his point across. I used to edit
him at the Chicago Tribune. Now he’s [ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/11033?t=1037&refcode=20260817_Mark_Jacob&akid=204%2E344797%2EPpHCE8 ]fighting the good fight at
USA Today.
* Jen Rubin
She was a conservative columnist for the Washington Post who realized
that support for the American right was incompatible with support for
decency and democracy. Rubin left WaPo and helped found [ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/11034?t=1038&refcode=20260817_Mark_Jacob&akid=204%2E344797%2EPpHCE8 ]The
Contrarian.

Some honorable mentions: [ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/11035?t=1039&refcode=20260817_Mark_Jacob&akid=204%2E344797%2EPpHCE8 ]Brian Beutler,[ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/11036?t=1040&refcode=20260817_Mark_Jacob&akid=204%2E344797%2EPpHCE8 ]Kai Ryssdal,[ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/11037?t=1041&refcode=20260817_Mark_Jacob&akid=204%2E344797%2EPpHCE8 ]Aaron
Parnas,[ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/11038?t=1042&refcode=20260817_Mark_Jacob&akid=204%2E344797%2EPpHCE8 ]Lawrence O’Donnell,[ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/11039?t=1043&refcode=20260817_Mark_Jacob&akid=204%2E344797%2EPpHCE8 ]Jay Rosen,[ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/11040?t=1044&refcode=20260817_Mark_Jacob&akid=204%2E344797%2EPpHCE8 ]Nancy Levine
Stearns,[ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/11041?t=1045&refcode=20260817_Mark_Jacob&akid=204%2E344797%2EPpHCE8 ]Jennifer Schulze,[ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/11042?t=1046&refcode=20260817_Mark_Jacob&akid=204%2E344797%2EPpHCE8 ]Dan Froomkin,[ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/11043?t=1047&refcode=20260817_Mark_Jacob&akid=204%2E344797%2EPpHCE8 ]Edwin
Eisendrath,[ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/11044?t=1048&refcode=20260817_Mark_Jacob&akid=204%2E344797%2EPpHCE8 ]Molly Jong-Fast,[ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/11045?t=1049&refcode=20260817_Mark_Jacob&akid=204%2E344797%2EPpHCE8 ]Jack Cocchiarella,[ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/11046?t=1050&refcode=20260817_Mark_Jacob&akid=204%2E344797%2EPpHCE8 ]Denny
Carter,[ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/11047?t=1051&refcode=20260817_Mark_Jacob&akid=204%2E344797%2EPpHCE8 ]Susan J. Demas,[ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/11048?t=1052&refcode=20260817_Mark_Jacob&akid=204%2E344797%2EPpHCE8 ]Kyle Tharp,[ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/11049?t=1053&refcode=20260817_Mark_Jacob&akid=204%2E344797%2EPpHCE8 ]Jamison Foser,[ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/11050?t=1054&refcode=20260817_Mark_Jacob&akid=204%2E344797%2EPpHCE8 ]Ron
Filipkowski,[ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/11051?t=1055&refcode=20260817_Mark_Jacob&akid=204%2E344797%2EPpHCE8 ]Jeff Jarvis,[ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/11052?t=1056&refcode=20260817_Mark_Jacob&akid=204%2E344797%2EPpHCE8 ]Josh Marshall,[ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/11053?t=1057&refcode=20260817_Mark_Jacob&akid=204%2E344797%2EPpHCE8 ]Ben Collins,[ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/11054?t=1058&refcode=20260817_Mark_Jacob&akid=204%2E344797%2EPpHCE8 ]John
Fugelsang,[ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/11055?t=1059&refcode=20260817_Mark_Jacob&akid=204%2E344797%2EPpHCE8 ]Tara McGowan,[ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/11056?t=1060&refcode=20260817_Mark_Jacob&akid=204%2E344797%2EPpHCE8 ]Marisa Kabas,[ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/11057?t=1061&refcode=20260817_Mark_Jacob&akid=204%2E344797%2EPpHCE8 ]Jacob Soboroff,[ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/11058?t=1062&refcode=20260817_Mark_Jacob&akid=204%2E344797%2EPpHCE8 ]Asawin
Suebsaeng, and [ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/11059?t=1063&refcode=20260817_Mark_Jacob&akid=204%2E344797%2EPpHCE8 ]Kevin M. Kruse.

body:

I was a commercial airline pilot for 14 years. I flew for SkyWest as a Captain and then Allegiant. I graduated from Utah State with an aviation degree and built my entire life around flying. I went to Washington on January 6 after being invited by friends. After President Trump's speech, I went to the Capitol. What I saw with my own eyes did not match what the news reported. In June 2021, Allegiant fired me. Without my W-2 income, I could no longer sustain the construction company my wife and I owned. It is now in bankruptcy. We have four children. I now work 6-7 days a week in construction just to survive. I'm hoping Stand in the Gap can help us raise $25,000 to stabilize our family and our company during this bankruptcy and help us recover from the financial destruction caused by the sudden end of my aviation career. | | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137410788/640685418/-201694504?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTMvMS84NzY1OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI5YThlNDg3MS03MjlhLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=JA2SiETnBLweOAMQpHDPUHoo1ToCHRCNcF-vIwBn_QA=&emci=94c2e937-7796-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&emdi=9a8e4871-729a-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&ceid=9494239)

| | High costs and a failing economy are hurting families and businesses in Northwest Washington. Now, President Trump is threatening to make matters worse with new 50% tariffs on Canadian goods that could send prices even higher next month. The President has tried and failed to grow the economy through tariffs. [**There is a better path forward, and it starts with strengthening the U.S.-Mexico-Canada trade agreement (USMCA).**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137410789/640685419/-220168985?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTMvMS84NzY1OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI5YThlNDg3MS03MjlhLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=JA2SiETnBLweOAMQpHDPUHoo1ToCHRCNcF-vIwBn_QA=&emci=94c2e937-7796-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&emdi=9a8e4871-729a-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&ceid=9494239)** ** What working families need are strong trade relationships that create good-paying jobs, lower costs, and give businesses the stability they need to grow. [READ MY OP-ED](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137410790/640685420/-220168985?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTMvMS84NzY1OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI5YThlNDg3MS03MjlhLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=JA2SiETnBLweOAMQpHDPUHoo1ToCHRCNcF-vIwBn_QA=&emci=94c2e937-7796-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&emdi=9a8e4871-729a-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&ceid=9494239) **Since 2020, USMCA has saved Washington businesses $126 million in direct tariff costs. Trade with Canada supports 2,200 jobs in Whatcom County, 1,400 in Skagit County, and 3,800 in Snohomish County.** Those are jobs that help families buy groceries, pay rent, and put gas in the car. Over the past year, I have also heard from more than 100 farmers, businesses, municipalities, ports, and others across Northwest Washington to understand how USMCA impacts our region. While there are different perspectives on trade policy, one thing is clear: Northwest Washington benefits from a strong and stable economic relationship with Canada and Mexico. clean_body: Strong trade relationships create jobs and lower costs. | | | | High costs and a failing economy are hurting families and businesses in Northwest Washington. Now, President Trump is threatening to make matters worse with new 50% tariffs on Canadian goods that could send prices even higher next month. The President has tried and failed to grow the economy through tariffs. What working families need are strong trade relationships that create good-paying jobs, lower costs, and give businesses the stability they need to grow. Since 2020, USMCA has saved Washington businesses $126 million in direct tariff costs. Trade with Canada supports 2,200 jobs in Whatcom County, 1,400 in Skagit County, and 3,800 in Snohomish County. Those are jobs that help families buy groceries, pay rent, and put gas in the car. Over the past year, I have also heard from more than 100 farmers, businesses, municipalities, ports, and others across Northwest Washington to understand how USMCA impacts our region. While there are different perspectives on trade policy, one thing is clear: Northwest Washington benefits from a strong and stable economic relationship with Canada and Mexico. Trump's tariffs and reckless rhetoric toward Canada are taking us in the opposite direction. Businesses in the communities I represent have already faced rising shipping and manufacturing costs, uncertainty, and lost business because of the President's trade policies. Families should not pay the price because the President wants to pick pointless trade fights with our neighbors. The United States now has an opportunity to enhance and renew USMCA and enforce the provisions of the agreement. The Trump administration needs to cut the BS and get to work. It is time to negotiate in good faith. Dear Friend,

WILL YOU HELP ME PUT GOD BACK IN YOUR TOWN SCHOOLS?

SPECIFICALLY, I'M ASKING YOU TO SIGN THE "SCHOOLS NEED A BIBLE
REVIVAL" PETITION AND TELL YOUR GOVERNOR THAT THE CHILDREN IN YOUR
COMMUNITY DESERVE TO HEAR THAT:
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.

* They are wonderfully made in the very image of God.
* And that God is calling them to love Him above all else.

What a country we’d be, if all of America’s children had just a
little bit of God’s Word in their lives - like you did.

Our Founding Fathers understood this.

That’s why throughout our history, the Bible has been the
cornerstone of American life, education, and law.

Abraham Lincoln believed the Bible was “the best gift God has given
to man.”

And Dwight D. Eisenhower said, “Without God there could be no
American form of government, nor an American way of life.”

But in 1963, in a wrongly decided Supreme Court case, the Left ripped
the everyday reading of the Bible out of public schools.

And the results speak for themselves: more violence, divorce,
abortion, drug addiction, depression, and the breakdown of the family.

Justice Stewart Potter was the lone dissenter in the Supreme Court
decision that outlawed the mandatory reading of the Bible in schools.

He wrote that the ruling didn’t ‘protect religious freedom’ but
rather ‘established a religion of secularism.’

And how right he was!

But even Justice Potter wouldn’t have predicted how far the
‘religion of secularism’ has taken us from Biblical values.

YOUR SIGNED “SCHOOLS NEED A BIBLE REVIVAL” PETITION IS SO
IMPORTANT BECAUSE INSTEAD OF THE TEN COMMANDMENTS, THE BEATITUDES, AND
THE GOLDEN RULE BEING PRESENTED IN SCHOOLS...
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.

...today radical “educators” teach our children and grandchildren
that:

* God is a myth for the weak and if their families believe in Him,
they’re probably uneducated, hateful, and racist.
* If these “educators” do acknowledge God, they say He makes
mistakes and some boys are really girls and some girls are really
boys.
* And they wrongly tell children, ‘God just wants you to be
happy’ so you should do whatever you want, do whatever feels good,
and anyone who tells you otherwise is an old- fashioned bigot who has
to go.

So many families are being torn apart by this madness that overturns
everything our Founders believed.

IT IS ONLY FITTING THAT DURING THE 250TH ANNIVERSARY OF OUR
INDEPENDENCE, WE PUT BIBLICAL LESSONS BACK INTO OUR PUBLIC SCHOOLS.

THAT’S WHY I’M SPEARHEADING A NATIONWIDE BIBLE REVIVAL IN PUBLIC
SCHOOLS AND ASKING YOU TO JOIN ME TODAY.
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.

Your signature on your “Schools Need a Bible Revival” petition
tells our elected officials that you want biblical lessons put back in
our public schools.

Think public schools are too far gone? Think I’m dreaming?

Consider this...

YOUR SIGNED “SCHOOLS NEED A BIBLE REVIVAL” PETITION IS GOING
STRAIGHT TO MY FRIENDS AT BRAVE FOR GOOD.
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.

WITH YOUR SUPPORT...
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.

BRAVE FOR GOOD is the powerhouse group behind my “See You at the
Library” movement featured on Fox News, that gets conservative Story
Hours into public libraries to counter the Left’s “Drag Queen
Story Hours.”

BRAVE FOR GOOD is the powerhouse group that got an historic
conservative Story Hour into the Library of Congress last year!

And BRAVE FOR GOOD is the powerhouse group that will get the Biblical
values you cherish – and that America was founded upon – back into
public schools this year!

HOW?

We’ve designed a mini-curriculum for America’s 250th Anniversary
that teaches children about the role of the Bible in our nation’s
Founding and emphasizes the Founding values that have made our country
great.

Last year I got into three public schools to reach 1,400 children with
biblical lessons.

WITH YOU AND BRAVE FOR GOOD BEHIND ME, I KNOW WE CAN EXPAND THAT
NUMBER TO 250,000 CHILDREN THIS YEAR IN HONOR OF AMERICA’S 250TH
ANNIVERSARY.

You know it won’t be easy.

The radical leftists who’ve taken over our public schools aren’t
just going to put out the welcome mat.

That’s why BRAVE FOR GOOD is getting ready for the battle by
collecting stacks of petitions.

Your signed “SCHOOLS NEED A BIBLE REVIVAL”
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.
petition tells our representatives that the Supreme Court ruling that
took the Bible out of schools only specified that the Bible could not
be mandatory reading.

The 1963 ruling 100% allows for the Bible to be taught in a historical
or cultural context!

And why wouldn’t it be?

In every corner of the world, the Bible is considered one of the
greatest books ever written. Of course children should learn about it
in your taxpayer-funded schools!

But radical educators will try to keep anything to do with the Bible
out of our schools and when they do, BRAVE FOR GOOD will be ready to
counter them with thousands of signed petitions.

BUT THAT MEANS GETTING YOUR SIGNED “SCHOOLS NEED A BIBLE REVIVAL”
PETITION BACK NOW.
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.

AND WILL YOU PLEASE ALSO CONSIDER A TAX-DEDUCTIBLE PETITION
SPONSORSHIP GIFT OF $35 OR MORE?

Every petition you send digitally must still be delivered, verified,
securely collected, and tabulated before it can be presented — AND
YOUR $35 COVERS THOSE COSTS FOR 400 MORE SIGNERS.
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.
That means your gift today puts hundreds of new voices on the record
before the deadline.

To be blunt, BRAVE FOR GOOD is a small but mighty Christian non-profit
and this Bible Revival is funded entirely as a grassroots effort from
patriots like you.

It won’t be easy going up against taxpayer-funded public schools and
their unlimited money.

But I know we can do it.

TOGETHER WITH BRAVE FOR GOOD AND PATRIOTS LIKE YOU, WE GOT
CONSERVATIVE AND PATRIOTIC VALUES BACK INTO PUBLIC LIBRARIES. NOW
WE’RE GOING TO GET BIBLICAL VALUES BACK INTO PUBLIC SCHOOLS.
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.

ONLY GOD CAN LEAD OUR NATION BACK TO HIS WORD.

BUT YOU AND I ARE CALLED TO DO OUR PART TOO.

Thank you for standing with us.

name: Peggy Flanagan
subject: I’m used to being the underdog
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Tammy Baldwin for Senate
body:
I’m no stranger to being underestimated, Peter.
It’s Peggy Flanagan, the Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate in Minnesota.
[](https://act.tammybaldwin.com/go/6050?c0=em-ms-tb-20260817-peggy.sh7eJv&amount=5&refcode=&t=1&akid=5602%2E35263%2EgN2cWV)
As a child with severe chronic asthma, I was constantly told what I wouldn’t be able to do. _And I proved them wrong._
[](https://act.tammybaldwin.com/go/6050?c0=em-ms-tb-20260817-peggy.sh7eJv&amount=5&refcode=&t=2&akid=5602%2E35263%2EgN2cWV)
When I first ran for school board in 2004, I was up against a crowded field — including two incumbents — and people told me I had no chance of winning. I became the youngest person to be elected to the Minneapolis Board of Education and won the most votes. _I proved the doubters wrong._
[](https://act.tammybaldwin.com/go/6050?c0=em-ms-tb-20260817-peggy.sh7eJv&amount=5&refcode=&t=3&akid=5602%2E35263%2EgN2cWV)
In 2015, I became only the second Native American woman in the Minnesota House when I won my special election and _proved the doubters wrong._
So now, when I hear folks say we can’t compete with the avalanche of GOP cash coming our way I know that we will do what we always do, _we’re going to prove the doubters wrong,_ again.
There will always be doubters, but I’ve always chosen not to listen. I keep my head down, get the work done, and deliver for the people of Minnesota.
**[That’s exactly what I’ll do on the Senate floor, Peter. Can you split a $10 donation between Tammy Baldwin and I now to help us make history again?](https://act.tammybaldwin.com/go/6050?c0=em-ms-tb-20260817-peggy.sh7eJv&amount=5&refcode=em20260817-5602&t=4&akid=5602%2E35263%2EgN2cWV)**
**[Donate $5 ››](https://act.tammybaldwin.com/go/6050?c0=em-ms-tb-20260817-peggy.sh7eJv&amount=5&refcode=20260817-5602&t=23&akid=5602%2E35263%2EgN2cWV)**
This campaign isn’t about me — it’s about all of us, working together to defeat extremist billionaires and make sure Minnesotans have a voice in the U.S. Senate.
That’s why I refuse to take a _cent_ of corporate PAC money. Every dollar we raise comes from people like you, giving a little bit at a time.
**[I’m used to being the underdog, and I’m not backing down from this fight — but Tammy Baldwin and I need people like you standing in my corner. A lot of folks say they’re building a different kind of campaign, but we really are and every penny counts. Please help us out with a split gift today.](https://act.tammybaldwin.com/go/6050?c0=em-ms-tb-20260817-peggy.sh7eJv&amount=5&refcode=em20260817-5602&t=24&akid=5602%2E35263%2EgN2cWV)**
💚 Peggy

Friends, I talk to a lot of people who are incredibly energized and motivated to flip the House this November and break Trump’s trifecta (maybe you’re one of them!), and with every conversation I have, I am more optimistic that we will get this done. I also talk to a lot of people who feel that energy and motivation, but don’t know exactly what to do with it all. How can we make the biggest difference? How can we actually ensure the outcomes we want? Totally fair questions, and the good news is that there IS a lot we can do. I’ve got a three-step plan for every driven Democrat who’s ready to build the big blue wave we all want: **1\. Think about every person in your life who either doesn’t usually vote or doesn’t usually vote for Democrats, try to find areas of common ground, and then make your sincere case to them about why they should vote blue this November. ** Personal conversations are so much more powerful than we often give them credit for, and I believe that there is at least one person you know who can be persuaded to vote for democracy and progress — especially if the conversation can be had with respect, empathy, and an understanding that we don’t have to agree on _everything_ in order to agree on one key vote. **2\. Get plugged into a local (or virtual) organizing group, and volunteer however you can. **
Whether that’s knocking on doors in person or making phone calls into another part of the country, there are thousands of progressive organizations wrangling volunteer opportunities that can make a big difference. Your state or county [Democratic party](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137411909/640689497/1020429087?refcode=260817em_sjj_bigbluewave&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjEvMS84OTMxMyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI2ZDllNzAzNy03NjlhLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=ksTSXC7MVc9ckG_MCKUvcWb25OnmeY0Of5cxr8AVcPw=&emci=26cdc9d0-ec97-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&emdi=6d9e7037-769a-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&ceid=14239920), [Mobilize.us](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137411911/640689499/-310503539?refcode=260817em_sjj_bigbluewave&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjEvMS84OTMxMyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI2ZDllNzAzNy03NjlhLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=ksTSXC7MVc9ckG_MCKUvcWb25OnmeY0Of5cxr8AVcPw=&emci=26cdc9d0-ec97-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&emdi=6d9e7037-769a-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&ceid=14239920), and [Indivisible](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137411913/640689501/2024546491?refcode=260817em_sjj_bigbluewave&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjEvMS84OTMxMyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI2ZDllNzAzNy03NjlhLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=ksTSXC7MVc9ckG_MCKUvcWb25OnmeY0Of5cxr8AVcPw=&emci=26cdc9d0-ec97-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&emdi=6d9e7037-769a-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&ceid=14239920) are great places to start. (A bonus of this step is that taking concrete action really does help ease election anxiety!) **3\. If you can afford it, contribute whatever amount works for you to Democratic campaigns. ** I know the text messages can be very annoying, but it’s undeniable that having the financial resources is a HUGE deal for campaigns and can be the clear difference between winning and losing. _So many_ campaigns rely on grassroots donations as their main source of funding, and your $5 (or even $1) does make a difference. They didn't kill them. | |
Peter,

**Ten of my bills survived suspense**. Now, they now go to the floor, and the Legislature has until August 31st to pass them.

They are [_in no particular order, I love them all equally_]:

✅ The No Kings Act - the first bill in the country giving people a way to hold ICE agents accountable in court when they violate your constitutional rights.
✅ The Plug and Play Solar Act - legalizing plug-in solar so renters, not just homeowners, can cut their own power bill.
✅ A bill banning law enforcement, including federal agents, from hiding their faces behind masks.
✅ Another clearing the red tape out of installing a heat pump.
✅ The science and research bond!! Because California can no longer count on Washington to fund research at all.
✅ Acupuncture coverage enshrined permanently in Medi-Cal.
✅ A bill strengthening our civil rights protections on sexual orientation.

While my time in the State Senate is nearly finished, I intend to carry every one of these fights into Congress.
