Lead Story · DefenseTRUMP ORDERS PENTAGON TO ‘SUBSTANTIALLY REDUCE’ SOUTH KOREA WAR GAMESWhat's Happening
* President Trump directed Secretary of War Pete Hegseth on Sunday to “substantially reduce” the joint military exercises the U.S. runs with South Korea.
* Trump cited his “very good relationship” with North Korea's Kim Jong Un, calling the drills **“costly”** and a signal “totally inappropriate and hostile” to Pyongyang.
* The order landed the night before Ulchi Freedom Shield, an 11-day exercise in which roughly **18,000 South Korean troops** train alongside U.S. forces; Trump said it was “too late to cancel,” so Hegseth should scale it back instead.

The Situation
* Trump said South Korean President Lee Jae Myung declined his request for Seoul to join the U.S. effort to denuclearize Iran, answering “No thanks!”
* Lee's office said the two governments have “maintained close coordination” on joint exercises and will continue to do so.
* Trump met Kim three times during his first term and posted over the weekend that “Kim Jong Un and I get along GREAT!”

The PerspectiveA president reaching for leverage rather than reflexive escalation is a feature, not a bug. Trump has long argued that wealthy allies should shoulder more of their own defense bill, and pressing Seoul to pay up is consistent with that. The honest tradeoff to watch: North Korea has kept testing missiles, so dialing back readiness drills is a bet that Pyongyang rewards goodwill rather than exploits it — and that bet, not the rhetoric, is what history will judge.[Read the full story at the Washington Examiner](https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/ss/c/u001.SfPhhFqVdCCzAqIAosiI_F0KAElx4yVoiF03sTMUTyUT70T3bUtUddhBUBTd1H3ExrbSifluHm7GYQPLph-_JhL6WceyES7FGZIX29i5ugO_R_H_sV_U5tWeRa8UWTp37DtGhrfZj9F-IwKDvdMGIIqYpq7wuH0ypVDPme9CcOzOPT6XstD3curyvjtOLqkCerJj6G4YXAtIvwh0o5W5rP7jJZ7GGXOPjKBXtPOXBnacVTxxVdpOMmg0lTiCvA5YiFtE-k8lDXM_QyQde1uc_vGDWx6y1cSQnZT0aYr-NAVwpNxfIh8AXDzN9ggSoKu_LR30NkKClfp8Z-wi0_j1l73zIZuLiLxtgAS1S4LulfVs2_OGt55WxriYSxNBVgY_10v8O4efhbXQEZD7C1cvGw/4t9/rMp5hO5MTTCrkoUwS1uuOg/h6/h001.AVeb6DOp-qxx277CKyBVMT2gEnfy9w4FtAi8ZoBExLw)

National SecurityIRAN CEASEFIRE CLOCK RUNS OUT AS TRUMP DEMANDS A ‘WHITE FLAG’What's Happening
* The **60-day U.S.–Iran ceasefire deadline expired Monday** with no deal to end Iran's nuclear program.
* In a phone interview with Fox News, Trump said Iran “should put up the white flag of surrender” and confirmed a direct backchannel between U.S. officials and Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.
* Trump set no new deadline — “I have no time schedule... I'm not in a hurry” — while insisting Iran “cannot have, in any way, shape, or form, a Nuclear Weapon.”

The Situation
* Asked about Oman's role in the talks, Trump issued a blunt warning that the U.S. would bomb the Gulf nation “if Oman gets in the way.”
* Talks remain stalled, with Tehran reportedly still demanding war reparations and an end to economic sanctions.
* The underlying memorandum dates to June; both sides have said in recent weeks the framework has effectively collapsed, making the deadline largely symbolic.

The PerspectiveRefusing to hand Tehran an artificial deadline denies the regime the leverage it craves, and holding the line at zero enrichment is the right standard after decades of the mullahs gaming softer ones. The off-the-cuff threat toward Oman, though, is the kind of freelancing that can complicate the very diplomacy a quiet backchannel is meant to enable. * Prices are still climbing faster than wages, which grew about **3.2%** over the same period.
* Economists point to a mix of Trump's tariffs and higher energy costs tied to the Iran conflict as pressures keeping inflation above the Federal Reserve's 2% target.

The Situation
* The U.S. Trade Representative has imposed tariffs of 10% to 12.5% on 60 economies, including China, Canada, the EU and Mexico.
* The Federal Reserve has held interest rates steady since the Iran conflict began and is widely expected to keep them there at its next meeting.
* The national average for regular gas sat near $4.07 a gallon, adding to household strain.

The PerspectiveA 3.4% reading is a long way from the runaway inflation of a few years ago, and cooling from 3.5% is movement in the right direction. But wages still trailing prices is the number families actually feel at the register, and it's a reminder that tariffs are a tax somebody pays. * Attorney General Todd Blanche declined on NBC's “Meet the Press” to pledge that the Justice Department would “always act independently” of the White House.
* **“No, I'm not going to pledge that. And no attorney general should ever pledge that,”** Blanche said, arguing the DOJ “is part of the executive.”
* Asked whether he would follow an unethical or illegal order, Blanche rejected the premise, said Trump had never made and would never make such a request, and pointed to his constitutional oath.

The Situation
* Blanche was confirmed **50–49** earlier this month; Republicans Susan Collins and Lisa Murkowski joined every Democrat in opposing him.
* A DOJ spokeswoman said the department's focus should “align with the policy goals of the President, who was elected by the American people.”
* Collins said Blanche has “eroded the Department's independence”; supporters counter that the attorney general has always served at the president's pleasure.

The PerspectiveBlanche is saying out loud what the Constitution already spells out: the DOJ sits inside the executive branch and answers to an elected president, not to an unaccountable notion of “independence” that too often meant a bureaucracy pursuing its own agenda. But the real test was never a talk-show pledge — it's whether prosecutions are handled evenhandedly, and that's the standard his supporters and critics alike should hold him to.[Read the full story at Fox News](https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/ss/c/u001.SfPhhFqVdCCzAqIAosiI_FZs2-LorCbFnvziquR6jlCZRsChthPK2XV4OP5r6737QBrQJKtOCgYap-GLlkvpWiYwkGnfl3mCSFkdfUFs-9j50X6WHtXm4MCPR5UvI-wm-rxSZ5bhlXFN-_DIzGr7zzMJ4tNepBwDCAOMbbkQ_rZj12Su81XYk-cYam0uKfVjHLoXx8BJy80_NHlaSjGFVSqaSflafzA-AB-6Nf-DptS20lHYma4f8iiwfQM5yfvqY7oBN6JyjL7fOIcyp3-cd2B7TfGymBSBbNc243165VpitemMQ-mslWDiIGlXWqNWSZBnEk60l3o7J_dy-fHzkCE9R0CqF2JHmwe_6PCVHWgRAUZJr0aH6xCnMeHWnrMZgaecOGK_Ve1jOXy8xLGhog/4t9/rMp5hO5MTTCrkoUwS1uuOg/h9/h001.88bPUcF9Z2ZBMjyOLRF-vQCBRBvOK7J9Qc2XIcLbW04)
| ⚡ The Bottom LineFrom the Korean peninsula to the Persian Gulf, this is a White House betting that personal leverage beats the old playbooks — pulling back drills with Seoul, staring down Tehran without a clock, and redefining what the Justice Department owes the man who runs it, all while families still feel the pinch of prices that outrun their paychecks. name: Letitia James
subject: They want to silence us:
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Demand Justice PAC
body:
This is our country, and I'll be damned if they ruin it.

This administration wants to exert its power over our great state —
bringing their routine of lawlessness, hatred, and intimidation right to
our front door.

They want to tear down everything we've built, target our most vulnerable
neighbors, and rule through fear and cruelty.

As long as I'm Attorney General of New York, I won't let them. Not now.
Not ever.

The justice system is one of the last lines of defense we have against
this administration’s cruel agenda. It stands between them and the
vulnerable people they're targeting — immigrants, communities of color,
working families, and anyone who dares to speak truth to power.

I’ve spent my entire career using the law as a sword and a shield. I've
used that sword against the NRA, predatory landlords, and the president
every time he’s abused his power. And I've used that shield to protect
tenants, immigrants, everyday New Yorkers, and anyone else who needed a
fighter in their corner.

That's exactly why the bad actors want this office in their pocket —
they're afraid of being held accountable for their corruption. They've
seen what happens when I take on the powerful, and they want me gone. They
want an Attorney General who will look the other way while they line their
pockets and trample on the rights of everyday people.

But I am not afraid of them. I never have been.

We can win this race and keep delivering justice in New York and across
the country. But we must be courageous. And we must be united.

### **NHGOP Responds to DNC Attempt to Push New Hampshire Aside**
---
| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | **FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE** August 17th, 2026
---
| | | **CONTACT** karina@nhrsc.com

---
| |

**CONCORD, N.H. —** Today, NHGOP Chairman Scott Maltzie issued the following statement after the Democratic National Committee voted to adopt a new presidential primary calendar for 2028 that places South Carolina ahead of New Hampshire:“The Democrats can vote on whatever they’d like, but New Hampshire will follow New Hampshire law, which requires our state to hold the first-in-the-nation presidential primary,” said NHGOP Chairman Scott Maltzie.“It is disgraceful that national Democrats would threaten their own candidates with sanctions and fines for participating in our primary, ultimately disenfranchising tens of thousands of New Hampshire voters. It is becoming increasingly obvious that the Democratic National Committee simply does not care about them.”“New Hampshire voters expect presidential candidates to meet them face-to-face, answer their questions, and earn their support. They should not be expected to simply accept million-dollar advertising campaigns in place of real engagement.”“The New Hampshire Republican delegation worked hard to secure our first-in-the-nation primary for 2028, and we have already begun the work of protecting it for 2032 and beyond. While Republicans are fighting to preserve New Hampshire’s historic role in the presidential nominating process, Democrats have chosen to abandon it.”“It is also disappointing that members of New Hampshire’s congressional delegation waited until after the votes were taken to speak up. Leadership means fighting before the decision is made, not objecting after the outcome is already decided.”“New Hampshire voters have long memories. They will remember who stood up for our state, and who failed to do so, when they go to the polls in November.”

# **[Gen Z is lighting their retirement accounts on fire at the sportsbook](https://substack.com/redirect/536e40cd-95fa-4426-98b5-51c124db96f9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
More than half of 18-to-29-year-olds took money they planned to invest for retirement and dumped it into sports betting last year. 26% now call gambling a deliberate long-term wealth strategy. They feel financially behind, hate traditional compounding, and think a parlays can close the gap faster than a 401(k). This is not fun money for most of them. It is their plan.
* **Winners?** DraftKings, FanDuel, prediction markets and every operator skimming the vig while Gen Z donates their future. Pure transfer of capital from the young and impulsive.
* **Losers?** Gen Z themselves. Their retirement balances, future net worth, and any shot at compounding. Same crowd already torching the American Dream elsewhere.
* **Next?** More surveys, more losses, more "I feel behind" rationalizations. Policy noise will come, but the behavioral damage is already priced into their balance sheets.

In **["Gen Z torches their American dream"](https://substack.com/redirect/97f5d9d5-50a0-41d7-808f-870e65415dec?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** I flagged their retirement funds as the biggest losers from short-term thinking and rejected compounding. Sports betting as a "strategy" is just the next chapter of the same suicide. Reality does not care about their feelings.
* * *
* * *
# **[30-year yields smash to the highest since 2007 as the bond market finally prices the debt binge](https://substack.com/redirect/536e40cd-95fa-4426-98b5-51c124db96f9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
The long bond just hit 5.29%. Highest since the financial crisis. Last week's 30-year auction cleared at 5.216% worst terms since 2001. Sticky inflation, endless Treasury supply, AI-driven corporate issuance and fading foreign demand are the accelerants. The market is done pretending deficits are free.
* **Winners?** Cash, floating-rate paper, and anyone who stayed short duration. Also the Treasury itself if it can force the market to fund the AI boom at these levels.
* **Losers?** Long-duration holders, pension funds locked into old paper, and the government's interest bill. Every basis point is real money leaving the budget.
* **Next?** More upward pressure until something breaks either fiscal restraint, slower AI debt issuance, or a hard landing that forces the Fed's hand. Fading this selloff still looks dangerous.

This is the bond market's version of a margin call on Washington's spending addiction. Rates this high rewrite every equity multiple and every private credit deal. Capital is getting expensive again. Act accordingly.

# **[Stripe just paid over $7 billion for the AI routing layer that sits above the models](https://substack.com/redirect/536e40cd-95fa-4426-98b5-51c124db96f9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Stripe is buying OpenRouter, the company that lets developers switch between hundreds of AI models based on price and performance. OpenRouter was valued at $1.3 billion three months ago. Now it is a $7 billion-plus deal. Stripe is not buying another chatbot it is buying the metering, routing and data layer that sits between every model and every customer. That is the real infrastructure play.
* **Winners?** Stripe shareholders and OpenRouter's early backers who just multiplied their money in 90 days. Also every AI customer who hates being locked into one model.
* **Losers?** Pure model companies that thought vertical integration would protect them forever. Stripe just bought the switching cost out from under them.
* **Next?** Stripe turns AI usage into billable, measurable, switchable traffic the same way it owns payments. Expect more infrastructure roll-ups at these multiples.

This is not hype capital. This is Stripe planting the flag on the AI ledger. The models will come and go. The toll booth stays. That is where the durable money lives.
* * *
* * *
# **[Synchrony is wiring store cards straight into ChatGPT so you can buy on credit without leaving the chat](https://substack.com/redirect/536e40cd-95fa-4426-98b5-51c124db96f9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Synchrony, the issuer of Amazon, Walmart and Lowe's credit cards cards, just partnered with OpenAI to let shoppers finance purchases inside ChatGPT using those private-label cards. No more redirect to a website. Real agentic checkout with real credit. Integration will take months because the brand partners have to play ball, but the direction is clear. OpenAI is turning ChatGPT into a transaction surface ahead of its own IPO.
* **Winners?** Synchrony, OpenAI, and every retailer whose card is already in the wallet. Also consumers who will spend more when friction disappears.
* **Losers?** Traditional e-commerce funnels and any payment rail that still requires a redirect. The chat becomes the storefront.
* **Next?** Revenue-share fights, more AI platforms (Claude, Gemini) demanding the same access, and a surge in impulse credit inside the conversation.

This is how agentic commerce stops being a PowerPoint and starts moving real dollars. Synchrony just bought a seat at the table. The rest of consumer finance is still watching.

| | | Eight weeks ago, this same poll had us trailing Greg Abbott by 6 points. **Today, that gap is down to 1. **
---

body:
Today we’re taking a look at the state of the race as we prepare for this year’s midterm elections.
#
Hi there,
As the midterm elections draw closer, Donald Trump continues to push Republicans in Congress to pass the SAVE Act, a bill that would make it much harder for people across the country to vote. While it appears unlikely that the SAVE Act will actually pass, his primary justification for pushing for the bill stands out as particularly dangerous: the accusation that Democrats could only win the House and Senate this November by cheating.
Let’s be clear about what that is. It’s not a serious claim—it’s a strategy. When Trump says Democrats can’t win fair and square, he’s trying to sow distrust in our elections because he’s worried about the strength building against him.
Voters are tired of Trump’s bluster, broken promises, and failure to put working people ahead of the special interests who fund Republican campaigns. And they’re ready to put a real legislative check on his agenda.
The best way to deliver that check is to help Democrats win back the House, Senate, and key governorships and state legislative majorities this November.
And that’s exactly what we’re doing at Swing Left—working to invest our collective time and dollars into the most important swing districts and states that have the potential to flip the national balance of power.
[**If you’re able, consider making a donation to the Balance of Power Fund today. This fund supports Swing Left and the Democratic nominees in critical House and Senate races across the country, helping to ensure these campaigns have the resources they need to compete—and win.**](https://act.swingleft.org/go/27?c0=sl-balance-of-power-2026.KwVigu&refcode=em20260817-2477&t=1&akid=2477%2E1562180%2EaHFU06)
One of the things Swing Left does to inform where our community can best spend our resources and time is closely tracking the political environment—what voters are saying, what the data shows, and what is happening on the ground in our target races.
So today, we want to take a look at the state of the midterm elections with less than three months until Election Day.
**Polling Numbers and Special Elections**
Since a few months after Trump took office, the majority of voters across the country have been telling pollsters that they are more likely to support the Democratic candidate for U.S. House in their district. And over the past couple of weeks, **Democrats have been polling anywhere from 2 to 11 points ahead of Republicans:**
[
](https://act.swingleft.org/go/27?c0=sl-balance-of-power-2026.KwVigu&refcode=em20260817-2477&t=2&akid=2477%2E1562180%2EaHFU06 "A table that lists several different polls for the generic congressional ballot. The polls were all taken within the last 3 weeks and all show Democrats up from anywhere between 2 to 11 points.")_Table Credit: The New York Times_
And the results we’ve seen in recent primary elections confirms this trend. Voter turnout is surging in Democratic primaries, with over 16 million votes cast in 20 states that have held a major statewide primary. That’s compared to 12.4 million votes in Republican primaries in the same states and up 40% compared to Democratic primary numbers from 2022.
**Democratic Fundraising**
But while the polling numbers and special election wins paint an optimistic picture for Democrats, candidates still need the resources to run successful campaigns and turn out the voters they need to win. And when it comes to fundraising, **Republicans currently have a real advantage at the national level:**
[](https://act.swingleft.org/go/27?c0=sl-balance-of-power-2026.KwVigu&refcode=em20260817-2477&t=3&akid=2477%2E1562180%2EaHFU06)
After the Supreme Court’s ruling this year that lifted restrictions on the extent to which those super PACs and party committees can coordinate with candidates, the Republicans’ national advantage will be stretched even further.
**How You Can Help**
To make sure Democrats remain competitive, Swing Left is directing grassroots donations to the Democratic nominees in all of our “Must-Flip” House races and “Must-Win” Senate races.
As they’re coming out of their primaries, campaigns need funds to hire more organizers, open more field offices, and communicate with more voters as they ramp up their operations for the general election.
**So if you’d like to help Democrats build on their momentum and ensure candidates have the resources they need to run winning campaigns,[consider making a donation of $25, or any amount that works for you, to the Balance of Power Fund today.](https://act.swingleft.org/go/27?c0=sl-balance-of-power-2026.KwVigu&refcode=em20260817-2477&amount=25&t=5&akid=2477%2E1562180%2EaHFU06)**
**[Donate $25 Now](https://act.swingleft.org/go/27?c0=sl-balance-of-power-2026.KwVigu&refcode=em20260817-2477&amount=25&t=7&akid=2477%2E1562180%2EaHFU06)**
Make sure to stay tuned for more updates soon, and thank you, as always, for everything you do.
— The Swing Left Team

**Since 2017, Swing Left has channeled the energy of grassroots volunteers and donors to elect Democrats, up and down the ballot, focusing on the most competitive races that can swing the national balance of power.** Right now, Swing Left is investing in grassroots organizing in key swing districts and initiatives across the country to flip the House and win the Senate and critical states in 2026. clean_body: Today we’re taking a look at the state of the race as we prepare for this year’s midterm elections. Hi there, As the midterm elections draw closer, Donald Trump continues to push Republicans in Congress to pass the SAVE Act, a bill that would make it much harder for people across the country to vote. While it appears unlikely that the SAVE Act will actually pass, his primary justification for pushing for the bill stands out as particularly dangerous: the accusation that Democrats could only win the House and Senate this November by cheating. Let’s be clear about what that is. It’s not a serious claim—it’s a strategy. When Trump says Democrats can’t win fair and square, he’s trying to sow distrust in our elections because he’s worried about the strength building against him. Voters are tired of Trump’s bluster, broken promises, and failure to put working people ahead of the special interests who fund Republican campaigns. And they’re ready to put a real legislative check on his agenda. The best way to deliver that check is to help Democrats win back the House, Senate, and key governorships and state legislative majorities this November. And that’s exactly what we’re doing at Swing Left—working to invest our collective time and dollars into the most important swing districts and states that have the potential to flip the national balance of power. One of the things Swing Left does to inform where our community can best spend our resources and time is closely tracking the political environment—what voters are saying, what the data shows, and what is happening on the ground in our target races. So today, we want to take a look at the state of the midterm elections with less than three months until Election Day. Polling Numbers and Special Elections Since a few months after Trump took office, the majority of voters across the country have been telling pollsters that they are more likely to support the Democratic candidate for U.S. House in their district. And over the past couple of weeks, Democrats have been polling anywhere from 2 to 11 points ahead of Republicans: "A table that lists several different polls for the generic congressional ballot. The polls were all taken within the last 3 weeks and all show Democrats up from anywhere between 2 to 11 points."Table Credit: The New York Times And the results we’ve seen in recent primary elections confirms this trend. Voter turnout is surging in Democratic primaries, with over 16 million votes cast in 20 states that have held a major statewide primary. That’s compared to 12.4 million votes in Republican primaries in the same states and up 40% compared to Democratic primary numbers from 2022. Democratic Fundraising But while the polling numbers and special election wins paint an optimistic picture for Democrats, candidates still need the resources to run successful campaigns and turn out the voters they need to win. And when it comes to fundraising, Republicans currently have a real advantage at the national level: After the Supreme Court’s ruling this year that lifted restrictions on the extent to which those super PACs and party committees can coordinate with candidates, the Republicans’ national advantage will be stretched even further. How You Can Help To make sure Democrats remain competitive, Swing Left is directing grassroots donations to the Democratic nominees in all of our “Must-Flip” House races and “Must-Win” Senate races. As they’re coming out of their primaries, campaigns need funds to hire more organizers, open more field offices, and communicate with more voters as they ramp up their operations for the general election. Team, Epstein survivors sat down with acting Attorney General Todd Blanche recently, hoping for real answers. Instead, they described the meeting as dismissive and evasive, an hour of deflection instead of accountability. Under Blanche's DOJ, victims' names and personal information were improperly released in case files, while questions about Epstein's associates have gone unanswered. He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

At the same time, the majors are sitting on the most cash they've ever held, thanks to today's gold prices.

So a major has exactly two options: watch its output shrink until it's out of business... or use that record cash to buy the best small miners and replace what it's losing.

That's not a choice. It's survival. Which means the buyouts don't stop — they keep coming, one after another, until the best small assets are gone.

And here's what that looks like from the outside, if you own one of those small miners before the major comes knocking:

You go to bed owning a small gold company.

Overnight, a major announces it's buying that company — at a premium.

For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18] | | | | | | Look at what's happened to these seven gold miners: MAG Silver — up 56.6% Reunion Gold — up 71.9% Calibre Mining — up 107.7% Probe Gold — up 166.7% Rupert Resources — up 177.9% Loncor Gold — up 181.8% G2 Goldfields — up 1,228.6% These weren't lucky picks or lottery tickets. Every one of them moved for the same reason — and it's a reason you can see coming. . Each of these was a small gold miner sitting on assets a major wanted. And one by one, the majors came and bought them. Now here's the part that matters: all seven were in my portfolio before the buyouts happened. Not seven picks out of hundreds. I did the training
Friend,

A few months ago, I was lying in a hospital bed with a fresh scar on my knee, staring at the ceiling, wondering how long it would take to get back on my feet.

I have spent decades pushing my body. Nearly 40 years in the National Guard. Triathlons for years. I have never been the guy who sits on the sidelines. So when the surgery finally came, it was not just physical. It was a gut check.

The doctors gave me a timeline. Physical therapy, patience, small steps before big ones.

[](http://links.justandfreegop.com/u/click?_t=8ca5ef3d31cc43bcb1fbe6968d953911&_m=3321754a8c00402ca2f3daba179981f5&_e=FhognSlQ4eiBN-GDqv6ZaInIbnx48uy-NWBHPZLEFq6LygCIMp6EGIO_UFjBqnD3GdgyfPT9c_VDcJet9PwLa4WNXOj1_kZZ14Bgb98AE4pjeEAP6ETbLtkhOeT79zn9dmVDTpEZcGKJJ-QhjWDJkXv4GFHODuh4DF2Rcz96Sj5OhL2V0aTAW7BGiQ74iva4IEekSO9fHpDpzz0469_afod6P92fDr6IY5L1RBNmC753_wvjvMfEDv8Tl-8iml8k95Vaad9t_HvL04heYMWy5ZDzPJKbYKf7rrxrbV0o7WoQ2ZOgSMW-bEQDSjcekf2-tALJiOwv85XunNNpHcf1wlP4p7RG9Jc7lp5VOUeM1bG2_5OBjOfMOW3uUX1aQfYbnWIw1GUcncxcU9ELGxtfMkUmHdq4gjNPeCDUmCaVZGaPkPt7ITpYZj5Pk4sK0wfeEjJ4QLjEiGiy6I7xlIRc3jXs2mBgXHbe1v3yhE0i5uUiTgWpbS3zYtDjzMd4RM5sEyO6hwcrALnwrRTefjvplzfwZ3xxJcswUYCdylmnk-Kv4YsRz_pKTKbRePJdFKqxtuJ5kxtyw36eZLUilmIoyyOLm8XOUG80-IJObEoPKlNm-dc8Zjwe8wNW9Y4EZHtaNCKYPzrYm-pqPvK24ZdBeyK5FUvg_OtlQdzH_rpuWjGY-6cXH-uZRBVC3djw4DlbdAR1f5jtXUzFvrrcfm3gUxBPgtt4Y6Vzw7jDBvQfXQuQYSfWAwkBpdVZQAfERkQDIGKByW1XuZOPuNZx6f8FXqtOhsz_bscjBLoCIaFJ0duwd8xn2MhL45fn5jElDcpVDIxsUSAnFfo-4WQVWcIZIxsOo2ii8UYNSZsKLKAmVeV7NflFQ8kp72d2hbmJ2gZOcAQvorJgvQKtrHjUF7YlFa6x6n1Kw7UpVg5w8BxGO9dD1nnAhRztkCu3omVAM1uDf3dhGEW-PVSFG_FItDb9J3y5lkqpPDKyfndFdP58D8Cw92kgG02oTDNRDfd0XEXVbb0FUTHpEtKgZ7U7xzME3r7H53L_21VQ5o0Er0rU6jLVYhYSzn9_wR678Fu66KSrDCO5uWo_4s57uPW8yyRiXQ%3D%3D)

Anyone who knows me knows patience is not exactly my strong suit.

[I did the work anyway, Friend.](http://links.justandfreegop.com/u/click?_t=8ca5ef3d31cc43bcb1fbe6968d953911&_m=3321754a8c00402ca2f3daba179981f5&_e=FhognSlQ4eiBN-GDqv6ZaInIbnx48uy-NWBHPZLEFq6LygCIMp6EGIO_UFjBqnD3GdgyfPT9c_VDcJet9PwLa4WNXOj1_kZZ14Bgb98AE4pjeEAP6ETbLtkhOeT79zn9dmVDTpEZcGKJJ-QhjWDJkXv4GFHODuh4DF2Rcz96Sj5OhL2V0aTAW7BGiQ74iva4IEekSO9fHpDpzz0469_afod6P92fDr6IY5L1RBNmC753_wvjvMfEDv8Tl-8iml8k95Vaad9t_HvL04heYMWy5ZDzPJKbYKf7rrxrbV0o7WoQ2ZOgSMW-bEQDSjcekf2-tALJiOwv85XunNNpHcf1wlP4p7RG9Jc7lp5VOUeM1bG2_5OBjOfMOW3uUX1aQfYbnWIw1GUcncxcU9ELGxtfMkUmHdq4gjNPeCDUmCaVZGaPkPt7ITpYZj5Pk4sK0wfeQbEJ1qnF5HMw6shEQWMYtt1lv0BOOagx8fT5oma_TAnJhAMnvC49_OmAGddB3ys2LkEsoFPI6_Q3mDLy4TDMfm6N_vcq0NqG2YsK20IFd-wZ4AxhsXOXIErlqv318qic6FAzjSmLAYyRkh0K7Cv2rsYxJNnVg3gIEQ65KwMB3xHurdEjNbY7peZMA5KWOwUkSuLs8bn-8UFln16LcppnetqffshE8QPuPCNccL1tdXbhpiDRY4wG6Szo7B3rm9TARRi0Oi4eGeMUMigOWhsXj0DRFNeOl2-Nks5mQuQYWOEpIEbMV1R6Yr9tzH-iUgjL-BCY4Ltf2wpLFkcJcAoWFFdOwmdAPKd8R-A3p5CDwK3B98oQdrlE0zvu2or-HuFytz4l3Q9y9kR4OnRABsEp25mJ3MWEjUAC_DbiBtql_RleuTlhRzCp6VRipQ9jRhwptrMWMwCXRHQzlUFIifRiC7qu4UM9PbbMgYX4iOOYUzjWIGi6O0CzqrpMlPI1b-gC_4L3aDwbNOPIKbKhWXk64zKq9_wscqr-KbauLAjJbXFNIO3E8jaws2EDpsSxzYGOdMC1KS31cixNNaaMs0Ve6ufcnbWHq4ihKXR7xRJXf3mUXki7WH2HNUwis0Fv9HOGpEjc4R_s0Mw5uIzcRRUctg%3D%3D)

A few weeks ago I was back out there, ran my first mile. Not fast. Not pretty. But moving forward, one more time, the same way I have my entire life.

clean_body: I did the training Friend, A few months ago, I was lying in a hospital bed with a fresh scar on my knee, staring at the ceiling, wondering how long it would take to get back on my feet. I have spent decades pushing my body. Nearly 40 years in the National Guard. Triathlons for years. I have never been the guy who sits on the sidelines. So when the surgery finally came, it was not just physical. It was a gut check. The doctors gave me a timeline. Physical therapy, patience, small steps before big ones. Anyone who knows me knows patience is not exactly my strong suit. Every rep. Every stretch. Every painful lap around the block before I could run it. I did not do it to prove a point to anybody else. I did it because quitting was never an option, not in uniform, not in a race, and not in this campaign. A few weeks ago I was back out there, ran my first mile. Not fast. Not pretty. But moving forward, one more time, the same way I have my entire life. That is fine. I have spent my whole life getting back up when people expected me to stay down. I did not rebuild my knee to sit on the porch. I rebuilt it to keep showing up, for my family, for the people I served with, and now for New Hampshire. If you believe in a guy who does not know how to quit, chip in today. Thank you for standing with me. Scott P. Brown Paid for by Scott Brown for New Hampshire, Inc. | | Good Afternoon,
Rob has continued fighting to make Northeastern Pennsylvania a great place to live, work, and raise a family. He is focused on lowering costs for families while standing up for the workers who keep our communities moving. Teamsters General President Sean O’Brien recently highlighted that commitment by visiting the Bazooka Ring Pop factory following the Pennsylvania Conference of Teamsters' endorsement of Rob’s campaign. Rob believes that supporting working families and creating more opportunities for good-paying jobs strengthens the entire community.
---

---](https://us.list-manage.com/zOG0padgtDo?e=131e83a3c2&c2id=e7faf2081078228733221dbd5e122ac9)
|

| |
Just this past week, Rob secured $1 million for early childhood education at the Illumination Early Learning Center at the Friedman Jewish Community Center in Kingston. Investing in our community means investing in families by giving parents greater opportunities, supporting educators, and ensuring our youngest children have the strong foundation they need to succeed.

Hey Peter,
---
It’s one thing to vote blindly down party lines, but another to celebrate when the vote removes thousands of North Carolinians from Medicaid coverage. Our current representative, Brad Knott, voted to pass the Big Beautiful Bill and celebrated with his party, saying Congress had "removed illegal aliens and able-bodied young people from programs" without once mentioning the over 40,000 people back home in District 13 who would be affected.In 30 years working in health care policy, I've worked to improve systems and help people get enrolled into coverage. I’ve seen how life-changing it can be to have access to health care services. And this I know: everyone deserves healthcare they can afford. Rising health care costs put coverage at risk. We know it costs more to see a doctor and get our medication, and we’ve seen premiums skyrocket. Both in my work and at almost every campaign event, I see how rising health care costs are affecting people. I need your help because corporate interest groups and big Pharma aren't backing me to pay my way through this campaign. I am relying on grassroots support from neighbors like you. Hey y’all
If we haven't met yet, I'm Chaz Molder, and I'm running for Congress in Tennessee's 5th Congressional District. I wanted to take a moment to introduce myself properly.
[](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/vdo66q8rYqQ1Dx6vAkvd0w~~/AAUS1hA~/C3fRarQ4WFe4Je25IDOtHvYyhJVYyG5UEZzXk3YE7lQfH_ucA64uTf-fRVs1wy-ah0p9-gwdMffG8b2H3vhrIPHQhQJdf_8G1eMgEnPRNsu4q6Vs7CXWHeYXryHh54dxq6nPNuIUkD2qTPV4KjvoEAzYYnn7W4XfbF0BAKXv5B0wG_kJkErZqbOWhvbjwj2UUrXJ7uLe9F2MVhvC4WjvVAF8rdpBXTbn8podF4RI5Xz3lFwXthzGvl4uXNTarLEmo0S8HQuW7dkwgxGxa0XlYQ~~)
I'm the two-term mayor of Columbia, Tennessee, about 45 minutes south of Nashville. I went to law school in Memphis, which is now part of the district I'm running to represent. My wife, Liz, is from Ripley in rural West Tennessee, also in the district, and she is a former public schools teacher. In fact, we both went to public schools, and our kids currently attend public schools, in fact, the very schools I attended growing up in Columbia. We are raising our kids in the same church where I was raised, we own a farm in Hickman County, and I am looking forward to the start of dove season in just a couple of weeks. (Fox News made sure everyone knows that last part).
But here's what I really want you to know. I've spent eight years as mayor proving that government can actually work for people. I helped pass eight balanced budgets. No property tax increases. I showed up for every resident who needed me, regardless of how they voted. That's not a political talking point. That's just how I think the job is supposed to work.
TN-05 deserves that same approach in Washington. And I intend to deliver it.

name: OnePA Team
subject: No blank check for Big Tech data centers
body:
A 3-year pause gives communities time to understand the real costs before corporations lock them in for decades. | |
---
Peter, **Big Tech is racing to build massive new data centers across the country to fuel the artificial intelligence boom, and corporations are counting on states to clear the way before working people have a real say in what gets built in their communities.** These facilities can consume staggering amounts of electricity and water while bringing more noise, traffic, pollution, and pressure on the electric grid. In less than 4 years, data centers are projected to consume 12% of all U.S. electricity, roughly as much as all other industries combined. Meanwhile, working families could be left paying higher utility bills while some of the richest corporations in the world collect tax breaks and other subsidies. We know what happens when corporations are allowed to write the rules. They take the profits while communities are forced to live with the consequences. Neighborhoods already carrying more than their share of pollution and disinvestment should not become sacrifice zones for Big Tech's expansion. But communities are organizing to set the terms. Pennsylvania lawmakers have introduced Senate Bill 1359 to create a 3-year statewide moratorium on new hyperscale data centers. **New York Governor Kathy Hochul has already ordered a 1-year pause on the largest data centers. Those are important steps that we need states across the country to be taking right now.** [**Tell your governor and legislators in both chambers to stand up to Big Tech and pass a 3-year statewide moratorium on new hyperscale data center development and permitting.**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm39uU1mwbYMW9amKE-asg_toD74K_fy9-sZiUkGFavlgPCt46JMm1kakwmzPAa-J2OTUj4_GwJNrSHGLvbgLyLVyodjiH7nBMqK5M6elNN3DAMr5LY5b2OpoINI4lmhLBanzd_3Z57kbOjWBT7zS4Z42oaAwaSLFIUzY6q-r822bXVq8y77-XJk6uqm9y3XPmIHv_DcvIPFoiqoz5AEJUm2-DjssshjDYT4tmfx0c46CTUazOK7kot_YCUHhjLErxd-tIeeE3byKR1sjJ0QfZZKvG5UT4MdiQbrzmJljwSjE61Y7Gl6SwLEomAvXlvErUCW720bkdJT8_WR7Y8yNZ6PMpyD4WqSue-UE3E9-ZoAya4zfppE13fHf_iaPe4x59Ng/4t9/DR62nQwUSP6IuaY0vTxHVA/h0/h001.ndvKQFVSUTkwYOwfU-F4DJevq18Q2MqUt6oEuTp2RlI) | | [SIGN & SEND](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm39uU1mwbYMW9amKE-asg_toD74K_fy9-sZiUkGFavlgPCt46JMm1kakwmzPAa-J2OTUj4_GwJNrSHGLvbgLyLVyodjiH7nBMqK5M6elNN3DAPMtR1QX7KiSKXI5YdAKwdoJFk7JAF468NrNoOBDFcHzoK5m8-NKKaEeqOLBWe0PgtWwLvL0DDkuR-J94Mt3q3ZJSl4gy9dTywFawiQLYKg2CkIYO55SGgz9PMvqRg3OEkV3Y4f9mtP9pblTYV7fPd2kMHW6kWyGWaB9M-2rBMMzQoOH-8x0Scshtb6TcsmwRmLp3pMh4m1SpCpKrh5bZLRPHsGKuoivLkODZdHD3RpN8RDAsfezVfS8AOFa4BAXIHsBzeiISHEGUAvP5of1saw/4t9/DR62nQwUSP6IuaY0vTxHVA/h1/h001._kIsddPEO-jtvmPk-JA-aOzRdFl0BoCAP0wTn_tdXuY)

**A moratorium gives communities something Big Tech does not want them to have: time. Time to understand what these projects will do to electricity rates, water supplies, public health, air quality, local budgets, and the neighborhoods where families actually live.**
In Pennsylvania, that means moving Senate Bill 1359 forward immediately. In New York, it means building on Governor Hochul's executive order by extending the pause to at least 3 years. In every other state, leaders should act now rather than waiting until corporations have already locked communities into projects that will shape energy and water use for decades.
Big Tech and data center developers have billions of dollars, lobbyists, and enormous political influence. We have organized people. When neighbors come together, speak out, and demand accountability, elected officials have to answer to the communities they represent instead of the corporations looking to extract from them.
**Our communities should decide what development looks like, who benefits from it, and what protections come first. State leaders have the power to stop the rush, study the consequences, and put working families ahead of Big Tech profits. Now they need to hear from us.**
[**Send a letter to your governor and state legislators and demand a 3-year statewide moratorium on all new hyperscale data centers.**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm39uU1mwbYMW9amKE-asg_toD74K_fy9-sZiUkGFavlgPCt46JMm1kakwmzPAa-J2OTUj4_GwJNrSHGLvbgLyLVyodjiH7nBMqK5M6elNN3DAIJbre3apZtX4qHHzBj_oOrcD1L2yAUk1_5UdENviwyHN34rksPUAFS4lI7u1PcdBlE4LKjWgfQWNMSJ_xH6BbQk8fgZ7shNj3DyY3tARFJ-14qliUFVrzjgn7Ddc4wQkpUbKCMI-CAGQi25sV-sxyQH9XDwxOWLibh9RrUDRERr1SAKyoPnlN4MHxLqUxQN5W0rBCZldyFfk_CHRZ018PYfDVztquEQWjBLn-Il_wf-dyYyEh_jPxZ9E2DaV8rmCPrMc2SAMVAcHhV6juH2Ve8/4t9/DR62nQwUSP6IuaY0vTxHVA/h2/h001.Kawbph470mtN3knxWFYTCXkTuXzyGfC4K01e86qeXo4)

clean_body: A 3-year pause gives communities time to understand the real costs before corporations lock them in for decades. | | Peter, Big Tech is racing to build massive new data centers across the country to fuel the artificial intelligence boom, and corporations are counting on states to clear the way before working people have a real say in what gets built in their communities. These facilities can consume staggering amounts of electricity and water while bringing more noise, traffic, pollution, and pressure on the electric grid. In less than 4 years, data centers are projected to consume 12% of all U.S. electricity, roughly as much as all other industries combined. Meanwhile, working families could be left paying higher utility bills while some of the richest corporations in the world collect tax breaks and other subsidies. We know what happens when corporations are allowed to write the rules. They take the profits while communities are forced to live with the consequences. Neighborhoods already carrying more than their share of pollution and disinvestment should not become sacrifice zones for Big Tech's expansion. But communities are organizing to set the terms. Pennsylvania lawmakers have introduced Senate Bill 1359 to create a 3-year statewide moratorium on new hyperscale data centers. New York Governor Kathy Hochul has already ordered a 1-year pause on the largest data centers. Those are important steps that we need states across the country to be taking right now. | | A moratorium gives communities something Big Tech does not want them to have: time. Time to understand what these projects will do to electricity rates, water supplies, public health, air quality, local budgets, and the neighborhoods where families actually live. In Pennsylvania, that means moving Senate Bill 1359 forward immediately. In New York, it means building on Governor Hochul's executive order by extending the pause to at least 3 years. In every other state, leaders should act now rather than waiting until corporations have already locked communities into projects that will shape energy and water use for decades. Big Tech and data center developers have billions of dollars, lobbyists, and enormous political influence. We have organized people. When neighbors come together, speak out, and demand accountability, elected officials have to answer to the communities they represent instead of the corporations looking to extract from them. Our communities should decide what development looks like, who benefits from it, and what protections come first. State leaders have the power to stop the rush, study the consequences, and put working families ahead of Big Tech profits. Now they need to hear from us. Let's put communities before Big Tech. -OnePA | OnePA is a 501(c)4 organization Contributions to OnePA are not tax deductible for federal income tax purposes Our mailing address is P.O. | | | Peter, it’s Sean McCann, the Democrat running against MAGA incumbent Bill Huizenga in Michigan’s 4th District.
---

I want to give you a brief update on where we are in the fight to protect New Mexico's land, water, and sacred places, [**but before I explain, can I ask you to chip in $5 or more right now to help keep New Mexico blue?**](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/15360?refcode=jtk1202-fr-nd&t=2&akid=11688%2E400544%2EYRU14n)

Here's why protecting New Mexico's sacred lands is so important to me:
**FIRST:** I learned that we all have a responsibility to care for our planet when I was a child. I grew up fishing with my dad, running through the desert of New Mexico with my cousins — and that gave me a deep appreciation for our state's natural wonders and the lives my ancestors built in the high desert.
**THEN:** I decided to run for Congress to help protect these sacred lands, which would later help me become the Secretary of the Interior, where I helped protect more land and water than any administration in U.S. history.
**BUT NOW:** All that progress is being undone by this administration. Donald Trump is moving to SLASH protections for the lands surrounding Chaco Canyon and reopen them to mining and oil and gas drilling — **putting New Mexico's public lands and sacred places on the chopping block.**
Friend: Governors are the first line of defense against the Trump agenda, especially when it comes to standing up against the brazen attacks on our environment. And as Governor, I will be a fierce defender of our home, but I can’t win this race on my own.
**_[Will you please chip in whatever you can today to help power my victory in November so I can protect New Mexico’s land, water, and future?](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/15360?refcode=jtk1202-fr-nd&t=5&akid=11688%2E400544%2EYRU14n)_**

# **3 Ways A.I. 's Boom Could Bust Your Retirement**
### **AI-driven job cuts, inflated tech stocks, and rising utility bills threaten your survival.**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/1bc6abac-4616-4f9b-89c4-a79314e7bc32?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

Experts in the tech and finance sectors both agree, AI will change the world. But here's the rarely mentioned truth.
If you are in or near retirement, the unintended consequences of the AI boom could end up costing you dearly. **[There are three key factors that present major risks if your savings are tied to retirement funds such as a 401(k), IRA, or pension.](https://substack.com/redirect/1bc6abac-4616-4f9b-89c4-a79314e7bc32?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
It starts in your 401(k). AI-linked companies now carry an estimated 36% of holdings in major indexes, leaving many 401(k)s overcommitted to this one sector. If those companies fall short of earnings projections at any point, retirement balances could fall fast.
Then there's job risk. AI-driven layoffs accounted for over 54,000 job cuts in 2025 alone. Fewer high-paying jobs can mean weaker consumer spending, softer earnings, and more pressure on the stocks and dividends inside retirement accounts.
Third, may leave you paying higher utility costs as communities upgrade infrastructure to fuel the beast. It's estimated, data centers nationwide use 400 million gallons of water per day to cool down the massive machinery that powers AI.
AI may be the future, but your life's savings should not be forced to carry every risk it creates.

Peter, this past Friday, something incredible happened.
At his rally in New York, President Trump called me up onstage and gave his full endorsement to our campaign for Congress!

I'm honored to have his support because it proves President Trump understands how important this race is.

That is exactly what I intend to be.

| | Hey Peter, I'm not gonna lie — it's easy to feel the weight of everything right now.

A reckless war with no end in sight. The most corrupt administration in our country's history. Billionaires using the White House to rig contracts and get richer while working families can't afford rent or groceries.

I see it. I feel it too.

But here's what I also see: people showing up anyway. Fighting anyway. Refusing to let this moment define what's possible.

On August 28, people from across the country will gather at the Lincoln Memorial in Washington, DC to defend voting rights, demand economic dignity, and call for a future that families can afford. | |
---
Peter, **On August 28, people from across the country will gather at the Lincoln Memorial in Washington, DC to defend voting rights, demand economic dignity, and call for a future that families can afford.** The date isn’t arbitrary. It marks the 63rd anniversary of the 1963 March on Washington, where Martin Luther King Jr. gave his _I Have A Dream_ speech. This year, we are marching again because the work started then is not yet finished. ****[**The March on Washington: Defend the Vote is a chance to show our collective power, demand a democracy that protects all of us, and make history together. Can you join us?**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.A3cd-kVlFz1CzUMSYeTvVTlJ9brtK9B32JPJ_JT5Q5PonQB1pJAEsjjWsDPHaE5G79cFTTm9BLfekhGY-m0A4SOjst18tVEE0cNRCmU-vzctESlXyaEVCzv9sRwb9gix5KflsCmM7t1AvYI7zJeJnjJATVBH3goU7f9EY7IDrncWckOFBhNDndGw_XetoLZs78Oi9TPIhf3g7K080jrIgXlpWv33j8y0HvaiFAUJAoaDd0O6PZOveuDwRt6a9zDJMUAL9tWEQsS_2FjAad_7KXtqpJAmR6OpBLyiSjsZL52pBkbi3lo86Gr9cwVZK8uYCsDclPd9TQUREZ_GSIDHKv3iJ592cOLAta980QpAN8A/4t9/q4cqjfxnR8aLjVXT10iVkg/h0/h001.HNDKV263AWuasXop2ZpLiQWOL-iO8tj1poI29frmOvw)**** We are marching for our voting rights. From the Supreme Court’s _Callais_ decision to the SAVE Act, these rights are under attack–rights that previous generations fought, bled, and died for. We are marching for economic justice and affordability, because everyone deserves livable wages, safe work, and the ability to care for themselves and their families. The March is convened by the National Action Network and the Drum Major Institute and co-chaired by Rev. Al Sharpton, Martin Luther King III, and Andrea Waters King. **It is nonpartisan, interfaith, intergenerational, and open to people from every community.** **[Now is the time to show our collective power, on the same ground that we walked in 1963. Can you join us in making history yet again as we march to defend voting rights and demand economic justice for all? Get more details and register here.](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.A3cd-kVlFz1CzUMSYeTvVTlJ9brtK9B32JPJ_JT5Q5PonQB1pJAEsjjWsDPHaE5G79cFTTm9BLfekhGY-m0A4dbnE0Y1voYWRH8lddHcRfKK3sdq8nAVYd0Yi1OizYjR4nqiBreeKhRttTMct68u9qmdbl1YPFVoppBWMfxoD2dc-TxgWicp8v9_T6hI7c_OEwD1WIyvJED8ytMLqz6mCpVpRv6uj-loLVQ2AphvjRZ_8YE608zuxghXxuEViBzoVvdd8BH_cvC2KZhFqN31QYWkKu8xT3KGJdgY5Wlc3sGphKyEJ4RIAOyix8aL-Q51_FBjNogIeTHsIHOqH2nWusdCV2hM1Se_V0L0g5IHnEI/4t9/q4cqjfxnR8aLjVXT10iVkg/h1/h001.Gx3NHYSOK8lQKwY2o8jRU5tMMeQ3st0yHlGmIZj29CA)** Hope to see you there. In Solidarity, Ken’Travius Coleman

body:
A tradition of grassroots organizing

| |
---
| | Dear David, First, let me say an enormous _thank you_ to everyone who contributed to help us send our second mailer out to 60,000 voters across the district. Thanks to your generosity, we met our goal, and our campaign is on track to **win** on September 8th! I also wanted to share a very special piece about our campaign that aired recently on Channel 9: As a historian and grassroots candidate for Congress, I know that I am walking in the footsteps of the many organizers, activists, and community leaders who came before me. One of the joys and honors of our campaign is to be able to take those steps with volunteers who walked a similar path with Representative Carol Shea-Porter when she first ran for Congress in 2006. [](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/ynCr7rUjS2HOUq_aIT7iRQ~~/AAUS1hA~/_SiyWERx4ws1P2lIpCBIrRnh1m66KHgzei13lrdtIfRL_m-jE0FLYx5m7AffjsStI-gL-ub5nVkGzykBntl8j0rlWdUTFqTCXQBMNZV98ssleKBDrwzCHwvyP1bfM1rAI2yq6OgrUak2X5O_eExqgirgPfkaVXtPRsLH272EPlxOMhNZfs1yeYsifzN_FQzbAZgsmqMPyx09WuIB9Z1mym0D5Qj1G5Ky2hDtN57z0B-RoFl_vFg7xv0OrIe5j2d_Lc8Afk7wsA7i26p5HIGXaw~~) | | [WATCH THE STORY HERE!](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/ynCr7rUjS2HOUq_aIT7iRQ~~/AAUS1hA~/_SiyWERx4ws1P2lIpCBIrRnh1m66KHgzei13lrdtIfRL_m-jE0FLYx5m7AffjsStI-gL-ub5nVkGzykBntl8j0rlWdUTFqTCXQBMNZV98ssleKBDrwzCHwvyP1bfM1rAI2yq6OgrUak2X5O_eExqgirgPfkaVXtPRsLH272EPlxOMhNZfs1yeYsifzN_FQzbAZgsmqMPyx09WuIB9Z1mym0D5Qj1G5Ky2hDtN57z0B-RoFl_vFg7xv0OrIe5j2d_Lc8Afk7wsA7i26p5HIGXaw~~)
---
Her grassroots campaign shocked New Hampshire and the nation in 2006, so I was honored when **Adam Sexton and the WMUR news team recognized the core volunteer leaders from that campaign who have assembled to help me organize a volunteer network to win this campaign in 2026!**
As I said in the interview, it is unfortunate that so many of the issues that animated the campaign in 2006 are the same ones we’re facing in this election cycle, but with this incredible grassroots team beside me, I am confident we can prevail.
**[I am honored to have their belief and support as we build this movement together! name: Kailee for Congress
subject: Peter, this is still waiting
body:
I set aside a Founding Membership for you, but it has not been accepted yet.

| | | | |
---
| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | |
Peter,
_I checked our Founding Member list this morning, and I didn’t see your name._
I know inboxes get busy, so I wanted to make sure my invitation didn’t get buried.
This race is about giving Central New York a representative who understands working families, listens to the people who live here, and knows how to deliver real results.
I’m building this campaign from the ground up, and I want you there from the beginning.
**Will you take ten seconds to accept your Founding Membership now?**
[**ACCEPT MY FOUNDING MEMBERSHIP >>**](https://us.list-manage.com/10LuDaCpXpx?e=7e42b80a6c&c2id=65ca27defa2b2ff4fbda44443b52d843)
Your acceptance means you’re ready to stand with our campaign as we fight to lower costs, back law enforcement, protect family farms, and create more opportunity right here at home.
I hope I can add your name today, Peter.
Kailee
\-------------------- FORWARDED MESSAGE --------------------
From: Kailee BullerTo: Peter, dpwillis67@gmail.com

---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/XXaWYfknVwU?e=7e42b80a6c&c2id=65ca27defa2b2ff4fbda44443b52d843)
| |
Peter, I wanted to personally thank you for joining our campaign.
I grew up in Auburn in a blue-collar family. My dad spent 41 years working as a correctional officer. My mom is a nurse who cares for Alzheimer’s patients. I worked multiple jobs to put myself through school, became the first person in my family to earn a four-year degree, and spent years paying off my student loans.
_I know what it means to work hard, do everything right, and still wonder why it keeps getting harder to get ahead._
**That is why I’m running for Congress: to lower costs, protect our communities, defend our farmers and small businesses, and make Central New York a place where our children can build their futures.**
But this campaign doesn't just belong to me. It belongs to every New Yorker who is ready to fight for something better.
_That means you, too._
Because you joined us at the very beginning, I’m inviting you to become an official FOUNDING MEMBER of Kailee Buller for Congress.
---
| [ACCEPT YOUR FOUNDING MEMBERSHIP >> ](https://us.list-manage.com/c4wNolRQyTT?e=7e42b80a6c&c2id=65ca27defa2b2ff4fbda44443b52d843)
---
| |
I want you to understand the responsibility that comes along with being a Founding Member.
These will be the people we rely on the most to share opinions and keep us in touch with every little thing that goes on in Central New York. We'll need to know who needs our help and who could use a yard sign, or a sticker, or anything like that.
We'll also be keeping you in the loop with all of the exclusive campaign-only memos and polls to keep you up-to-date on any important news the campaign receives.
_You'll be our best tool for sharing important updates with your friends and family._
Can I count on you to do that, Peter?
I hope so.
[**And I hope you accept the invitation to become an OFFICIAL Founding Member of the campaign.**](https://us.list-manage.com/15BQHHon4en?e=7e42b80a6c&c2id=65ca27defa2b2ff4fbda44443b52d843)
Once you do, keep an eye on your inbox for any exclusive news.
And Peter, heads up...
**This offer won’t last long. Our Founding Member invite is only going to our staunchest supporters, so make sure you sign up as soon as possible.**

---
| [YES: I ACCEPT! >> ](https://us.list-manage.com/7jEsuvkEpD8?e=7e42b80a6c&c2id=65ca27defa2b2ff4fbda44443b52d843)
---
| |
I’m honored to have you on this team. Let’s get to work.
Kailee BullerRepublican Candidate for Congress, NY-22
[**P.S. Founding Members will be the first supporters I turn to for feedback, campaign updates, and the biggest moments in this race. Please confirm your membership by CLICKING HERE.**](https://us.list-manage.com/5zYlPvi3Jqa?e=7e42b80a6c&c2id=65ca27defa2b2ff4fbda44443b52d843)

| | **_Meet Rob:_** Born and raised in Kingston, PA, Rob Bresnahan is currently serving his first term as PA-08’s homegrown Congressman. He’s a fifth-generation Northeastern Pennsylvanian, and the only representative in Congress who is part of the National Electrical Contractors Association. A product of the American Dream, Rob learned the true meaning of hard work by getting his hands dirty early and often. He wired junction boxes, ran heavy equipment, drove trucks, and learned the value of an honest day’s work in the process. His family instilled the values of hard work, discipline, and perseverance in him at a young age – and Rob has stayed true to these foundational values all his life. At just 19 years old, Rob joined his family’s business as the CFO for Kuharchik Construction. He became the CEO of the company in 2013. Rob spent over a decade working and connecting with blue-collar Americans across the country before running for Congress in 2024. He was outspent 2:1 in his race against a 12-year Democrat that year, but the people of Northeastern Pennsylvania demanded change when they sent Rob to be their fighter in Washington. Through his experience as an electrical contractor, Rob saw the real world struggles facing America’s blue-collar workers first hand. Wages are not keeping up with the skyrocketing cost of living, and Americans who wake up every day and pay their dues are being left out to dry by their elected officials. But Rob’s voting record in Congress tells a different story. He’s stood up for hardworking Americans at every opportunity, regardless of partisan politics. Simply put, Rob Bresnahan brings both insight and candid concern for blue-collar America to Congress that your run-of-the-mill representatives don’t. Every day that he steps foot on Capitol Hill, Rob is 100% devoted to restoring America’s energy independence, deregulating the economy, and bringing well-paying jobs back to the great commonwealth of Pennsylvania. While he’s still serving his freshman term in Congress, Rob has already introduced key legislation to re-invest in American trades and pave avenues to success for young people who forgo a traditional college education. Now running for re-election in one of the most pivotal battleground races in the country, Rob is stepping up to the plate once again to deliver for the people of PA-08 and preserve our Republican House majority for the remainder of President Trump’s second term.

name: Roy Cooper
subject: The polls keep missing
body:
This is a warning sign for us.
|
# [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1135&source=&t=1&akid=2791%2E124072%2E3djuw0)
| | | |
---
Peter, I want to talk about all the polls we’ve been seeing recently.
Last Tuesday in Wisconsin, we saw a 20+ polling miss in the Democratic primary. The polls showed one candidate with a massive lead heading into the final stretch, yet on election night, she _lost_ by 0.5%.
A week before that, we saw a 10+ point polling miss in Michigan – where the polls said one thing pretty definitively, and then the election results said something completely different.
**Here in North Carolina, Peter, we’re a much smaller potential polling miss away from losing this race – and losing the seat that experts say Democrats have to flip to take back the Senate.**
With GOP super PACs pouring nearly $100 million so far into this race to defeat me, a recent poll shows my narrow lead cut to just a handful of points, and it’s only going to get tighter. Elections in North Carolina are always close, always down to the thinnest of margins. **And the last few weeks have shown us yet again that polls can’t predict the future.**
**So today, I’m asking you to make a donation to my campaign so we have the resources to fight back against this onslaught of GOP spending, protect our lead and keep surging ahead.** No Democrat has won a U.S. Senate seat here since 2008, but with your support, we can change that. Let me tell you exactly where our race stands — because the numbers that just came in are unlike anything I've seen in this state in a long time.

**This race is now a one-point toss-up. And the momentum is entirely ours.
**
This trend line tells the story. At the start of this year, public polls showed Abbott ahead by 7–10 points. Then:

* TPOR (April 2026): Abbott +5
* TPOR (May 2026): Abbott +5
* TPOR (July 2026): Abbott +3, inside the margin of error
* Fox News (July 2026): Abbott +1, a statistical tie
* Texas A&M Bush School / Texas Pulse (August 2026): Abbott +1, a statistical tie

Two separate polls, from two independent organizations, now show a one-point race. As one Democratic strategist put it plainly to Newsweek: "Hinojosa has the momentum. This race has gone from a 10-point race to a 7-point race to a 5-point race to a 3-point race." It's now at 1.
And here's what makes this movement so significant: Gina is still introducing herself to Texas voters. In June, more than half of likely voters had no opinion of her. Today, fewer than one in three do. Her favorability has jumped from 31% to 43% in two months — entirely through earned media, social media, grassroots organizing, and Gina traveling every corner of this state. We _just_ launched our first TV ads this month.
**Abbott is underwater — and sinking.**
After 12 years as governor, Greg Abbott's job approval has flipped negative: 47% approve, 51% disapprove. More Texans disapprove of Abbott than approve of him. His favorability sits at 46% favorable, 50% unfavorable.
A three-term Republican incumbent whose own job approval has gone negative in Texas is an incumbent in serious trouble.
**The coalition Gina is building is exactly the one that wins this race.**
The July TPOR poll showed Gina leading among Latino voters by 38 points, independents by double digits, and Black voters by 49 points.
And then there's TX-15. A recent poll by House Majority PAC in that district — which Donald Trump carried 58–41 in 2024 — shows Gina leading Abbott 52–47. She is winning in Trump country. She is cutting into Abbott's base in territory Republicans have taken for granted for years.
This is not a narrow coalition. This is a new Texas majority being built in real time.
**Abbott's war chest is real — and it's built on corruption.**
Greg Abbott entered 2026 with $105.7 million on hand. His top donors include corporate executives, energy magnates, and data center developers — at a time when data centers are threatening to blow up Texas utility bills. He has handed out $1 billion in no-bid contracts to his donors. He rammed through a $1 billion school voucher scam after receiving the largest campaign contribution in Texas history from an out-of-state billionaire.
After 12 years, Texans are paying the price: the highest uninsured rate in the country, property taxes up 34% since 2019, school districts laying off staff and closing schools after Abbott held their funding hostage to pass his voucher scheme, and a power grid that failed catastrophically in 2021 and still hasn't been fully fixed.
The Greg Abbott Corruption Tax is real. Texans know it. The polls show it.
**Even Republicans are admitting this race is real.**
When a reporter asked outgoing Senator John Cornyn — who lost the Republican primary to Ken Paxton — whether Democrats have a chance in Texas this year, Cornyn said simply: "Yes." Asked again if he was sure, he said: "Yeah." That's the Republican who knows Texas best, in his own words.
**The governor’s race in Texas has national implications.**
The stakes go beyond the governor's race. Texas is growing at a rapid pace and is set to control nearly 10% of Congress by the end of the decade. With Texas Republicans committed to gerrymandering the state, they could draw maps so severe that it would be impossible for Democrats to win control of Congress for a generation. _Unless we elect a governor who will veto those rigged maps._
We are not just running for governor. We are running to reshape the entire political landscape in Texas and what happens here will impact the entire country. This race will determine who controls Congress for a generation.
**The bottom line.**
Abbott is scared. He's told his own donors he's at real risk of losing seats statewide. The polls — and now members of his own party — confirm it.
The coalition is here. The momentum is ours. Gina is closing fast in a state that hasn't elected a Democratic governor in 30 years — and she's doing it with a coalition of nearly 120,000 grassroots donors, no corporate PAC money, and a message that connects with Texans.
What determines whether we win is whether Democrats decide Texas is worth the investment. We can win this race if we all show up.

_**By Brett Di Resta & Cliff Schecter**_
**Cliff 's Note:** If you want Democrats to win the races that could blow the midterms wide open, [become a paid subscriber](https://substack.com/redirect/16e4feff-d6b1-4c15-8c9c-71b4165d032f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). We're finding the campaigns national media overlook--showing you where your attention and support can make the biggest difference!
If you're a political junkie who follows campaigns online, you could be forgiven for believing that this election cycle consists solely of a few Senate races and a bunch of DSA vs. Normie Dem primaries. You would know more about Graham Platner's knowledge of Nazi iconography and Francesca Hong's holiday preferences than, say, what's going on in the Florida Governor's race.
**But there are a ton of other races, including targeted pick-ups, that are happening out of view.**
For Democrats to have a true wave year, a bunch of wins must come from these under-the-radar campaigns. These races aren't getting the funding they need, nor the attention they deserve. We're not predicting wins in all these races (unless they win, in which case we'll take all the credit), but rather highlighting little-known races where Democrats have a huge opportunity to win, turning the coming wave into a azure tsunami.
* * *
### **ALABAMA-02**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/16e4feff-d6b1-4c15-8c9c-71b4165d032f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
With Donald Trump's popularity rivaling that of measles (or the measles vaccine for you MAHA fans), the GOP decided to gut the Voting Rights Act and try to remove as many African-American-held seats as possible. One such seat was Alabama's second district.
[Leave a comment](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=3722532&post_id=211625908&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&isFreemail=true&comments=true&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjExNjI1OTA4LCJpYXQiOjE3ODcwMTA4NDMsImV4cCI6MTc4OTYwMjg0MywiaXNzIjoicHViLTM3MjI1MzIiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.5WVbRRZB62TmDxh8PS7NNuyERcfx5RG84ML_lYJCuZQ&r=1hvr60&utm_campaign=email-half-magic-comments&action=post-comment)
Democrat Shomari Figures carried this seat by 9 points in 2024 and was heavily favored to win again before the GOP decided to ~~cheat~~ redistrict the seat. According to the Cook Political Report, the new one leans right, at R+7.
But rather than tuck tail and run, Figures is seriously competing.
He's outraised all the Republicans running for the seat, including his Trump-backed opponent, State Rep. Rhett Marques. That means he'll have solid name recognition and a financial advantage with just under three months to go til election day. He may also be the beneficiary of rising Black turnout this cycle, which could be enough to put him over the top.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/16e4feff-d6b1-4c15-8c9c-71b4165d032f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Alabama isn't the only supposedly "safe" Republican territory suddenly very much in play. Below, we break down seven more overlooked races--including two Senate contests!--that could turn a Democratic wave into a blue tsunami...

clean_body: Can we be honest with you? Our grassroots fundraising has been a little slower than we need it to be — and in a race against MAGA Governor Joe Lombardo and his mega-donors, that’s a real problem. So today, we’re lowering our ask to $1. When one person chips in $1... another follows. And another after that. Together, we can create a wave of support capable of taking on Lombardo’s mega-donors and winning. That’s the potential our grassroots team has. Now, it’s just a matter of whether we use it. MAGA mega-donors think they can simply spend their way to a Lombardo victory. It’s up to us to prove them wrong and elect Aaron, a true fighter for Nevadans. Thank you, Team Ford
